rows.summary:
This RBI communication instructs all regulated entities covered by the KYC Directions, 2025—specifically commercial banks, small finance banks, payment banks, urban co-operative banks, rural co-operative banks, regional rural banks, local area banks, NBFCs, asset reconstruction companies, and all-India financial institutions—to continue complying with Section 51A of the UAPA, 1967 by ensuring they do not maintain accounts in the names of persons or entities appearing on UNSC-approved terrorist sanctions lists. It is issued in the context of the Reserve Bank of India’s Chapter IX obligations on international-agency communications and follows a Ministry of External Affairs intimation regarding UNSC press release SC/16443 dated August 27, 2026.

The substantive change reported is an update to the UN Security Council Committee’s 1988 (2011) Taliban Sanctions List: one entry has been amended. The document says the Committee, established under UNSC Resolution 1988 (2011), has made changes shown by strikethrough and/or underline to the relevant entry on the 1988 list, which covers individuals and entities subject to an assets freeze, travel ban, and arms embargo under paragraph 1 of Security Council Resolution 2816 (2026), adopted under Chapter VII of the UN Charter.

For compliance purposes, the operational requirement is that regulated entities must review the updated UNSC list against their customer and account records and ensure no account is held in the name of any listed individual or entity. Because the notice only states that one entry was amended and refers readers to the specific list changes, compliance teams should treat this as a sanctions-screening update requiring immediate list refresh and rescreening of existing relationships and transactions against the revised Taliban Sanctions List. The document is dated September 07, 2026 and does not itself specify a separate internal deadline beyond the obligation to remain continuously compliant with the updated sanctions list.

rows.title: Deposits and Accounts – Accounts of Non-resident banks
rows.desc: RBI/2026-27/251 A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 20 September 02, 2026 To All Authorised Dealer Category-I banks Madam / Sir Deposits and Accounts – Accounts of Non-resident banks Please refer to Para B.2(ii) and B.8(i) of Part B of the A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No.92, dated April 4, 2003, in terms of which AD banks were required to: a. Furnish an up-to-date list of all its offices/branches maintaining Rupee accounts of non-resident banks, as at the end of December each year before 15th January of the following year to the Central Office of Reserve Bank, and b. Report temporary overdrawals by overseas branches/ correspondents over permissible limit, if not adjusted within five days, to the Central Office of Reserve Bank. 2. On a review, it has been decided to dispense with the above reporting requirements with immediate effect. 3. The directions contained in this circular have been issued under sections 10(4) and 11(1) of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (42 of 1999) and are without prejudice to permissions/approvals, if any, required under any other law. Yours faithfully (N. Senthil Kumar) Chief General Manager
rows.summary:
The Reserve Bank of India has removed two reporting obligations for Authorised Dealer Category-I (AD Cat-I) banks with immediate effect, as of **September 2, 2026**. Previously, under Para B.2(ii) and B.8(i) of Part B of A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 92 dated **April 4, 2003**, AD banks had to (1) send the RBI Central Office an up-to-date list of all offices/branches maintaining **rupee accounts of non-resident banks** as of **December 31** each year, by **January 15** of the following year, and (2) report **temporary overdrawals** by overseas branches/correspondents that exceeded the permissible limit if those overdrawals were not adjusted within **five days**.  

The circular states that, following a review, both of those requirements are now **dispensed with immediately**, so affected banks no longer need to make those specific annual and exception reports to the RBI under those provisions. The change applies to **all Authorised Dealer Category-I banks** and relates specifically to their handling of **non-resident bank rupee accounts** and monitoring/reporting of **overdrawals by overseas branches/correspondents**. The RBI notes that the directions are issued under **sections 10(4) and 11(1) of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999**, and that they do not affect any permissions or approvals that may still be required under other applicable laws.

rows.title: Relief Measures in Areas Affected by Natural Calamities - Reporting through Centralised Information Management System (CIMS) Portal - Introduction of Half-Yearly Return
rows.desc: RBI/2026-27/250 CO.FIDD.FSD.No.S544/05-10-001/2026-27 September 02, 2026 The Chief Executive Officer / Managing Director All Scheduled Commercial Banks (including Regional Rural Banks and Small Finance Banks) All Local Area Banks/ Urban Cooperative Banks/ Rural Cooperative Banks/ Non- Banking Financial Companies / AIFIs Madam / Dear Sir, Relief Measures in Areas Affected by Natural Calamities - Reporting through Centralised Information Management System (CIMS) Portal - Introduction of Half- Yearly Return The regulatory framework governing the relief measures to be extended by the Regulated Entities (REs) in areas affected by natural calamities has been revised vide the amendment directions on Resolution of Stressed Assets dated April 29, 2026 (list enclosed), which came into effect from July 1, 2026. 2. These directions require REs to submit data relating to relief measures extended in areas affected by natural calamities through the CIMS portal on a half-yearly basis. Accordingly, in order to align the existing reporting mechanism with the revised regulatory framework, REs shall furnish the required information in the revised reporting format through the CIMS portal. 3. The return shall be submitted within 30 days from the end of each half-year, i.e., by October 30 for the half-year ending September 30, and by April 30 for the half-year ending March 31. 4. REs shall ensure that the information submitted through the CIMS portal is accurate, complete, and duly validated. Appropriate internal systems and processes may be 2 established to facilitate timely collection, verification, consolidation, and submission of the required information. 5. Further, the existing monthly return which was applicable to all Scheduled Commercial Banks (including Small Finance Banks and excluding Regional Rural Banks) on relief measures extended in areas affected by natural calamities stands discontinued with effect from July 1, 2026. Yours sincerely, (R Giridharan) Chief General Manager
rows.summary:
The Reserve Bank of India has revised the reporting framework for relief measures extended in areas affected by natural calamities under the amended Resolution of Stressed Assets directions dated April 29, 2026, which became effective on July 1, 2026. Under the new requirement, regulated entities must now report data on such relief measures through the Centralised Information Management System (CIMS) portal in a revised format on a half-yearly basis, rather than under the prior reporting approach.

The half-yearly return must be filed within 30 days after the end of each half-year: by October 30 for the period ending September 30, and by April 30 for the period ending March 31. This applies broadly to all regulated entities covered by the circular, specifically Scheduled Commercial Banks, including Regional Rural Banks and Small Finance Banks, as well as Local Area Banks, Urban Cooperative Banks, Rural Cooperative Banks, Non-Banking Financial Companies, and All India Financial Institutions. Entities are required to ensure the submitted information is accurate, complete, and properly validated, and they should establish internal systems and processes to support timely collection, verification, consolidation, and submission of the data.

The circular also states that the existing monthly return for relief measures in natural calamity-affected areas, which applied to Scheduled Commercial Banks including Small Finance Banks but excluding Regional Rural Banks, has been discontinued effective July 1, 2026. In practical terms, compliance teams should treat the half-yearly CIMS filing as the operative reporting obligation going forward and stop the prior monthly submission for the affected bank categories from that date.

rows.title: Reserve Bank of India (Urban Co-operative Banks – Classification, Valuation, and Operation of Investment Portfolio) Second Amendment Directions, 2026
rows.desc: RBI/2026-27/249 DOR.MRG.REC.No.217/00-00-011/2026-27 September 2, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Urban Co-operative Banks – Classification, Valuation, and Operation of Investment Portfolio) Second Amendment Directions, 2026 Please refer to Chapter VIII of Reserve Bank of India (Urban Co-operative Banks - Classification, Valuation, and Operation of Investment Portfolio) Directions, 2025 dated November 28, 2025, on Investment in non-SLR securities. In view of the establishment of Indian Digital Payment Intelligence Corporation (IDPIC) as the nation's central digital payment fraud intelligence platform and to enable UCBs to acquire its membership, there is a need to amend the extant instructions. 2. Accordingly, in exercise of the powers conferred by Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 (hereinafter called the Act), read with Section 56 thereof, and all other laws enabling the Reserve Bank in this regard, the Reserve Bank, being satisfied that it is necessary and expedient in the public interest so to do, hereby, issues the Amendment Directions hereinafter specified. 3. (i) These Directions shall be called the Reserve Bank of India (Urban Co-operative Banks – Classification, Valuation and Operation of Investment Portfolio) Second Amendment Directions, 2026. (ii) These Amendment Directions shall come into effect from the date of issue. 4. The Reserve Bank of India (Urban Co-operative Banks - Classification, Valuation, and Operation of Investment Portfolio) Directions, 2025, are amended as provided below. (i) Paragraph 101.(5) shall be substituted by the following, namely:- “101.(5) Equity shares of Umbrella Organization (UO) of UCB sector and Indian Digital Payment Intelligence Corporation (IDPIC) for acquiring membership;”. (ii) Paragraph 107.(1) shall be substituted by the following, namely:- “107.(1) Equity shares of Market Infrastructure Companies (MICs), Umbrella Organization (UO) of UCB Sector, IDPIC, and CCBs / StCBs, if it becomes necessary to do so for
rows.summary:
The Reserve Bank of India’s **Urban Co-operative Banks (UCBs) – Classification, Valuation, and Operation of Investment Portfolio** directions were amended on **September 2, 2026** through the **Second Amendment Directions, 2026**, and these amendments take effect **immediately from the date of issue**. The stated purpose is to reflect the establishment of the **Indian Digital Payment Intelligence Corporation (IDPIC)** as the country’s central digital payment fraud intelligence platform and to allow UCBs to become members of IDPIC.

The key substantive change is in the treatment of eligible equity investments. **Paragraph 101(5)** of the 2025 Directions is replaced so that UCBs may invest in **equity shares of the Umbrella Organization (UO) of the UCB sector and of IDPIC, specifically for acquiring membership**. In other words, IDPIC is now expressly added as a permitted investment target in the membership context.

A related change is made to **Paragraph 107(1)**, which is also substituted to expand the list of permitted equity-share investments. The revised text includes **equity shares of Market Infrastructure Companies (MICs), the UCB sector’s Umbrella Organization (UO), IDPIC, and CCBs/StCBs where necessary for acquiring membership**. For compliance purposes, the amendment means UCBs should now treat IDPIC-related membership equity as expressly authorized under the investment portfolio framework, alongside the previously recognized entities, and apply the amended provisions as of **September 2, 2026**.

rows.desc: RBI/2026-27/248 DOR.SOG(SPE).REC.214/13.03.00/2026-27 August 25, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Rural Co-operative Banks – Interest Rate on Deposits) Second Amendment Directions, 2026 Please refer to the Reserve Bank of India (Rural Co-operative Banks – Interest Rate on Deposits) Directions, 2025 (hereinafter referred to as ‘Directions’), dated November 28, 2025 (Updated as on June 17, 2026), wherein temporary withdrawal of the interest rate ceiling on fresh FCNR(B) deposits of 3-5 year tenors and restriction on interest rates on NRE deposits of 3 year and above tenors, including the deposits that are renewed upon maturity, have been provided with effect from June 17, 2026, for the period until September 30, 2026. On a review, it has been decided to amend the date ‘September 30, 2026’ to the date ‘August 31, 2026’ for the aforementioned temporary relaxation. 2. Accordingly, in exercise of the powers conferred by Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act,1949 and all other laws enabling the Reserve Bank India (RBI) in this regard, the RBI, being satisfied that it is necessary and expedient in public interest so to do, hereby, issues the Amendment Directions hereinafter specified. 3. These Amendment Directions shall be called the Reserve Bank of India (Rural Co- operative Banks – Interest Rate on Deposits) Second Amendment Directions, 2026. 4. These Amendment Directions shall come into force with immediate effect. 5. These Amendment Directions shall modify the Directions, as under: i. In paragraph 24(4) subscript ( 1 ), the phrase “with effect from June 17, 2026, for the period until September 30, 2026” shall be substituted with “with effect from June 17, 2026, for the period until August 31, 2026”. ii. In paragraph 29(7) subscript ( 2 ), the phrase “with effect from June 17, 2026, for the period until September 30, 2026” shall be substituted with “with effect from June 17, 2026, for the period until August 31, 2026”. (Dr. Sudarsana Sahoo) Chief Gene
rows.summary:
The Reserve Bank of India’s **Reserve Bank of India (Rural Co-operative Banks – Interest Rate on Deposits) Second Amendment Directions, 2026** amends the earlier **Directions dated November 28, 2025** (updated June 17, 2026) that had granted a **temporary relaxation** on deposit pricing for rural co-operative banks. The underlying relaxation, which began **June 17, 2026**, had allowed the **temporary withdrawal of the interest rate ceiling on fresh FCNR(B) deposits with 3–5 year tenors** and had also **restricted interest rates on NRE deposits with tenors of 3 years and above, including renewals upon maturity**, originally running through **September 30, 2026**. This amendment shortens that end date by replacing **“September 30, 2026” with “August 31, 2026”** in the relevant provisions, so the temporary relaxation now applies only until **August 31, 2026**.

The amendment is issued under **Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949** and states that it is made in the public interest. It is titled the **Second Amendment Directions, 2026** and **takes effect immediately** upon issuance dated **August 25, 2026**. Operationally, compliance teams at affected rural co-operative banks should ensure that deposit-rate practices for the specified FCNR(B) and NRE categories are aligned to the revised sunset date and that any systems, product documentation, customer communications, or rate-setting controls referencing the earlier **September 30, 2026** deadline are updated to **August 31, 2026**.

The amendment updates the existing **Non-Banking Financial Companies – Concentration Risk Management Directions, 2025** by revising the **large exposure framework** for a specific class of entities: **Infrastructure Debt Fund–NBFCs (IDF-NBFCs)** that fall within the **Upper Layer** regulatory category.

Substantively, RBI has inserted a new **paragraph 39A** into **Chapter IV – Guidelines Applicable to NBFC – Upper Layer**. This new paragraph states that the **large exposure limits applicable to NBFC-IFCs** will also apply to **IDF-NBFCs** that are subject to Upper Layer regulation under **paragraph 60A of the RBI (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Undertaking of Financial Services) Directions, 2025**, read together with **paragraph 18(4)(i) of the RBI (Commercial Banks – Undertaking of Financial Services) Directions, 2025**. In practical terms, any IDF-NBFC in the Upper Layer must now comply with the same concentration/large exposure limits that apply to NBFC-IFCs, rather than relying on a separate framework.

For compliance purposes, the key takeaway is that affected **Upper Layer IDF-NBFCs** must immediately align their exposure monitoring, internal limits, and concentration-risk controls with the **NBFC-IFC large exposure regime**. The amendment does not specify new numerical thresholds in this text itself; instead, it imports the existing NBFC-IFC limits by reference. The change is regulatory in nature, is mandatory, and applies as soon as the amendment is in force.

rows.title: Implementation of Section 51A of UAPA, 1967: Updates to UNSC’s 1267/ 1989 ISIL (Da'esh) & Al-Qaida Sanctions List: Amendment of 21 Entries

In this connection, Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), Government of India has informed about the UNSC press release SC/16435, dated August 18, 2026 wherein the Security Council pursuant to resolutions 1267 (1999), 1989 (2011) and 2253 (2015) concerning ISIL (Da’esh), Al‑Qaida and associated individuals, groups, undertakings and entities enacted the amendments specified with strikethrough and underline in the entries mentioned in Annexure 1 on its ISIL (Da’esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions List of individuals and entities subject to the assets freeze, travel ban and arms embargo set out in paragraph 1 of Security Council resolution 2734 (2024), and adopted under Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations. 2 3. Press release dated August 18, 2026 regarding the above can be found at https://pres
rows.summary:
This RBI circular updates regulated entities on changes to the UNSC 1267/1989 ISIL (Da’esh) and Al‑Qaida Sanctions List and must be read together with Chapter IX of the RBI KYC Directions, 2025 (dated November 28, 2025, amended December 29, 2025). It reiterates that, under section 51A of the UAPA, 1967, regulated entities must not maintain any account in the name of any individual or entity appearing on the UNSC-approved list of persons/entities suspected of terrorist links. The circular is addressed to commercial banks, small finance banks, payment banks, urban co-operative banks, rural co-operative banks, regional rural banks, local area banks, NBFCs, asset reconstruction companies, and all India financial institutions.

The trigger for this update is Ministry of External Affairs intimation of UNSC press release SC/16435 dated August 18, 2026. That UNSC action, taken under resolutions 1267 (1999), 1989 (2011), and 2253 (2015) and adopted under Chapter VII of the UN Charter, amended the ISIL (Da’esh) and Al‑Qaida Sanctions List by changing 21 entries. The amendments are shown in Annexure 1 using strike-through and underline, and the list remains tied to the UN sanctions measures of asset freeze, travel ban, and arms embargo under Security Council resolution 2734 (2024).

For compliance purposes, the practical requirement is that firms must review the updated list and ensure their customer and sanctions-screening controls reflect the 21 amended entries immediately upon issuance of this circular. Any match to the updated UNSC list must be handled in accordance with the UAPA section 51A process and the RBI KYC Directions, including ensuring no account is maintained in the name of a listed person or entity. The circular also points readers to the UNSC press release dated August 18, 2026 as the source document for the amendments.

This RBI communication, dated **August 18, 2026**, directs all regulated entities covered by the **RBI KYC Directions, 2025**—including **commercial banks, small finance banks, payment banks, urban and rural co-operative banks, regional rural banks, local area banks, NBFCs, asset reconstruction companies, and all India financial institutions**—to continue ensuring compliance with **Section 51A of the UAPA, 1967** by not maintaining accounts in the names of persons or entities appearing on the UNSC-approved terrorism sanctions lists circulated under the Directions. The substantive change is an **amendment of 04 entries** on the sanctions list, shown in the document with **strikethrough and underline** formatting. Although the excerpt provided begins the listing of amended entries, the key compliance point is that regulated entities must treat the UNSC update as immediately relevant to screening, onboarding, and ongoing monitoring so that no account is opened or maintained for any listed individual/entity and any hit is handled in line with the existing UAPA/UNSC freezing obligations under the RBI Directions. Compliance teams should use the updated list circulated through the MEA/RBI framework and ensure sanctions screening logic, watchlists, and customer due diligence records reflect the amended UNSC entries without delay.

rows.title: Reserve Bank of India (Priority Sector Lending – Targets and Classification) Second Amendment Directions, 2026
