Effective **June 20, 2026**, the single filing system is being **extended to XBRL filing** for the newly covered event(s), and the Exchange has also released additional XBRL utilities. For the initial phase, companies may continue to submit the **PDF filing first**, and NSE will treat that PDF submission as compliance under Regulation 30; however, the listed entity must then **submit the corresponding XBRL filing within 24 hours** of the PDF submission. The XBRL utility for the newly covered events will be available in the Exchange portal under **COMPLIANCE >> Common XBRL Upload >> Equity Announcement- XBRL**, and the same filing will also be made available in **iXBRL/readable format** on NSE’s website at the specified corporate filings/announcements XBRL page.

The circular also states that the **XBRL utility and separate filing process for the Para B event in Part A of Schedule III of SEBI LODR 2015**—specifically **“Awarding, bagging/receiving, amendment or termination of awarded/bagged orders/contracts not in the normal course of business”**—will be **discontinued effective June 20, 2026** and **merged into the single utility for Para B events**. Compliance teams should therefore ensure that, from that date, these disclosures are routed through the updated single filing/API-based integration workflow and that the 24-hour XBRL follow-up requirement is met after any PDF submission.

This NSE circular (NSE/CML/2026/16 dated June 12, 2026) is addressed to all listed entities and provides FAQs for submitting the quarterly Integrated Filing – Governance, formerly called the Corporate Governance Report. NSE states that the FAQs are for guidance only and do not replace or amend the underlying requirements in law, SEBI regulations, or exchange circulars, but listed entities are specifically instructed to take note and comply accordingly.

The key compliance deadline confirmed in the FAQs is that the Integrated Filing – Governance report must be filed within 30 days from the end of each quarter, consistent with Regulation 27(2) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations. For newly listed entities, the filing obligation begins from the quarter ending immediately after the date of listing, so the first report is not due for the listing quarter itself but for the next quarter-end reporting period.

The document also makes clear that the filing must be submitted through the XBRL utility, and it covers the governance reporting format in detail across board composition, committee composition, board meetings, committee meetings, and “other” disclosures, as well as quarterly disclosures under Schedule III of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. Although the extract shown does not include the detailed answers for each topic, the circular signals that listed entities must use the FAQ framework to ensure their quarterly governance filing is completed correctly in the prescribed electronic format and within the statutory deadline.

The portion of the FAQs visible in the excerpt does not yet state any new substantive thresholds, ratios, or special exemptions, but it does emphasize that the filing obligation applies to listed entities generally and that the guidance should be read alongside the existing SEBI/LODR and exchange filing framework. Compliance teams should therefore treat this as an operational reminder and process guidance document, not as a replacement for the governing regulations, and should continue to ensure timely quarterly governance filings starting from the first quarter after listing.

rows.title:
Pre-Packaged Insolvency Resolution Process under Section 54L of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy 
Code, 2016.
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2026/15 Date: June 01, 2026 To All Listed Companies, Sub: Pre-Packaged Insolvency Resolution Process under Section 54L of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. Attention is invited to the provisions relating to Pre-Packaged Insolvency Resolution Process (“PPIRP”) under Chapter III-A of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (“IBC”). In this regard, as advised by SEBI, it is clarified that, the exemptions available under various SEBI Regulations in respect of a Resolution Plan approved under Section 31 of the IBC are not available in case of a Resolution Plan approved under Section 54L of the IBC under the PPIRP framework. Accordingly, listed entities undergoing PPIRP shall be required to comply with all applicable procedural and regulatory requirements prescribed under the relevant SEBI Regulations. The listed companies are advised to take note of the above and ensure compliance of the same. For and on behalf of National Stock Exchange of India Limited Yukti Sharma Head - Listing
rows.summary:
The NSE’s circular dated **June 1, 2026** clarifies how **Pre-Packaged Insolvency Resolution Process (PPIRP)** cases under **Section 54L / Chapter III-A of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC)** are to be treated for listed companies. SEBI has advised that the **regulatory exemptions that are available when a resolution plan is approved under Section 31 of the IBC do not apply** if the plan is approved under the **PPIRP framework under Section 54L**.

For compliance purposes, this means that a **listed entity undergoing PPIRP must continue to comply with all applicable procedural and regulatory requirements under the relevant SEBI Regulations**; it cannot assume that the usual listing-regulation exemptions linked to Section 31-approved resolution plans will be available. The circular does not create a new deadline or filing format, but it is an immediate compliance clarification for **all listed companies** that may enter PPIRP. Listed companies are specifically advised to take note and ensure they meet the full set of obligations under the applicable SEBI framework during PPIRP.

rows.title: Update of single filing system through API-based integration between Stock Exchanges
rows.summary:
The NSE has updated its **single filing system through API-based integration between stock exchanges** by expanding the **XBRL filing** functionality to additional disclosure events, effective **May 29, 2026** for most items listed in the circular. This update is issued under **Circular Ref. No. NSE/CML/2026/14 dated May 29, 2026**, and it refers back to the earlier framework in **NSE/CML/2024/28 dated September 30, 2024**. The practical compliance change is that eligible listed entities can now use the single filing/API-based exchange integration for these disclosures rather than filing separately across exchanges, subject to the applicability shown by category of listed entity.

For **Schedule of analysts or institutional investors meet, investor presentation, transcripts, and audio/video recordings** required under **Regulation 30 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 read with sub-para 15 of Para A, Part A of Schedule III**, the API-based single filing system is available from **May 29, 2026** and applies to **only equity** and **equity + debt** listed companies, but not to **exclusively debt** entities or **REITs/InvITs**. The same effective date and applicability applies to disclosures of **actions initiated or orders passed by any regulatory, statutory, enforcement authority, or judicial body** under **Regulation 30 read with sub-para 19 of Para A, Part A of Schedule III**, and **actions taken or orders passed by any regulatory, statutory, enforcement authority, or judicial body** under **Regulation 30 read with sub-para 20 of Para A, Part A of Schedule III**; these are available for **only equity** and **equity + debt** companies, but not for **exclusively debt** entities or **REITs/InvITs**.

The circular also states that **Initiation of forensic audit** under **Regulation 30 read with sub-para 17 of Para A, Part A of Schedule III** has been enabled through the single filing system with effect from **May 5, 2026**, again applicable only to **equity** and **equity + debt** listed companies. In addition, **Prohibition of Insider Trading** disclosures under **Regulation 7(2) and 7(3) of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015** are available through the same API-based filing system from **May 5, 2026**, and this row shows applicability to **only equity**, **equity + debt**, and **REITs/InvITs**, but not to **exclusively debt** listed entities.

The table in the circular also begins to list **Outcome of Board Meeting for Dividend, Buyback, Bonus and Voluntary Delisting events**, indicating this disclosure is part of the expanded API-based single filing framework as well, though the excerpt provided cuts off before the full applicability matrix and effective-date details are visible. For compliance teams, the key operational point is that listed entities must now route the above covered disclosures through the **single filing/API integration between exchanges** as soon as the relevant effective date applies, and confirm whether their entity type falls within the permitted categories for each disclosure type.

rows.title: Filing of disclosures in XBRL format under Regulation 7(2) and Regulation 7(3) of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2026/12 Date: May 04, 2026 To, The Company Secretary, All Listed Entities Subject: Filing of disclosures in XBRL format under Regulation 7(2) and Regulation 7(3) of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 Dear Sir/Madam, This is to inform you that disclosures under Regulation 7(2) and Regulation 7(3) of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 were previously being filed through the following path: NEAPS  Compliance  Disclosures  Insider Trading The above-mentioned filing path has now been discontinued, and a new XBRL based utility has been introduced for submission of such disclosures. Accordingly, all listed companies, REITs and InvITs are required to submit the aforesaid disclosure only in XBRL format through the revised process as detailed below: To download XBRL utility: NEAPS  Compliance  Download XBRL Utilities For Submission of disclosures: NEAPS  Compliance  Common XBRL Upload  Prohibition of Insider Trading Please note that previously filed disclosures shall continue to be available at the following link: https://www.nseindia.com/companies-listing/corporate-filings-insider-trading-archive-data Further, with reference to Exchange Circular No. NSE/CML/2026/11 dated May 04, 2026, the said utility will also be available for Single Filing system through API-based integration. You are requested to take note of the above and ensure compliance. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Harshad Dharod Chief Manager-Listing Compliance
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India has discontinued the old NEAPS submission path for insider trading disclosures under Regulation 7(2) and Regulation 7(3) of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. Going forward, all listed companies, REITs, and InvITs must file these disclosures only in XBRL format using the new process: the XBRL utility is to be downloaded through **NEAPS → Compliance → Download XBRL Utilities**, and the disclosures are to be submitted through **NEAPS → Compliance → Common XBRL Upload → Prohibition of Insider Trading**. The prior filing route **NEAPS → Compliance → Disclosures → Insider Trading** is no longer available for these filings.

The circular also states that disclosures already filed earlier will remain accessible through the NSE archive link provided in the notice: **https://www.nseindia.com/companies-listing/corporate-filings-insider-trading-archive-data**. In addition, NSE notes that, pursuant to **Exchange Circular No. NSE/CML/2026/11 dated May 04, 2026**, the same XBRL utility will also be available for the **Single Filing system through API-based integration**, which is relevant for entities using automated/API submission workflows. Compliance teams should ensure their filing process is updated immediately to the XBRL-only route and confirm that any internal reporting or system integrations are aligned with the revised submission method.

This circular updates the existing “single filing system” between stock exchanges by extending API-based XBRL filing integration to additional disclosures for listed entities, building on Exchange Circular No. NSE/CML/2024/28 dated September 30, 2024. The key change is that, effective April 25, 2026, the single filing system became available for XBRL filing of the “Outcome of Board Meeting for Dividend, Buyback, Bonus and Voluntary Delisting events” under Regulation 30 of SEBI (LODR) read with sub-para 4 of Para A, Part A of Schedule III; a footnote indicates the listed effective date in the table as April 25, 2026.

rows.title: XBRL based filing for Violations related to Code of Conduct (CoC) under SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2026/13 Date: May 04, 2026 To, The Company Secretary, All Listed Entities/Intermediaries/Fiduciaries Subject: XBRL based filing for Violations related to Code of Conduct (CoC) under SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 SEBI vide Circular No. SEBI/HO/ISD/ISD/CIR/P/2020/135 dated July 23, 2020, prescribed the format for reporting violations of the Code of Conduct under SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. To enhance accuracy and efficiency in disclosures, the Exchange has introduced an XBRL utility for reporting such violations through NEAPS with effect from May 05, 2026. All Listed Companies/Intermediaries/Fiduciaries shall submit the reporting through the following paths: To download XBRL utility: NEAPS  Compliance  Download XBRL Utilities For Submissions: NEAPS  Compliance  Common XBRL Upload  Violation of Code of Conduct under SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015 It may be noted that reporting by listed entities shall be made only in XBRL mode without submission of any PDF. Further, any unlisted entity reporting in the capacity of Intermediary or Fiduciary shall continue to submit the disclosures through email at pit_coc@nse.co.in, as per Exchange Circular No. NSE/CML/2020/44 dated August 26, 2020. The disclosure pertaining to violations of the Code of Conduct shall not be disseminated on the Exchange website. All listed entities are advised to mandatorily submit the reporting through NEAPS only. Submission through any other mode shall not be taken on record and shall be considered invalid. Listed entities, Intermediaries and Fiduciaries are advised to take note of the above and comply accordingly. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Harshad Dharod Chief Manager-Listing Compliance
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India has introduced a new XBRL-based filing process for reporting violations of the Code of Conduct under the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. This change is based on SEBI’s earlier circular dated July 23, 2020, which had prescribed the reporting format for Code of Conduct violations, but the NSE circular now requires use of an XBRL utility to improve accuracy and efficiency.

The new process is effective from May 05, 2026. From that date onward, all listed companies, intermediaries, and fiduciaries must use the NEAPS platform to submit these violation reports, with the utility downloadable through NEAPS under Compliance → Download XBRL Utilities and submissions made through Compliance → Common XBRL Upload → “Violation of Code of Conduct under SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015.” For listed entities specifically, the filing must be made only in XBRL mode and must not be accompanied by any PDF submission. Any submission by a listed entity through a channel other than NEAPS/XBRL will not be taken on record and will be treated as invalid.

The circular preserves the existing treatment for unlisted entities that are reporting in the capacity of intermediaries or fiduciaries: they must continue to send the disclosures by email to pit_coc@nse.co.in, as required under NSE Circular No. NSE/CML/2020/44 dated August 26, 2020. The circular also states that disclosures relating to Code of Conduct violations will not be disseminated on the Exchange website. Compliance teams should therefore ensure that listed entities switch to mandatory NEAPS XBRL filing immediately from the effective date, while unlisted intermediaries/fiduciaries continue using the email route.

rows.title: Update of single filing system through API-based integration between Stock Exchanges
rows.summary:
NSE has updated its **single filing system through API-based integration between stock exchanges**, expanding the scope of disclosures that can be filed once and then shared across exchanges. This update is issued under **Circular Ref. No. NSE/CML/2026/08 dated April 20, 2026**, and it references the earlier framework from **NSE/CML/2024/28 dated September 30, 2024**.

The main change is that, **with effect from April 20, 2026**, the single filing system now also applies to **XBRL filings for Annual Report filings under Regulation 34 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**. The circular indicates that this facility is available for **listed entities that are Equity and Equity+Debt listed companies**, and it is **not available** for **Exclusively Debt**, **REITs**, or **InvITs** for this disclosure. The circular specifically marks the Annual Report-XBRL item as applicable from **April 20, 2026**.

The circular also states that the API-based single filing system is available for certain **Regulation 30 LODR disclosures**, including disclosures relating to **acquisition, amalgamation, merger, de-merger, sale or disposal, or other restructuring** under **Regulation 30 read with sub-para 1 of Para A, Part A of Schedule III**. It further covers disclosures for **changes in directors, key managerial personnel such as the Managing Director, Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Company Secretary, and other senior management, as well as changes in the auditor, compliance officer, and registrar to an issue and share transfer agent** under **Regulation 30 read with sub-paras 7 and 8 of Para A, Part A of Schedule III**.

For resignation-related filings, the circular notes that the utility now provides an option to submit both the **resignation details and the resignation letter(s)** where required under **sub-paras 7A, 7B, and 7C of Para A, Part A of Schedule III**. It also expressly includes **resignation of the statutory auditor** under **Regulation 30 read with sub-para 7A**, and **resignation of an independent director, director, KMP, SMP, or compliance officer** under **Regulation 30 read with sub-paras 7B and 7C**. For compliance teams, the practical obligation is to use the updated filing utility for the above covered events from the effective date, and ensure the correct supporting resignation documents are uploaded wherever the regulation requires them.

rows.title: Update on single filing system through API-based integration between Stock Exchanges
rows.summary:
The circular updates the NSE’s “single filing system” implemented through API-based integration between stock exchanges, expanding the types of XBRL/disclosure filings that can be filed once and then shared across exchanges. This update is issued by NSE Circular Ref. No. NSE/CML/2026/05 dated March 30, 2026, and it references the earlier circular NSE/CML/2024/28 dated September 30, 2024.

The main change is that, effective March 31, 2026, the single-filing API system is extended to cover the XBRL filing for the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) under Regulation 34(2)(f) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. The circular indicates this filing is available for listed entities that are equity-only and equity-plus-debt listed companies; it is not marked as available for exclusively debt listed entities, REITs, or INVITs.

The circular also lists other disclosures that are already covered or have specific effective dates within the single-filing framework, including prior intimation of board meetings under Regulation 29 of SEBI (LODR), effective March 7, 2026; closure of trading window under the SEBI PIT Regulations; fraud/default/arrest disclosures under Regulation 30 and Para A Part A Schedule III of SEBI (LODR), effective February 21, 2026; corporate debt restructuring disclosures; resolution plans/restructuring involving bank/financial institution borrowings, including Inter-Creditors Agreement and one-time settlement (OTS); and Issue Summary Document (ISD) filings for buybacks through open and tender routes under the relevant SEBI circular. The table shows these are applicable to equity and equity-plus-debt listed entities, while the debt-only, REIT, and INVIT columns remain unmarked for these items.

For integrated filing of financials under Regulations 23(9), 30 read with Section V-B of the Master Circular, and Regulations 32(1) and 33(3), the circular shows an effective date of January 3, 2026 for equity and equity-plus-debt listed entities, but states that applicability for exclusively debt listed entities and REITs/INVITs “shall be communicated later.” The table also includes “Annual Secretarial Compliance Report” as an item in the sequence of filings covered by the single filing system, but the excerpt provided cuts off before showing the full applicability/effective-date details for that line.

From a compliance perspective, listed entities should confirm whether they fall into the equity, equity-plus-debt, debt-only, or REIT/INVIT category before relying on the API-based single filing process. Entities that are in scope for the newly extended BRSR filing should begin using the single-filing mechanism for that disclosure from March 31, 2026, while continuing to track any separate exchange or regulatory instructions for categories that are not yet marked as covered.

This circular updates the existing “single filing system” created under Exchange Circular No. NSE/CML/2024/28 dated September 30, 2024 by extending the API-based, single-filing/XBRL integration to additional disclosure types for listed entities. The Exchange states that, with effect from **March 07, 2026**, the single filing system will now also be available for **XBRL filings** relating to **Prior Intimation for Board Meeting under Regulation 29 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**. The table in the circular also shows that the following disclosure categories are now within the single-filing/API framework for the relevant classes of listed entities: **Closure of Trading Window** under the SEBI PIT Regulations; **Fraud/Default/Arrest** disclosures under **Regulation 30 of SEBI LODR** and **sub-para 6 of Para A, Part A of Schedule III**; **Corporate Debt Restructuring** under **Regulation 30 of SEBI LODR** and **sub-paras 9 and 10 of Para A, Part A of Schedule III**; **Resolution plan / restructuring in relation to loans or borrowings from banks/financial institutions (including Inter-Creditors Agreement) and One Time Settlement (OTS)**; and **Issue Summary Document (ISD)** for **buyback through open and tender route** under the SEBI circular on ISD and issue advertisements.

The circular specifies that the applicability of these filings varies by issuer type. The table indicates that the single-filing system is available for **Equity-listed entities** and **Equity + Debt listed entities**, while the columns for **Exclusively Debt** and **REITs and INVITs** are marked as not applicable for the disclosed items shown. For some disclosure categories, the table already shows earlier effective dates: **Fraud/Default/Arrest** is marked effective **February 21, 2026**, **Integrated Filing – Financials** is marked effective **January 03, 2026**, and **Annual Secretarial Compliance Report** is marked effective **September 15, 2025**. The table also indicates that for certain categories shown, applicability for “Exclusively Debt” and “REITs and INVITs” will be **“communicated later,”** so those entities should not assume coverage unless and until a separate communication is issued.

From a compliance perspective, the practical change is that listed entities covered by the relevant rows should route the specified disclosures through the Exchange’s **API-based single filing system/XBRL mechanism** rather than treating stock exchange submissions separately, subject to the exact category and entity type. Companies secretaries and disclosure teams should align internal calendars and filing workflows to the stated effective date of **March 07, 2026** for the newly extended items and confirm whether any earlier-effective items already need to be in the single-filing process. The circular does not introduce monetary thresholds, rates, or penalties; its core requirement is procedural integration of filings across stock exchanges for the covered disclosure categories.

The NSE has updated its single filing system through API-based integration between stock exchanges, extending the system to cover XBRL filings for certain **Regulation 30** disclosures, effective **February 21, 2026**. This update means eligible listed entities can now use the single filing/API-based process for filings relating to **Fraud/Default/Arrest** under **Regulation 30, sub-para 6 of Para A, Part A of Schedule III of SEBI LODR**, **Corporate Debt Restructuring** under **sub-para 9 and 10 of Para A, Part A of Schedule III**, **resolution plans/restructuring in relation to bank or financial institution borrowings (including Inter-Creditors Agreement) and One Time Settlement (OTS)**, and the **Issue Summary Document (ISD)** for **buybacks via open and tender route** under the SEBI circular introducing ISD and dissemination of issue advertisements. For these newly extended items, the table indicates the facility is available for **Equity** and **Equity + Debt** listed companies, while it is not marked as available for **Exclusively Debt**, **REITs**, or **InvITs** for these rows.

The circular also reproduces earlier already-enabled categories in the single filing framework, including **Integrated Filing – Financials** under **Regulations 23(9), 30 read with Section V-B of the Master Circular, 32(1), and 33(3)** with an effective date of **January 03, 2026**, **Annual Secretarial Compliance Report** under **Regulation 24A(2)** with an effective date of **September 15, 2025**, and **Integrated Filing (Governance)** under **Regulations 13(3), 27(2), and 30** with an effective date of **March 01, 2025**. For those categories, the table indicates applicability to **Equity** and **Equity + Debt** listed companies, while applicability for **Exclusively Debt**, **REITs**, and **InvITs** is marked as “shall be communicated later.” The circular is addressed to the **Company Secretaries of all listed entities** and is an update to **NSE/CML/2024/28 dated September 30, 2024**, so compliance teams should ensure that, from **February 21, 2026**, the relevant Regulation 30 XBRL disclosures and buyback ISD filings are routed through the updated single filing/API mechanism where applicable.

rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE), through Circular No. NSE/CML/2026/02 dated February 3, 2026, is seeking comments and feedback on a proposed shift to an XBRL-based filing framework for Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP) applications. The proposal would replace the current application-based process, under which listed entities manually enter information and upload supporting documents in PDF format, with an XBRL-exclusive filing process.

The document explains that listed entities are already required under the SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015, SEBI ICDR Regulations, 2018, and other applicable provisions/circulars/guidance notes, to obtain Stock Exchange approval for QIP-related issuances. The approvals covered in this proposal are the in-principle approval and post-allotment listing approval (the circular text also refers generally to QIP applications and notes that companies currently file in-principle approval, post-allotment approval, and trading approval requests with the exchange). The stated rationale is to continue the exchanges’ phased migration from document-based filings to XBRL reporting in order to standardize securities market data, improve regulatory efficiency, and make filing and monitoring easier for both listed entities and the exchange.

If implemented as described, the new requirement would mean that QIP-related information must be filed by listed entities in XBRL only, using the prescribed XBRL formats that the circular says are being made available. The document is framed as a consultation/feedback exercise rather than an effective rule change, so it does not itself set a compliance deadline or effective date for mandatory adoption; instead, it asks stakeholders to review and comment on the proposed transition.

rows.summary:
The NSE has issued an update to its single filing system through API-based integration between stock exchanges, referring back to its circular of September 30, 2024. The main change is that the single filing system has now been extended to cover **Integrated Filing (Financials)** under **Regulation 33 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**, and this extension is **effective January 03, 2026**. This means listed entities that fall within the applicable categories can use the API-based single filing mechanism for this financial disclosure instead of separate filings, subject to the availability and applicability set out by the exchange.

The circular identifies the disclosures currently available through the single filing system and ties each one to its governing regulation and rollout date. For **Integrated Filing (Financials)**, the relevant provisions are **Regulation 23(9), Regulation 30 read with Section V-B of the Master Circular, Regulation 32(1), and Regulation 33(3)**, and the facility is marked as available from **January 03, 2026** for **equity** and **equity+debt** listed companies; for **exclusively debt** issuers and **REITs/INVITs**, the circular says the position will be **communicated later**. The other disclosures already listed as part of the broader single filing framework are **Annual Secretarial Compliance Report** under **Regulation 24A(2)** effective **September 15, 2025**; **Integrated Filing (Governance)** under **Regulations 13(3), 27(2), and 30** effective **March 01, 2025**; **Meetings of shareholders and voting results** under **Regulation 44(3)** effective **December 28, 2024**; and **Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit Report** under **Regulation 76** effective **November 15, 2024**.

The circular also clarifies a status change for the **Corporate Governance Report** under **Regulation 27(2)**: it was effective **October 26, 2024**, but has now been **merged with Integrated Filing (Governance)** pursuant to a **SEBI circular dated December 31, 2024**. For the categories where the table shows “shall be communicated later,” the exchange has not yet provided implementation timing for **exclusively debt** and **REIT/INVIT** entities for some filings, so compliance teams for those entity types should not assume immediate availability beyond what is expressly stated. In practical terms, listed entities should verify whether they are in the **equity** or **equity+debt** category to determine immediate use of the API-based single filing system for financials from **January 3, 2026**, and they should continue following the prescribed SEBI regulation-specific filing obligations through the single filing mechanism as rolled out by the exchange.

rows.title: SEBI Circular on “Minimum information to be provided to the Audit Committee and Shareholders for approval of Related Party Transactions.”
rows.summary:
SEBI has issued Circular No. **SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/135 dated October 13, 2025**, which is being circulated by NSE to all listed entities. The circular does **not create an entirely new RPT approval framework**, but reinforces that listed entities must follow the **“Minimum information to be provided to the Audit Committee and Shareholders for approval of Related Party Transactions”** standards already formulated by the **Industry Standards Forum (ISF)** under the SEBI Master Circular dated **November 11, 2024** and SEBI Circular dated **June 26, 2025**.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that **minimum disclosure information for Related Party Transaction (RPT) approvals must be provided to both the Audit Committee and shareholders** when seeking approval for such transactions. This applies to **all listed entities** and is relevant whenever an RPT requires approval at either forum. The document is a direction to follow the ISF-issued standards, meaning companies should ensure their board/audit committee/shareholder approval materials contain the required minimum information set out under those standards, rather than relying on ad hoc or incomplete transaction summaries.

The NSE circular dated **October 14, 2025** simply forwards SEBI’s October 13 circular and states that it is for the recipient’s **reference and necessary action**. No separate numeric threshold, filing deadline, or monetary limit is stated in the excerpt provided; however, the compliance obligation is immediate in the sense that listed entities are expected to align their RPT approval materials with the prescribed minimum information requirements already in force under the SEBI framework. Compliance teams should therefore review current RPT approval templates, audit committee notes, and shareholder resolution support documents to ensure they conform to the ISF minimum-information standard before the next RPT approval cycle.

rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India has issued a listing compliance circular dated October 9, 2025 to all REITs and all InvITs requiring them to file financial results in XBRL mode using a revised format. The change is based on SEBI’s Master Circulars dated July 11, 2025 — SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/99 for REITs and SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/102 for InvITs — which revised the financial results submission format under Chapter 4 on continuous disclosures and compliances.

NSE states that the updated Excel utility for the revised format is now available on the NEAPS portal at Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Invit/Reit- Financial Results, and the file name to use is “Financial Results_Invits_Reits.” The compliance obligation is that REITs and InvITs must submit their financial results in XBRL mode within 24 hours after submitting the financial results in PDF mode. In practical terms, this creates a two-step filing process: first the PDF submission, then the XBRL submission within the 24-hour window.

For operational questions, the circular directs entities to the contact details available on NEAPS under NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance, or to email listingfr@nse.co.in. No separate effective date beyond the circular date is stated, so the requirement appears to apply immediately upon issuance and use of the revised filing utility.

rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India has updated its single filing system through API-based integration between stock exchanges, expanding it to include the **Annual Secretarial Compliance Report under Regulation 24A(2) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**, with **effect from September 15, 2025**. This means listed entities covered by this reporting obligation will be able to submit the report through the single-filing/API mechanism instead of separate exchange filings, in line with the NSE’s earlier circular dated September 30, 2024 on the same system.

The circular also restates the set of disclosures currently covered by the API-based single filing framework and their implementation dates: **Investor Grievance Report under Regulation 13(3)** became effective **October 1, 2024** and is noted as being **merged with Integrated Filing (Governance)** pursuant to the SEBI circular dated December 31, 2024; **Corporate Governance Report under Regulation 27(2)** became effective **October 26, 2024**; **Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit Report under Regulation 76** became effective **November 15, 2024**; **Meetings of shareholders and Voting Results under Regulation 44(3)** became effective **December 28, 2024**; and **Integrated Filing (Governance) under Regulations 13(3), 27(2) and 30** became effective **March 1, 2025**. The newly added **Annual Secretarial Compliance Report under Regulation 24A(2)** is effective **September 15, 2025**.

For applicability, the circular indicates the single-filing/API system is available to **equity-listed companies** and **equity + debt listed companies** for the covered disclosures marked with a tick in the table. The table also indicates that for **exclusively debt listed entities** and for **REITs and InvITs**, availability for some items is marked **“shall be communicated later,”** meaning the NSE has not yet announced implementation for those categories. The practical compliance requirement is that affected listed entities should route the applicable reports through the single filing system via API-based integration starting on the stated effective dates, so that filings are captured once and shared across exchanges under the framework.

rows.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on Applicability of the Industry Standards on “Minimum information to be provided for Review of the Audit Committee and Shareholders for Approval of Related Party Transaction (RPT)”
rows.summary:
This NSE circular (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2025/36 dated September 4, 2025) informs all listed entities that SEBI’s June 26, 2025 circular on the “Industry Standards on Minimum information to be provided for Review of the Audit Committee and Shareholders for Approval of Related Party Transaction (RPT)” is now accompanied by FAQs for implementation guidance and necessary action. The most important compliance point is that the RPT Industry Standards **replace the prior RPT disclosure formats** in Section III-B of NSE’s Master Circular dated November 11, 2024, rather than merely supplement them. The FAQ expressly states that the new standards substitute the Section III-B disclosure requirement from the “specified date,” and if any part of the standards conflicts with later amendments to the LODR Regulations and/or SEBI circulars, those later regulatory changes prevail.

For compliance teams, the practical impact is that listed entities must use the new minimum-information framework when preparing materials for **Audit Committee review** and **Shareholder approval** of related party transactions, instead of the old disclosure templates under the Master Circular. The document does not introduce a separate numerical threshold, rate, or transaction cap; its significance is in changing the **required disclosure format/content** for RPT approval processes and clarifying that the FAQs should be used as reference and for necessary action. The circular also points readers to NSE’s website for the circular text and the enclosed FAQs, which should be treated as part of the implementation guidance for determining what information must be provided in RPT approval submissions.

rows.title: Processing of waiver applications by the Exchanges in case of commonly listed entities.
rows.summary:
NSE has announced a new procedure for waiver applications relating to SOP fines for **commonly listed entities**—that is, listed companies that are listed on more than one exchange. The change is intended to streamline handling of waiver requests, speed up disposal, and ensure uniform outcomes where the same non-compliance has resulted in penalties from multiple exchanges. Under the new arrangement, waiver applications from such entities will be **segregated so that only one exchange processes the request**, and the **decision of that one exchange will be binding on all other exchanges** that have levied penalties for the same non-compliance.

This policy is being implemented in the context of SEBI’s SOP framework, under which exchanges monitor listed-entity filings and may impose actions such as **penalties, shifting securities to the “Z” category, freezing promoter holdings, and suspension of trading** for non-compliance. SEBI has also required that if an exchange deviates from the prescribed SOP actions, it must do so **only after recording written reasons**. To handle waiver requests, exchanges had already constituted internal committees, and this circular formalizes a coordinated process for commonly listed companies.

A further new requirement is that the exchange assigned to process the waiver application will charge a **nominal non-refundable processing fee**. The circular states that the detailed procedural aspects and the applicable fee schedule are provided in the policy, and that these rules will apply to **waiver applications seeking waiver of SOP fines submitted on or after September 1, 2025**.

For compliance purposes, this means any commonly listed entity seeking waiver of SOP fines after that effective date should expect the application to be handled through a single designated exchange rather than separately across multiple exchanges, and the resulting decision will apply across all exchanges involved in the same penalty matter. Companies should also budget for the new **non-refundable processing fee** and ensure waiver submissions are complete and timely under the new single-processing framework.

rows.summary:
This NSE circular is an intimation to all Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs), all parties to InvITs, and all registered depositories that SEBI has issued Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/114 dated August 8, 2025, titled **“Review of Framework for conversion of Private Listed InvIT into Public InvIT.”** The NSE notice itself does not set out the operative regulatory changes, conditions, thresholds, or procedural steps; it simply forwards SEBI’s circular and states that the enclosed SEBI circular should be referred to for “necessary action.”  

From a compliance perspective, the immediate requirement is to review the SEBI circular enclosed with the NSE communication and assess whether the entity is a **private listed InvIT** seeking conversion to a **public InvIT**, or is otherwise involved in that conversion process as a party or depository. The date of the NSE notice is **August 12, 2025**, and it refers to the SEBI circular issued **August 8, 2025**; no separate compliance deadline is stated in the NSE text itself. The NSE notice also indicates the circular is available on the NSE website for reference.  

Because the NSE communication is purely forwarding information, it does **not** specify any new obligations, filing forms, approvals, eligibility criteria, timelines, percentage thresholds, valuation requirements, or investor-protection conditions on its face. A compliance team should therefore treat this as a trigger to obtain and analyze the underlying SEBI circular, which is the document that contains the actual framework for conversion and any actionable requirements.

rows.title: Circular on System driven disclosure for Credit Rating- Regulation 30 and ESG Rating as per SEBI Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements 2015. (‘SEBI LODR’)
rows.summary:
This circular sets out the stock-exchange-led, system-driven disclosure framework for two types of ratings under SEBI LODR: credit ratings reported under Regulation 30(6) read with sub-para 3 of Para A of Part A of Schedule III, and ESG ratings disclosed under the ESG Rating Provider framework. It is issued to all listed entities, all SEBI-registered credit rating agencies (CRAs), and all SEBI-registered ESG rating providers (ERPs), and it follows earlier SEBI directions that exchanges, in consultation with SEBI, must define the process, procedure, and timelines for automated disclosure of “new rating(s) or revision in ratings,” as well as publication of ESG ratings on stock-exchange websites.

For credit ratings, the circular implements system-driven disclosure for any new rating or revision in rating that is required to be filed/disclosed by a listed entity under Regulation 30(6). The practical effect is that the disclosure will be generated through the exchange system rather than relying only on manual issuer-driven publication. Listed entities remain responsible for the underlying compliance event, but the exchange infrastructure becomes the mechanism for public dissemination of the rating information once the rating is filed.

For ESG ratings, the circular gives effect to SEBI’s April 29, 2025 clarificatory/procedural changes requiring stock exchanges to prominently display ESG ratings on their websites in a separate tab/section. If the ESG rating is for an issuer/entity, the disclosure must appear on the stock exchange where that issuer is listed, on the listed company’s page; if the ESG rating is for a debt security, the disclosure must appear on the stock exchange where that security is listed, on the listed security’s page. The requirement is specifically for prominent website disclosure in a dedicated section, not buried in a generic filings area.

The circular is operative as part of the exchanges’ implementation of the SEBI framework referenced above, so compliance teams should assume these disclosures will be system-triggered through exchange infrastructure and should ensure ratings data submitted to CRAs/ERPs and exchanged via the listed entity’s filing processes is accurate, timely, and complete. From a controls perspective, listed entities should verify that rating actions they are required to disclose under LODR are promptly captured in the exchange system, and they should confirm that the relevant stock exchange page reflects the correct credit rating and ESG rating information for the issuer or debt security as applicable.

rows.title: Joint Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for application filed under Regulation 37 and 59A of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 w.r.t. Scheme of Arrangements.
rows.summary:
This NSE circular, dated July 31, 2025, introduces a **Joint Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)** for applications filed under **Regulation 37 and Regulation 59A of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015** in relation to **schemes of arrangement**. It is stated to be **in addition to** NSE Circular **NSE/CML/2023/70 dated September 29, 2023** and BSE Notice **20230929-30 dated September 29, 2023**, and it was issued because SEBI advised the exchanges to streamline and expedite the scheme-of-arrangement approval process.

The circular applies to **all listed entities** and their **company secretaries** that are proposing or are involved in a scheme of arrangement. It specifies that the SOP and related guidance are to be read with the **SEBI Master Circular dated June 20, 2023 and May 21, 2024**. The document lists several supporting materials: an SOP for applications under Reg. 37 and Reg. 59A, an SOP for applications seeking relaxation under **sub-rule (7) of rule 19 of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Rules, 1957**, checklists for both types of applications, and FAQs on schemes of arrangement.

The key effective date is explicit: **the circular is applicable with effect from August 1, 2025**. From that date onward, listed entities filing a draft scheme of arrangement before any court or tribunal must follow the new joint SOP and the associated checklist/FAQ framework for their regulatory submissions. The document excerpt provided begins the Annexure I SOP by stating that a listed entity desirous of undertaking or involved in a scheme of arrangement must file the **draft scheme of arrangement** before the relevant judicial forum under the applicable legal provisions, indicating that the filing process is being standardized at the exchange level for Reg. 37 and 59A matters.

rows.title: Intimation of credit of Dividend into attached bank accounts of notified parties under Special Court (TORTS) Act 1992
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India Limited issued Listing Circular NSE/CML/2025/31 on July 23, 2025 to all listed entities, through their company secretaries, regarding dividend payments to parties whose bank accounts are attached under the Special Court (TORTS) Act, 1992. The Exchange says it received a letter from the Custodian’s office and is directing listed entities to ensure that whenever an online dividend payment is credited into the bank account of any notified party, the listed entity must send intimation of that credit to the Custodian’s office without fail for further necessary action.

For compliance purposes, the practical requirement is not a change in dividend policy or a new payment threshold, but a mandatory notification step tied to dividend credits made into attached accounts of notified parties under the Special Court (TORTS) Act regime. The circular does not specify a separate deadline date, implementation window, monetary threshold, or reporting format; instead, it requires immediate and consistent compliance whenever such a credit occurs. Listed entities should therefore have procedures in place to identify when dividend disbursements are made to notified parties subject to account attachment and to ensure prompt communication to the Custodian each time. The circular closes by stating that listed entities are “once again requested” to take note and comply accordingly, indicating the Exchange expects ongoing adherence rather than a one-time action.

rows.title:
Filing of Announcements pertaining to Awarding, bagging/ receiving of orders/contracts in XBRL format on 
NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform.
rows.desc: Non-Confidential Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2025/30 Date: July 07, 2025 To, The Company Secretaries, All Listed Entities Subject: Filing of Announcements pertaining to Awarding, bagging/ receiving of orders/contracts in XBRL format on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform. Further to the various Exchange circulars (Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2023/34 dated May 15, 2023, Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2023/28 dated March 31, 2023, Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2023/11 dated January 27, 2023, Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2023/85 dated December 08, 2023) issued for filing of equity announcement for the Regulation 30 events in XBRL mode, the facility for filing disclosures for the event Awarding, bagging/ receiving, amendment or termination of awarded/bagged orders/contracts (whether in normal course or not in normal course) has now been made available in XBRL format and will be effective for filing from July 07, 2025. At the initial stage, the PDF filings will be considered by the Exchange as compliance under Regulation 30 of the SEBI LODR Regulations 2015. Further, all listed entities would be required to submit the filings in XBRL mode within 24 hours of submission of the said PDF filing. The XBRL utility for the above-mentioned event is made available at the path COMPLIANCE >> Common XBRL Upload>> Equity Announcement- XBRL >> Awarding or Bagging of Orders/Contracts Further, it may be noted that the aforesaid XBRL filing, will be made available in iXBRL format to the listed entities/stakeholders on the website of the Exchange at path https://www.nseindia.com/companies-listing/corporate-filings- announcements-xbrl (selection of announcement type) and it will also be made available to the listed entities at the path Report >> Announcement XBRL Report in NEAPS. Note: 1. It has been observed that the listed entities are submitting the disclosures for awarding/bagging of orders/contracts under Updates or Press Release, it is hereby advised
rows.summary:
NSE Circular No. NSE/CML/2025/30 dated July 7, 2025 expands the Exchange’s XBRL filing framework to cover Regulation 30 disclosures for the award, bagging/receipt, amendment, or termination of orders/contracts, whether entered into in the ordinary course of business or otherwise. This new XBRL utility is available on the NEAPS platform under **COMPLIANCE >> Common XBRL Upload >> Equity Announcement- XBRL >> Awarding or Bagging of Orders/Contracts**, and the filing requirement is effective immediately for disclosures made on or after **July 7, 2025**.

For compliance purposes, NSE states that at the initial stage it will treat the **PDF filing** as satisfying the listed entity’s Regulation 30 disclosure obligation, but the entity must then file the same disclosure in **XBRL within 24 hours** of submitting the PDF. The Exchange also notes that the XBRL disclosure will be made available in **iXBRL** format on NSE’s corporate filings/announcements webpage and in NEAPS under **Report >> Announcement XBRL Report**, so companies should expect the submission to flow into both the public website and internal reporting views.

The circular also reinforces that disclosures about awarding/bagging of orders/contracts should not be routed merely as **Updates** or **Press Release** items; they should be filed through the prescribed Regulation 30 announcement process. In practical terms, listed entities need to ensure their internal workflows identify these contract/order events, prepare the PDF disclosure promptly, and then complete the XBRL upload within the 24-hour window to remain compliant with the Exchange’s filing process.

rows.title: SEBI Circular on Industry Standards on “Minimum information to be provided to the Audit Committee and Shareholders for approval of Related Party Transactions.”
rows.summary:
SEBI has issued a circular dated **June 26, 2025** establishing **industry standards on the minimum information that must be provided to the Audit Committee and to shareholders when seeking approval for Related Party Transactions (RPTs)** under **Regulations 23(2), 23(3) and 23(4) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**. The circular applies to **all listed entities** and is also addressed to the **recognized stock exchanges** and industry bodies; the NSE has circulated it to listed entities for implementation. The practical compliance change is that companies can no longer rely on generic or minimal RPT papers: they must now provide the **prescribed minimum set of information, in the specified format**, to support approval by the Audit Committee and, where required, shareholders.

The circular is part of SEBI’s effort to standardize RPT approval materials across the market, so that the decision-makers receive consistent information before approving a transaction. For compliance teams, the key implication is that **all RPT proposals placed before the Audit Committee and shareholders must be prepared in line with the new industry standards note enclosed with the circular**, and those materials should contain the minimum disclosures required by the standard before approval is sought. The document also indicates that SEBI expects listed entities to take **“necessary action”** based on the circular and accompanying standards note, meaning internal RPT approval templates, board/audit committee packs, and shareholder approval documentation may need to be revised immediately.

The NSE circular itself does not set a separate future compliance date or phased implementation timeline in the text provided; the governing date visible in the circular is **June 26, 2025**. The circular is expressly linked to the SEBI-issued industry standards note titled **“Minimum information to be provided to the Audit Committee and Shareholders for approval of Related Party Transactions”**, which is the operative reference point for what information must be furnished. In short, listed entities must ensure that any RPT seeking approval is supported by the newly standardized minimum disclosure package, and compliance teams should review and update their RPT approval workflow, documents, and shareholder-resolution support materials accordingly.

Dear Sir / Madam, This is with reference to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/IMD/IMD-RAC/P/CIR/2025/54 dated April 11, 2025, issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (‘SEBI’) titled “Specialized Investment Funds (‘SIF’) – Application and Investment Strategy Information Document (ISID) formats”. A copy of SEBI Circular dated April 11, 2025, is enclosed for your reference and for necessary action at your end. The copy of the circular is also available on the NSE website (www.nseindia.com). This is for your information please. Yours Faithfully For National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. Akshay Agarwal Senior Manager- Listing Approval Encl: 1. SEBI Circular
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) circular dated **May 7, 2025** is addressed to **all mutual funds and all Asset Management Companies (AMCs)** and is issued only as a forwarding communication referencing a SEBI circular; the NSE notice itself does not introduce separate requirements, but it alerts market participants that SEBI has issued binding guidance on **Specialized Investment Funds (SIFs)**. The underlying SEBI circular is **SEBI/HO/IMD/IMD-RAC/P/CIR/2025/54 dated April 11, 2025**, titled **“Specialized Investment Funds (‘SIF’) – Application and Investment Strategy Information Document (ISID) formats”**, and the NSE states that a copy is enclosed and also available on its website for necessary action.

From the content provided, the material compliance point is that **SEBI has prescribed standardized application and Investment Strategy Information Document (ISID) formats for SIFs**, which affects entities operating or launching Specialized Investment Funds and the AMCs/mutual funds that manage or distribute them. The document excerpt does **not** provide the actual form fields, operational instructions, or any numeric thresholds, rates, or phased deadlines; it only confirms that the SEBI circular exists and should be followed. Compliance teams should therefore treat this as a notice to obtain and implement the SEBI-prescribed **application format and ISID format** for any SIF-related offering or documentation process, and verify internal onboarding, disclosure, and product-approval workflows against the April 11, 2025 SEBI circular.

Because the NSE circular is informational and says “**This is for your information please**,” it does not itself impose a new standalone deadline, but the operative compliance obligations, if any, would arise from the referenced SEBI circular. A corporate compliance team should review the SEBI circular in full to determine exactly how SIF applications and ISIDs must be prepared, approved, and maintained, and whether any existing fund-launch or investor-disclosure templates must be updated to the prescribed format.

rows.title: FAQs on SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is a forwarding notice to all listed companies that SEBI has published FAQs explaining how to implement the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2024, which were dated December 12, 2024, as well as SEBI’s implementing circular dated December 31, 2024. The FAQs relate to the recommendations of SEBI’s Expert Committee intended to make it easier for listed entities to do business, so the practical purpose is to clarify compliance expectations under the amended LODR framework rather than to introduce a separate NSE rule of its own.

The circular itself does not set new thresholds, filing deadlines, rates, or standalone obligations; instead, it alerts listed companies that SEBI has issued an FAQ document clarifying how the December 2024 amendments should be applied. Compliance teams for listed entities should review the SEBI FAQ and the December 31, 2024 circular together with the Third Amendment Regulations to determine whether their existing disclosure, governance, or other listing-obligation processes need to be adjusted in light of the clarified implementation guidance. The FAQ document is available on SEBI’s website, and this NSE notice encloses a copy for reference.

rows.title: Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of Securities and Exchange Board of India (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 - Extension of automated implementation of trading window closure to Immediate Relatives of Designated Persons, on account of declaration of financial results
rows.summary:
The NSE circular dated April 21, 2025 informs all listed companies of SEBI’s new circular dated the same day, which extends the automated trading window closure mechanism to the immediate relatives of designated persons (“DPs”) when financial results are being declared. This is an expansion of the earlier framework under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, and it builds on prior NSE circulars from 2022–2024 that implemented the system of freezing PAN at the security level to restrict trading by DPs during closed periods.

The key change is that, where a company has to close the trading window on account of declaration of financial results, the automated restriction is no longer limited to the DP alone; it now also applies to the DP’s immediate relatives. The purpose, as stated by SEBI, is to make compliance easier and to reduce inadvertent violations of the PIT Regulations by DPs and persons connected to them. The circular does not create a new trading restriction period or alter the underlying obligation to keep the trading window closed; rather, it broadens the population subject to the existing automated block.

For compliance teams, the practical requirement is to ensure that systems and records used for PAN-based trading restrictions at the security level are capable of identifying and freezing trading access for immediate relatives of DPs during the trading window closure period triggered by financial results. Companies should verify that their internal insider lists, relative mappings, and automated controls are updated so the restriction is implemented correctly and consistently. The circular is issued in continuation of the earlier NSE/SEBI circulars referenced in it and should be treated as an operational enhancement to existing PIT compliance procedures rather than a standalone regime.

rows.title: Updates on the Implementation of recommendations of the Expert Committee for facilitating ease of doing business for listed entities - Disclosure of Integrated Filing - Financial
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India has updated listed entities on the rollout of the SEBI-mandated “Integrated Filing - Financial” process under SEBI circular SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/CIR/P/2024/185 dated December 31, 2024, as referenced in the Exchange’s earlier circular dated January 2, 2025. The key operational change is that the XBRL utility for “Integrated Filing - Financial” is now available on the NEAPS portal, and listed entities must use this utility only to submit financial results in XBRL mode via the path Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Integrated Filing > Integrated Filing- Financial. In parallel, the outcome of the Board Meeting for financial results must still be filed in PDF format within the applicable prescribed timeline of 30 minutes or 3 hours, as relevant, but only through the announcement path specified in the circular: Compliance > Announcements/Corporate actions > Create announcement/corporate actions > Intimation type: Announcement > Regulation 30 – Para A > Subject – Outcome of board meeting > Type – Financial results.

A further obligation is that the Integrated Filing - Financial submission in XBRL must be made on the same date as the PDF filing of the financial results. The circular also makes clear that certain older filing methods have been discontinued effective April 1, 2025: financial results can no longer be submitted in PDF form through the NEAPS “Quick Results” tab, and the PDF filing of “Integrated Filing - Financial” through the Corporate Announcement route is also discontinued. This update applies to all listed entities on the NSE and specifically governs how they must file financial results and related board-meeting outcomes going forward.

rows.title: SEBI Circular on Amendment to Master Circular for Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) dated May 15, 2024
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is an intimation to all listed Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and “all parties to REITs” that SEBI has issued an amendment to the REIT Master Circular dated May 15, 2024. The NSE circular itself does not set out the substantive changes; it only references SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/43 dated March 28, 2025, and forwards that circular for “necessary action” by market participants. The effective date in the NSE notice is April 01, 2025, so compliance teams should treat the SEBI amendment as operative from that date unless the SEBI circular specifies a different implementation timeline.

From a compliance perspective, the key point is that this communication is directed specifically to REITs and all parties associated with REITs, meaning the amendment may affect the sponsor, manager, trustee, designated stock exchange obligations, and any other persons governed by the REIT framework. The notice does not provide any thresholds, fees, ratios, timelines, or operational requirements of its own, and it does not describe the actual regulatory edits made by SEBI. Accordingly, a corporate compliance team should review the enclosed SEBI circular and update internal REIT compliance procedures, disclosures, filings, and governance processes based on the substantive amendments contained there.

rows.title: SEBI Circular on Amendment to Master Circular for Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) dated May 15, 2024
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is a forwarding/implementation notice, not a substantive rule by itself, and it applies to **all Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) and all parties to InvITs**. The NSE states that it is issuing the notice in reference to **SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/44 dated March 28, 2025**, which is titled **“Amendment to Master Circular for Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) dated May 15, 2024.”** In other words, the operative regulatory change is contained in the SEBI circular being referenced; the NSE circular’s role is to circulate that amendment and inform market participants that they should review and take necessary action.

The document does **not** reproduce the amended provisions, so it does not itself specify the exact compliance changes, thresholds, procedural updates, or filing obligations introduced by SEBI. It also does not set out a separate compliance deadline in this notice beyond the issuance date of the NSE circular itself, which is **April 01, 2025**. From a compliance perspective, the key action item is to obtain and review the enclosed SEBI circular immediately, because any amended requirements under the InvIT Master Circular would apply to the affected InvITs and their counterparties from the effective date stated in the SEBI circular.

For a corporate compliance team, the practical takeaway is that this is a formal alert that the SEBI framework governing InvITs has been amended as of **March 28, 2025**, and the exchange expects impacted entities to ensure implementation as required. Since the NSE circular says it is “for your information” and “for necessary action at your end,” compliance teams should treat the SEBI circular as the controlling document and verify whether any internal policies, disclosures, trustee/manager processes, reporting calendars, or transaction documentation for InvITs need to be updated in response to the amendment.

rows.title: SEBI Circular on Measures to facilitate ease of doing business with respect to framework for assurance or assessment, ESG disclosures for value chain, and introduction of voluntary disclosure on green credits.
rows.summary:
SEBI has amended the sustainability/ESG compliance framework for listed entities to make it easier to implement, mainly by revising the rules on BRSR Core assurance/assessment, changing the treatment of ESG disclosures for the value chain, and creating a new voluntary disclosure regime for green credits. The change follows recommendations of SEBI’s Expert Committee for Facilitating Ease of Doing Business and a public consultation, and SEBI states that its Board approved these revisions on December 18, 2024; the operative circular is SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2025/42 dated March 28, 2025, with the NSE circular issued April 1, 2025 for dissemination to all listed entities.

For compliance purposes, the key substantive change is that listed entities now have an option to obtain either “assessment” or “assurance” in relation to BRSR Core and ESG disclosures for the value chain, rather than being limited to only one approach. The circular also revises the disclosure framework for ESG matters in the value chain, meaning entities that make or plan to make those disclosures need to follow the updated SEBI requirements and any associated methodology/verification expectations set out in the amended LODR framework. In addition, SEBI has introduced a voluntary disclosure on green credits, so entities may disclose information about green credits if they choose, but this is not framed as mandatory for all listed entities.

The circular is addressed to all listed entities and recognized stock exchanges, so the immediate practical effect is on listed companies that are subject to SEBI LODR compliance, especially those preparing BRSR Core disclosures, value-chain ESG disclosures, or considering voluntary sustainability reporting around green credits. Because the NSE notice says the SEBI circular is enclosed “for reference and necessary action,” compliance teams should treat this as an implementation update requiring review of current ESG reporting controls, assurance/assessment arrangements, and disclosure templates to align with the revised regime. The document excerpt provided does not include specific filing deadlines, numeric thresholds, or rate changes, so those details would need to be confirmed from the full enclosed SEBI circular if applicable to the entity’s reporting cycle.

rows.title: Circular for Submission of Integrated Filing- Governance
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India has revised the filing requirement for listed entities’ governance-related reporting under the Integrated Filing-Governance framework, effective for the quarter ended March 31, 2025 onward. Beginning with that quarter, the XBRL submission for Integrated Filing-Governance must be filed within **30 days from the end of the quarter**. Listed entities are required to submit **only the Integrated Filing-Governance XBRL form** in that timeframe, and the previous separate XBRL filings for **Corporate Governance** and the **Investor Grievance Report** are no longer required under the current process.

This update is issued by NSE Listing Circular Ref. No. **NSE/CML/2025/16** dated **April 01, 2025**, and it references the underlying SEBI circular dated **December 31, 2024** as well as prior NSE implementation circulars dated **January 02, 2025**, **January 13, 2025**, and **February 28, 2025**. The practical compliance change is a consolidation of governance reporting into one XBRL filing with a clear 30-day post-quarter deadline, replacing the earlier dual-reporting process. For queries, entities are directed to the NEAPS platform under **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance** or to email **takeover@nse.co.in** / **nsexbrl@nse.co.in**.

rows.title: Updates on the SEBI Circular on the Industry Standards on “Minimum information to be provided for review of the Audit Committee and Shareholders for approval of a related party transaction”
rows.summary:
This update does **not change the substance of the “minimum information” requirements** for related party transaction approvals; instead, it **extends the effective date** of the SEBI Industry Standards that govern the information to be provided to the **Audit Committee and shareholders** when seeking approval of a related party transaction. The original SEBI circular dated **February 14, 2025** had made the Industry Standards effective from **April 1, 2025**, but after receiving stakeholder feedback requesting more time, SEBI has revised the applicability date to **July 1, 2025**.

The document applies to **all listed entities** and is also addressed to **all recognized stock exchanges** and industry bodies for awareness. The practical compliance impact is that listed entities must now ensure their processes, internal templates, and approval papers for related party transactions are aligned with the Industry Standards by **July 1, 2025**, rather than April 1, 2025. No new numeric thresholds, rates, or transaction-value changes are introduced in this circular; the only specified change is the **deferral of the implementation date**.

NSE’s circular (Ref. No. **NSE/CML/2025/15**, dated **March 21, 2025**) simply communicates SEBI’s revised timeline and states that the SEBI circular dated March 21, 2025 is enclosed and available on NSE’s website for reference and necessary action. For compliance purposes, the key takeaway is to treat **July 1, 2025** as the operative date from which the Industry Standards on minimum information for audit committee/shareholder review must be followed for related party transaction approvals.

rows.title: Disclosure of holding of specified securities in dematerialized form
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated March 20, 2025 is an intimation to all listed entities that SEBI has issued a new circular, SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/35, also dated March 20, 2025, titled “Disclosure of holding of specified securities in dematerialized form.” The NSE circular itself does not set out the substantive disclosure requirements; it simply forwards the SEBI circular and directs listed entities to review it and take necessary action. The affected parties are all listed entities, i.e., companies whose securities are listed on the exchange and that are subject to SEBI/NSE disclosure obligations. The document does not state any compliance deadline, threshold, rate, or procedure in the text provided, other than noting that the SEBI circular is attached/enclosed and available on the NSE website for reference.  

For compliance purposes, the practical requirement is to obtain and follow the underlying SEBI circular because that will contain the actual obligations regarding disclosure of holding of specified securities in dematerialized form. The NSE notice confirms that the SEBI circular is effective as of March 20, 2025, but no implementation timeline is specified in the NSE covering notice itself.

rows.title: Online Filing System for reports filed under Regulation 10(7) of SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011
rows.summary:
The circular informs all listed entities that the National Stock Exchange is forwarding a SEBI circular dated March 20, 2025 introducing an **online filing system for reports submitted under Regulation 10(7) of the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011**. The immediate practical change is that companies subject to this regulation should expect the relevant reports to be filed through the new SEBI online mechanism rather than relying only on the existing non-digital process; the NSE note itself does not set out the technical filing steps, but it directs recipients to the enclosed SEBI circular for the operative requirements and for any action needed at their end.

This communication is addressed to **company secretaries of all listed entities**, so the compliance impact is broad for listed companies that have reporting obligations under **Regulation 10(7)**, which concerns filings related to acquisitions exempt under Regulation 10. No separate deadline, threshold, or fee is stated in the NSE covering circular itself. The only date specified is the **SEBI circular date of March 20, 2025**, which indicates when the new online filing arrangement was issued and became relevant for compliance planning.

The NSE also notes that the SEBI circular is available on the NSE website for reference and says the circular is being provided “for necessary action” and “for your information,” meaning compliance teams should review the SEBI circular itself to determine any procedural changes, filing format requirements, authentication steps, or transitional instructions applicable to their organization.

rows.title: Industry Standards Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on Applicability of the Industry Standards on “Minimum information to be provided for Review of the Audit Committee and Shareholders for Approval of Related Party Transaction (RPT)"
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India issued Circular NSE/CML/2025/12 on March 15, 2025 to all listed entities, enclosing new FAQs on the applicability of the industry standards for the “Minimum information to be provided for Review of the Audit Committee and Shareholders for Approval of Related Party Transaction (RPT).” This circular does not itself create new substantive RPT approval rules; rather, it directs listed entities to use the accompanying FAQs as guidance for applying the industry standards that were already introduced under NSE Circular NSE/CML/2025/05 dated February 15, 2025. The notice also makes clear that the circular and FAQs are available on the NSE website and are issued for information and necessary action by listed entities.

The underlying regulatory framework referenced is Section III-B of the SEBI Master Circular dated November 11, 2024, read with Regulations 23(2), 23(3), and 23(4) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. These provisions require listed entities to place specified information before the audit committee and, where shareholder approval is required, before shareholders for approval of related party transactions. The FAQs are intended to clarify how the industry standards should be applied when determining what information must be furnished and in what situations those standards are applicable.

From the material provided, no new monetary threshold, percentage limit, filing deadline, or effective date beyond the March 15, 2025 issuance date is stated in the circular excerpt itself. The affected entities are all listed entities governed by the NSE/SEBI LODR framework, and the practical compliance obligation is to ensure that RPT proposals brought to the audit committee or shareholders include the minimum information required under the industry standards as interpreted by the FAQs. A compliance team should therefore treat this as an interpretive update that may affect the completeness of RPT approval papers and supporting documentation, and should review the enclosed FAQs alongside the February 15, 2025 circular and the referenced SEBI provisions when preparing or vetting related party transaction approvals.

rows.title: Circular on the Regulatory Framework for Specialized Investment Funds (SIF’)
rows.summary:
SEBI has introduced a new regulatory framework for **Specialized Investment Funds (SIFs)** through Circular No. **SEBI/HO/IMD/IMD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2025/26 dated February 27, 2025**, and the NSE circular dated **March 13, 2025** simply forwards that SEBI circular to mutual funds and AMCs for information and necessary action.
