rows.title: SCORES 2.0 New Technology to strengthen SEBI Complaint Redressal System for Investors
rows.summary:
SEBI has launched **SCORES 2.0**, the upgraded investor complaint redressal platform, **effective April 1, 2024**, and the exchange is notifying all **listed companies, municipal debt securities issuers, and registrars and share transfer agents (RTAs)** that they must comply with the new process. SEBI will send the **SCORES user ID and password** to the registered **e-mail ID of the respective contact person** for each covered entity.

Under the new workflow, once a complaint is received on SCORES, the concerned listed company / municipal debt securities entity / RTA must **resolve the complaint and submit the Action Taken Report (ATR) within 21 calendar days** through SCORES. The ATR is then **automatically routed to the complainant**. If the complainant is dissatisfied, the complaint is **escalated to the Exchange for first-level review**, and the Exchange must handle that escalated complaint **within 10 calendar days**. If the investor is still not satisfied after the Exchange’s review, the investor may **escalate the matter to SEBI for a second review**.

The circular also states that if the covered entity or the relevant designated body **fails to meet the prescribed timelines**, the complaint will be **auto-escalated** under the SCORES 2.0 mechanism. The excerpt provided ends mid-sentence after referring to auto-escalation for nonadherence, so any additional consequences or procedural details are not visible here; however, the key compliance obligation is clear: entities in scope must ensure prompt complaint resolution, timely ATR filing, and readiness for escalation review under the new SCORES 2.0 process.

rows.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) – Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Extending framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level to all listed companies in a phased manner
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated **March 28, 2024** (Ref. **NSE/CML/2024/08**) forwards **FAQs** on the SEBI trading-window closure framework under **Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015**. The substantive point is that the **framework restricting trading by Designated Persons (DPs) through freezing PAN at the security level** is being **extended to all listed companies in a phased manner**. The circular reiterates that companies must continue to comply with the **PIT Regulations** and any other applicable laws as amended, and it states that the FAQs are for **guidance only** rather than creating independent legal requirements.

The most important operational change is the **expansion of the security-level PAN freeze mechanism beyond the initial group of large-cap companies**. The FAQs state that, as of the date of the circular, the mechanism applies to **NIFTY 50 / SENSEX 30 companies and the TOP 2000 companies by BSE market capitalization for the quarter ending December 2023**, and that it will be **extended to all remaining listed companies from 1 April 2024**. For compliance teams, this means the issuer must ensure its trading-window closure controls, DP restrictions, and depository-level PAN freeze process are ready for the applicable phase and aligned with the phased rollout date.

The circular references the prior NSE circulars **NSE/CML/2024/03 dated January 30, 2024**, **NSE/CML/2023/79 dated November 17, 2023**, **NSE/CML/2022/40 dated August 5, 2022**, **NSE/CML/2023/49 dated June 28, 2023**, and **NSE/CML/2023/59 dated July 31, 2023**, as well as SEBI circulars **SEBI/HO/ISD/ISD-SEC-4/P/CIR/2022/107 dated August 5, 2022** and **SEBI/HO/ISD/ISD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2023/124 dated July 19, 2023**. While the text provided only includes the first FAQ in full, the overall purpose is clear: listed entities must understand who is responsible for updating the trading-window closure period and related controls, and must use the depository/PAN-freezing framework to prevent prohibited trades by DPs during closure periods.

From a compliance standpoint, the key action item is to determine whether the company falls within the **current phase** or the **1 April 2024 expansion phase**, and then ensure internal procedures, depository instructions, and DP monitoring are updated accordingly. The circular also makes clear that listed companies are expected to follow the SEBI/NSE framework as amended from time to time; therefore, compliance officers should treat the FAQs as interpretive guidance supporting the underlying regulatory obligations, not as a substitute for the regulations themselves.

rows.title: Corporate Grouping of Listed Companies
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE), by circular NSE/CML/2024/07 dated March 27, 2024, is reaffirming and operationalizing the requirement that any listed company whose corporate group changes because of an event such as a corporate restructuring, takeover, merger, demerger, acquisition, or delisting must notify the Exchange within two working days of the effective date of that change. The key update in this circular is procedural: going forward, the intimation must be filed only through NSE’s new online module in the NEAPS application, rather than through any other route, and the circular provides the NEAPS login path and annexed procedure for making the change.

This requirement applies to all listed companies on the NSE, specifically when an event causes a change in the company’s corporate group. The Exchange emphasizes that the corporate group repository exists solely for compliance with SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/AFD/AFD–PoD–2/CIR/P/2023/148 dated August 24, 2023, and must not be treated as a legal definition or interpretation of “group,” “related party,” or “associate companies” under any other SEBI regulation, circular, or law. Companies are therefore expected to exercise caution and verify their classification before submitting the intimation, because the repository is for compliance reporting purposes only.

The practical compliance obligation is now both time-bound and system-specific: identify any corporate-group change promptly, ensure the effective date is captured correctly, and complete the filing in NEAPS within the two-working-day deadline. The circular does not introduce a new substantive threshold or rate, but it does replace any prior manual or alternate intimation process with mandatory use of the online NEAPS module for this specific disclosure.

rows.title: Repeal of circular(s) outlining procedure to deal with cases where securities are issued prior to April 01, 2014, involving offer / allotment of securities to more 49 but up to 200 investors in a financial year
rows.summary: This NSE circular dated March 14, 2024 is a forwarding notice to all listed entities informing them of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/016 dated March 13, 2024, titled “Repeal of circular(s) outlining procedure to deal with cases where securities are issued prior to April 01, 2014, involving offer / allotment of securities to more than 49 but up to 200 investors in a financial year.” The substance of the communication is that the earlier SEBI circular(s) on how to handle such legacy issuances are being repealed, meaning the prior procedural guidance for cases where securities were issued before April 1, 2014 in offerings/allotments to more than 49 but up to 200 investors in a financial year is no longer operative. The NSE circular itself does not set out a new approval process, threshold, reporting requirement, or deadline for listed entities beyond directing them to take note of the SEBI circular and ensure compliance. From a compliance perspective, this matters only to entities with historical pre-April 1, 2014 issuances falling within that investor range, and they should review the underlying SEBI circular to determine whether any legacy actions or pending matters are affected by the repeal. The circular also notes that the SEBI circular is available on the NSE website for reference.

rows.title: Revised Pricing Methodology for Institutional Placements of Privately Placed Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT)
rows.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India issued this circular on February 9, 2024 to all Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) and all parties to InvITs, directing them to take note of and comply with SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-PoD/P/CIR/2024/10 dated February 8, 2024, titled “Revised Pricing Methodology for Institutional Placements of Privately Placed Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT).” The NSE circular itself does not restate the full pricing rules; it functions as a compliance notice pointing recipients to SEBI’s underlying circular, which is available on the NSE website for reference. The material change referenced is a revised pricing methodology applicable to institutional placements of privately placed InvITs, meaning entities involved in such placements need to review the SEBI circular to determine the exact pricing requirements and adjust offering/pricing procedures accordingly. The NSE asks recipients to “ensure compliance,” so compliance teams should treat this as an immediate obligation to verify whether any ongoing or planned institutional placement transactions are affected by the revised SEBI methodology and to align internal processes with the new rule effective February 8, 2024.

rows.title: Guidelines for returning of draft offer document and its resubmission
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India has circulated SEBI’s Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/009 dated February 06, 2024, titled “Guidelines for returning of draft offer document and its resubmission.” The NSE notice itself does not spell out the detailed operational rules; it serves to alert all listed entities and all issuers proposing to list specified securities that SEBI has issued new guidelines on how draft offer documents may be returned and how they must be resubmitted. The only explicit instruction in the NSE communication is that recipients must take note of the SEBI circular and ensure compliance.

For compliance purposes, this means companies involved in an IPO, FPO, or other listing of specified securities should review the SEBI circular directly on the NSE website and align their disclosure and filing process with the new return/resubmission framework. No thresholds, procedural deadlines, or numeric requirements are described in the NSE cover notice beyond the circular date itself, so any substantive obligations, timelines, or grounds for return would be contained in the SEBI circular referenced as an enclosure. The notice is dated February 07, 2024, and the underlying SEBI circular is dated February 06, 2024.

rows.title: Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Extending framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level to all listed companies in a phased manner
rows.summary:
This circular extends SEBI’s trading-window restriction framework for Designated Persons under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 by requiring a **PAN-level freeze at the security level** for trading in the securities of listed companies. The practical effect is that when a trading window is closed for a listed company, the restriction will no longer be limited to internal company monitoring; instead, **the PAN of each Designated Person will be frozen in the relevant security across the market infrastructure**, preventing trades in that company’s securities through that PAN during the closure period. The circular states that this enhancement will be **rolled out to all listed companies in a phased manner**, so compliance teams should expect implementation in stages rather than all at once.

For affected entities, the key obligation is to ensure that their **Designated Persons** are correctly identified and linked to the appropriate PANs so that trading restrictions can operate effectively at the security level. Companies will need to align their internal trading-window closure processes with the new external freeze mechanism, including maintaining accurate and updated PAN details for DPs and ensuring that their trading-window closure communications remain timely and consistent with the period during which the freeze is expected to apply. The document’s title ties the change specifically to the existing trading-window closure regime under the PIT Regulations, meaning this is not a replacement of insider-trading restrictions but an enforcement enhancement to make those restrictions operationally binding through market-level controls.

The extracted content provided does not include readable text showing any **specific commencement date, phased rollout schedule, transitional deadline, or numeric thresholds/rates** beyond the reference to phased implementation. It also does not provide additional procedural details such as the exact exchange/depository workflow, reporting format, or exceptions, so a compliance team should treat the core requirement as: **during a trading window closure, DPs will be barred from trading in that security through a PAN freeze, and issuers must be ready for this mechanism to be activated as the rollout reaches them**.

rows.title: Framework for Offer for Sale (OFS) of Shares to Employees through Stock Exchange Mechanism
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India issued this circular on January 30, 2024 to all listed entities, informing them of a SEBI circular dated January 23, 2024 titled “Framework for Offer for Sale (OFS) of Shares to Employees through Stock Exchange Mechanism.” The NSE notice itself does not set out any substantive new operational rules, thresholds, or timelines; instead, it serves as a forwarding notice directing listed companies to the SEBI circular and stating that the updated circular is available on the NSE website for reference and necessary action.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that this is a regulatory update affecting listed entities that may conduct an OFS of shares to employees through the stock exchange mechanism. Because the notice does not describe the framework’s specific eligibility conditions, pricing, allotment, procedural steps, or deadlines, a compliance team should review the SEBI circular referenced in the notice to determine what changes apply and whether any internal policies, disclosure processes, or transaction procedures need to be updated.

rows.title: Extension of timeline for verification of market rumours by listed entities
rows.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India issued this listing circular on January 29, 2024 to all listed entities, forwarding SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2024/7 dated January 25, 2024, which extends the timeline for listed companies to verify market rumours. The NSE notice itself does not add new substantive requirements beyond referencing SEBI’s action; it serves to inform listed entities that the attached SEBI circular should be reviewed and acted on as necessary. From a compliance perspective, the key point is that the obligation concerns **all listed entities** and relates specifically to the **verification of market rumours**, so any internal disclosures, rumor-response processes, or stock-exchange communication workflows should be checked against the updated timeline in the underlying SEBI circular. The NSE circular indicates the SEBI circular is enclosed and available on the NSE website, and that listed entities should take “necessary action” at their end. No additional dates, thresholds, rates, or procedural details are set out in the NSE notice itself beyond the issuance date of January 29, 2024 and the SEBI circular date of January 25, 2024.

rows.title: Revision to the Framework on Social Stock Exchange
rows.summary:
This NSE circular does not introduce a standalone new compliance regime; it informs market participants that SEBI has revised the existing **Framework on Social Stock Exchange (SSE)** and that the Exchange previously disseminated the original SSE framework through its circular dated **September 22, 2023**. The update comes through **SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/196 dated December 28, 2023**, which states that certain **modifications/additions** have been made to the earlier SSE framework issued by SEBI on **September 19, 2022**.

The NSE circular is addressed to **all social enterprises and all listed companies**, meaning compliance teams for entities that are already listed or that may seek to be recognized as social enterprises on the SSE should treat the SEBI circular as the operative source of the changes. The document itself does **not** spell out the substantive amendments, thresholds, filing requirements, or procedural steps; it simply provides notice that the framework has been updated and encloses the SEBI circular for review and implementation.

For compliance purposes, the key action is to **review the enclosed SEBI circular immediately** and assess whether any of the modifications affect the organization’s SSE eligibility, disclosures, registration status, reporting obligations, or any other continuing compliance under the SSE framework. Because the circular states that it is issued “for your kind information and necessary compliance,” affected entities should assume the revisions are applicable as of the SEBI circular date, **December 28, 2023**, unless the enclosed SEBI text specifies a different effective date or transition period.

rows.title: Extension of timelines for providing ''choice of nomination’ in eligible demat accounts and mutual fund folios
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India’s circular (NSE/CML/2023/87, dated December 28, 2023) is an informational notice to all listed companies pointing them to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/POD-1/P/CIR/2023/193 dated December 27, 2023, titled “Extension of timelines for providing ‘choice of nomination’ in eligible demat accounts and mutual fund folios.” The NSE does not itself create new obligations in this notice; it forwards the SEBI circular for reference and necessary action, indicating the underlying compliance change comes from SEBI. The substance of the change, as described by the title and referenced SEBI circular, is an extension of the deadline for investors to provide or exercise a “choice of nomination” in eligible demat accounts and mutual fund folios.

For a compliance team, the key point is that entities involved in handling demat accounts and mutual fund folios should review the SEBI circular to identify the revised timeline and any related operational steps for nomination processing, investor communication, or recordkeeping. The document identifies the affected areas as eligible demat accounts and mutual fund folios, so compliance obligations would apply to the account/folio-level nomination process rather than to listed companies generally, except to the extent they interface with investors or service providers subject to these rules. The NSE notice itself does not specify the new extended deadline, thresholds, or procedures; it only confirms that SEBI has extended the timeline and that the circular is available on the NSE website for action as needed.

rows.title: Amendment to Circular dated July 31, 2023 on Online Resolution of Disputes in the Indian Securities Market
rows.summary:
This NSE communication is a forwarding circular to **all listed companies** on **December 20, 2023**, drawing attention to a **SEBI amendment** to the earlier **July 31, 2023 circular on online resolution of disputes in the Indian securities market**. The NSE notice itself does **not** describe any substantive new rule text or operational change; it states only that SEBI Circular **No. SEBI/HO/OIAE/OIAE_IAD-3/P/CIR/2023/191 dated December 20, 2023** has been issued and that a copy is enclosed and available on the NSE website for reference and “necessary action.”

For compliance purposes, the practical requirement here is to **review the enclosed SEBI amendment circular** and determine whether any internal dispute-resolution, grievance-handling, or investor-facing procedures need updating. However, based on the text provided, there are **no explicit deadlines, thresholds, fees, procedural steps, or new obligations stated in this NSE covering note itself** beyond the instruction to take necessary action in light of the SEBI circular. The affected population is broad—**all listed companies**—but the document provided is only an informational transmittal, not the full substantive amendment.

rows.title: Filing of Announcements pertaining to Loss of Share Certificate/Issue of Duplicate Share Certificate/Closure of Trading Window and Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (''CIRP’) in XBRL format on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform
rows.summary:
NSE has introduced a new XBRL filing requirement on the NEAPS platform for three specific Regulation 30 announcements: **loss of share certificate/issue of duplicate share certificate, closure of trading window, and corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP)**. The facility becomes available **effective December 9, 2023**, and the announcement states that, at the initial stage, **PDF filings will still be treated as compliant under Regulation 30**, but listed entities must **also submit the same filing in XBRL format within 24 hours of the PDF submission**. In other words, companies affected by any of these three events must make a dual submission during the transition period: first the normal PDF announcement, then the corresponding XBRL filing within the 24-hour window.

The circular also says that **XBRL utility access** for these subjects is available in NEAPS under **COMPLIANCE >> Common XBRL Upload >> Equity Announcement- XBRL**, with the filer selecting the relevant **“Subject of Announcement”**. NSE further notes that these three events will also be made available in **iXBRL format** for listed entities, although the document excerpt cuts off before completing the instruction; the clear compliance point is that this is part of the move toward structured digital filing. Finally, NSE states that **at a later date, to be announced separately, it will shift to XBRL-only submission**, so compliance teams should treat this as an interim dual-filing process and prepare for a future full migration away from PDF-only compliance.

rows.title: Revised framework for computation of Net Distributable Cash Flow (NDCF) by Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs).
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is only an intimation and forwarding notice, but it is important because it applies to **all Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs)** listed/covered by NSE. NSE states that SEBI issued a new circular on **December 6, 2023** titled **“Revised framework for computation of Net Distributable Cash Flow (NDCF) by Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs)”** and has enclosed that SEBI circular for reference and necessary action. The NSE circular itself does **not** set out the revised NDCF rules, formulas, thresholds, or reporting steps; instead, it directs REITs to review and implement the SEBI circular’s requirements. 

For compliance purposes, the key point is that there is now a **revised regulatory framework governing how REITs must compute NDCF**, which is the basis for distributable cash flow determinations and therefore directly affects distribution policy, calculation methodology, and any related disclosures or internal controls. The operative date in the notice is the date of the underlying SEBI circular, **December 6, 2023**, and NSE’s forwarding circular is dated **December 7, 2023**. Since no substantive terms are reproduced in the NSE notice, a compliance team should treat this as a prompt to obtain and implement the SEBI circular itself and confirm whether any updated computation, timing, approval, or reporting obligations apply to the REIT and its manager/trustee structures.

rows.title: Revised framework for computation of Net Distributable Cash Flow (NDCF) by Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs).
rows.summary:
The NSE circular dated December 7, 2023 is a forwarding notice to all Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) advising them of a SEBI circular issued one day earlier, on December 6, 2023, titled “Revised framework for computation of Net Distributable Cash Flow (NDCF) by Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs).” The NSE notice itself does not set out the revised NDCF rules in detail; instead, it states that SEBI’s December 6, 2023 circular is enclosed and should be reviewed for “necessary action” by the affected InvITs, and notes that the circular is also available on the NSE website.

From a compliance perspective, the material point is that the framework for computing NDCF for InvITs has been revised by SEBI, and the change applies to all InvITs covered by the SEBI regime. The notice does not specify any numerical thresholds, formula changes, implementation date, or compliance deadline in the text provided, so those particulars must be taken directly from the SEBI circular referenced by the NSE. The obligation conveyed here is to review the revised SEBI framework promptly and align internal NDCF computation and distribution processes accordingly.

rows.title: Extension of timeline for implementation of provisions of circular SEBI/HO/OIAE/IGRD/CIR/P/2023/156 dated September 20, 2023 on Redressal of investor grievances through the SEBI Complaint Redressal (SCORES) Platform and linking it to Online Dispute Resolution platform.
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is addressed to all listed companies and serves only to notify them of a SEBI extension, not to impose a new standalone NSE requirement. It references SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/OIAE/IGRD/CIR/P/2023/183 dated December 1, 2023, which extends the implementation timeline for the provisions of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/OIAE/IGRD/CIR/P/2023/156 dated September 20, 2023. Those underlying SEBI provisions concern the redressal of investor grievances through the SEBI Complaint Redressal (SCORES) platform and the linking of that grievance process to the Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) platform.

For compliance purposes, the material point is that the effective implementation date for the September 20, 2023 SEBI requirements has been pushed out by the December 1, 2023 SEBI circular. The NSE circular itself does not restate the new date, thresholds, or any substantive procedural details; it simply says the SEBI extension circular is enclosed for reference and necessary action, and that the circular is also available on the NSE website. Accordingly, listed companies should review the SEBI circular dated December 1, 2023 to determine the revised compliance timeline and any actions required for SCORES/ODR integration and grievance-handling processes.

rows.title: Simplified norms for processing investor’s service requests by RTAs and norms for furnishing PAN, KYC details and Nomination
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is a forwarding notice to **all listed companies** informing them of a new **SEBI circular dated November 17, 2023** (SEBI/HO/MIRSD/POD-1/P/CIR/2023/181) titled **“Simplified norms for processing investor’s service requests by RTAs and norms for furnishing PAN, KYC details and Nomination.”** The NSE letter itself does not set out the detailed compliance rules, but it makes clear that the underlying SEBI circular is attached and is issued for **necessary action** by recipients, meaning listed companies should review and implement the requirements in that SEBI circular as applicable to their investor servicing and shareholding records processes.

For compliance purposes, the material point in this document is the **triggering of new/updated obligations around how RTAs process investor service requests and how PAN, KYC, and nomination information must be furnished**. No monetary thresholds, fees, or numeric limits are stated in the NSE covering letter, and no separate effective date is specified in the NSE communication beyond the **November 17, 2023** SEBI circular date and the **November 20, 2023** NSE circulation date. The notice applies to entities that are **listed on NSE** and therefore should ensure coordination with their **registrar and transfer agent (RTA)** and internal shareholder servicing teams so that any revised procedural, documentation, or reporting requirements in the SEBI circular are followed. The document also points recipients to the NSE website where the SEBI circular is available for reference.

rows.title: Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Extending framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level to all listed companies in a phased manner - Next 1,000 companies in terms of BSE Market Capitalization as of June 30, 2023 for PIT - Trading Window Closure Period
rows.summary:
This SEBI communication extends the “trading window closure period” framework under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 to additional listed companies by requiring trading restrictions to be enforced through freezing of PAN at the security level. It is specifically directed at the next 1,000 listed companies, ranked by BSE market capitalization as of June 30, 2023, and these companies are to be brought into the framework in a phased manner. For companies covered by this rollout, Designated Persons (“DPs”) will be prevented from trading in the relevant securities during trading window closure periods because the PAN-based restriction will block transactions at the security level rather than relying only on internal controls.

The document’s practical compliance effect is that affected listed entities must ensure their systems and market-intermediary coordination support this PAN-freeze mechanism for DPs during closure periods, so trading cannot occur in violation of PIT restrictions. Because the instruction is tied to the trading window closure regime, the obligation is not a new general prohibition on trading at all times, but a technical and procedural reinforcement of the existing insider-trading blackout mechanism. The key applicability trigger is the company’s position among the next 1,000 companies by BSE market capitalization on June 30, 2023, and compliance teams should treat the notice as a phased implementation requirement for those issuers rather than a universal rule for all listed companies at once. No specific monetary thresholds, penalty rates, or separate filing deadlines are stated in the text provided beyond the June 30, 2023 reference date used to identify the rollout cohort.

rows.title: Procedural framework for dealing with unclaimed amounts lying with Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) and manner of claiming such amounts by unitholders
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated **November 09, 2023** does not itself introduce new substantive requirements; it **notifies all Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs)** that SEBI has issued a binding circular on **November 08, 2023** titled **“Procedural framework for dealing with unclaimed amounts lying with Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) and manner of claiming such amounts by unitholders.”** The NSE letter is a forwarding/administrative communication that encloses the SEBI circular and directs InvITs to take “necessary action” in line with that SEBI framework.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that **InvITs are now subject to a formal procedural framework for identifying, handling, and ultimately enabling claims of unclaimed amounts held by the InvIT**, and unitholders have a specified manner for making claims. The document provided here does **not reproduce the operative details** of SEBI’s framework, so it does not state the exact definition of “unclaimed amounts,” the holding period before transfer/escalation, the account or fund destination, or the step-by-step claim process; those details would need to be read from the enclosed SEBI circular itself. No specific monetary threshold, rate, or deadline is stated in the NSE covering letter beyond the **SEBI circular date of November 08, 2023** and the NSE notification date of **November 09, 2023**.

In practical compliance terms, any InvIT receiving this notice should review the SEBI circular immediately, determine whether it holds any unclaimed distributions or other payable amounts, and implement whatever tracking, disclosure, transfer, and unitholder-claim procedures SEBI has mandated. Because the NSE letter expressly references the SEBI circular and says it is enclosed “for necessary action,” the obligation is to comply with the SEBI framework, not merely acknowledge receipt.

rows.title: Procedural framework for dealing with unclaimed amounts lying with Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and manner of claiming such amounts by unitholders.
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated **November 9, 2023** is addressed to **all Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs)** and simply forwards SEBI’s underlying circular **SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-RAC-1/P/CIR/2023/177 dated November 8, 2023** on the **“Procedural framework for dealing with unclaimed amounts lying with REITs and manner of claiming such amounts by unitholders.”** The NSE notice itself does **not** set out the substantive requirements; it directs REITs to refer to the attached SEBI circular and take **necessary action** in accordance with that framework.  

From a compliance perspective, the key point is that **REITs are the affected entities**, and the subject matter concerns **unclaimed amounts held by REITs and the process unitholders must follow to claim them**. The circular indicates that a formal procedural framework now applies, so REIT compliance teams should review the SEBI circular, identify what balances may be treated as unclaimed, and ensure internal processes are aligned with the prescribed claim-handling mechanism. No thresholds, monetary limits, deadlines, or implementation dates beyond the **SEBI circular date of November 8, 2023** and the **NSE forwarding date of November 9, 2023** are specified in the text provided.

rows.title: Revision in manner of achieving minimum public unitholding requirement – Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs)
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is a forwarding notice to all Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs), issued by the National Stock Exchange of India on November 1, 2023, referencing SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2023/174 dated October 31, 2023. The NSE note itself does not set out the substantive rule changes; it informs InvITs that SEBI has issued a circular titled “Revision in manner of achieving minimum public unitholding requirement – Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs)” and encloses that SEBI circular for review and “necessary action” by the recipients.

For compliance purposes, the affected entities are all InvITs listed or otherwise subject to the minimum public unitholding regime. The key action item is to review the underlying SEBI circular and align any ongoing or planned compliance steps with the revised method for meeting the minimum public unitholding requirement. The NSE notice does not state the revised thresholds, timelines, mechanics, or exemptions itself, so those operative details must be taken from the SEBI circular dated October 31, 2023. The circular is also available on the NSE website for reference.

rows.title: Ease of doing business and development of corporate bond markets – revision in the framework for fund raising by issuance of debt securities by large corporates (LCs).
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is primarily an intimation to listed entities other than scheduled commercial banks that SEBI has issued a new circular on October 19, 2023 revising the framework for fund raising by issuance of debt securities by large corporates (LCs). The NSE letter itself does not create separate substantive requirements; instead, it forwards SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-RACPOD1/P/CIR/2023/172 and asks recipients to take necessary action, with the circular also available on the NSE website.  

For compliance purposes, the important point is that the referenced SEBI circular changes the corporate bond / debt securities fundraising framework for “large corporates,” so any listed entity that may qualify as an LC should review the SEBI circular in detail and assess whether its debt issuance and disclosure/compliance processes need to be updated. However, this NSE communication does not state the revised LC criteria, thresholds, reporting obligations, timelines, or procedural changes itself; it only identifies the issuer, date, subject matter, and the population potentially affected.  

The document is dated October 20, 2023, and it is addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed entities other than scheduled commercial banks. No filing deadline, transition date, or specific compliance cutoff appears in this NSE covering letter.

rows.title: Mandatory Filing of Voting Results in XBRL Mode
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India Limited issued Circular NSE/CML/2023/74 on October 17, 2023, addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed entities, stating that under Regulation 44(3) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, listed entities must submit voting results for a general meeting within two working days of the meeting’s conclusion in the format specified by SEBI. The key change is that NSE is discontinuing the PDF reporting format for voting-result submissions and will accept compliance only through XBRL going forward.  

The prescribed XBRL voting-results template is available in NEAPS under “Compliance > Event Based Compliances > Voting Result,” and the actual submission path for listed entities is “NEAPS > Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Voting Results.” This requirement becomes mandatory for all listed entities effective November 01, 2023.  

From that date onward, filing the voting results in XBRL will be treated as the only valid compliance under Regulation 44(3); no other filing format, including PDF, will count as compliant. Listed entities therefore need to ensure their internal reporting and filing process is updated so voting results are uploaded only in XBRL mode within the required two-working-day deadline. For filing issues or concerns, NSE directs entities to contact takeover@nse.co.in or use the contact details available on the NEAPS platform.

rows.title: Relaxation from compliance with certain provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 – Reg.
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is an informational communication to **all listed entities with specified securities listed**. It does not itself impose a new substantive requirement; rather, it points recipients to **SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2023/167 dated October 07, 2023**, which grants a **relaxation from compliance with certain provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (LODR)**.

For compliance purposes, the key takeaway from the NSE notice is that the **SEBI circular is the operative document** and has been circulated by NSE for review and necessary action. The NSE letter states that a copy of the SEBI circular is enclosed and also available on the NSE website, indicating that listed entities should consult the SEBI-issued document directly to determine **which specific LODR provisions were relaxed, the scope of the relaxation, and any conditions or timelines attached to it**. The NSE circular itself is dated **October 09, 2023**, and it is addressed to the **Company Secretary** of listed entities, signaling that internal compliance/legal teams should assess applicability promptly.

Because the text provided does **not reproduce the substance of the SEBI relaxation**, it does not specify in this notice alone **which exact filings, disclosures, approvals, or obligations are deferred or waived**, nor does it state any numerical thresholds, exemptions, or amended deadlines. A compliance officer should therefore treat this as a **prompt to review the enclosed SEBI circular immediately** and update internal compliance calendars and reporting obligations based on the precise relief granted there.

rows.title: Centralized mechanism for reporting the demise of an investor through KRAs.
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India is notifying all listed entities of a SEBI circular dated **October 03, 2023** titled **“Centralized mechanism for reporting the demise of an investor through KRAs.”** This NSE communication itself does not set out the operational rules; rather, it directs listed entities to review and take necessary action in line with the underlying **SEBI circular No. SEBI/HO/OIAE/OIAE_IAD-1/P/CIR/2023/0000000163**. The subject matter is a **centralized reporting mechanism** for notifying the death of an investor through **KRAs (KYC Registration Agencies)**, which implies that entities handling investor records and KYC-related processes may need to align their internal procedures with the KRA-based reporting framework.

From a compliance perspective, the key action point is that listed entities should obtain and implement the requirements contained in the SEBI circular, as the NSE states the circular has been enclosed for “necessary action” and is also available on its website. The NSE letter is dated **October 04, 2023** and is addressed to **all listed entities**, so any company with listed securities should treat this as relevant unless SEBI’s underlying circular expressly limits applicability. No monetary thresholds, fees, or numerical limits are stated in the NSE covering circular itself, and no separate deadline beyond the October 03/04, 2023 circular dates is specified here. The practical compliance obligation is to ensure investor-death reporting processes are updated to use the centralized KRA mechanism described by SEBI, and to check the attached SEBI circular for the exact procedural requirements.

rows.title: Extension of timeline for verification of market rumours by listed entities
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India circulated SEBI’s September 30, 2023 circular extending the timeline for verification of market rumours by listed entities. This notice is addressed to all listed entities and is informational in tone, but it signals that listed companies should take note of the updated SEBI requirement and comply with it as necessary. The NSE circular itself does not restate the operative rule changes, deadlines, or thresholds; it simply forwards SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/162 dated September 30, 2023, and says a copy is enclosed and available on the NSE website for reference and necessary action.

From a compliance perspective, the key point is that the rule on verification of market rumours has been given an extended timeline by SEBI, and the change applies to listed entities. The circular was issued by NSE on October 04, 2023, and compliance teams should review the underlying SEBI circular to identify the exact revised response period and any associated obligations for confirming or denying rumours. Because this NSE communication contains no additional implementation instructions beyond forwarding the SEBI text, any concrete procedural requirement would need to be taken from the SEBI circular itself rather than from this NSE cover notice.

rows.title: Revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) on application filed under Regulation 37 and 59A of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 w.r.t. Scheme of Arrangements.
rows.summary:
The circular dated **September 29, 2023** (NSE/CML/2023/70) revises the **Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)** for listed entities that file a **draft Scheme of Arrangement** with stock exchanges seeking **NOC/observation under Regulation 37 and Regulation 59A of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**. The revised SOP applies to **all listed companies** submitting such applications and is to be followed in addition to the requirements of the **SEBI Master Circular dated June 20, 2023** and the **SEBI operational circular dated July 29, 2022** (updated December 1, 2022), as amended.

A key procedural change is that the **Scheme of Arrangement application must be filed with the exchange within 15 working days of the board meeting approving the draft scheme**, and it must include **all documents required under the Exchange checklist**. If the company misses that 15-working-day window, it cannot simply file the same package later; it must obtain **fresh board approval**, based on **fresh financial statements, a fresh valuation report, and other updated inputs**.

The circular also tightens the financial-documentation requirements for schemes involving **unlisted companies**. At the time of filing under Regulation 37/59A, the listed entity must submit the **audited financials for the last 3 financial years** of the unlisted company(ies) involved, and those financials must be **not older than 6 months**, consistent with the cited SEBI circular provisions. In addition, the **audited financials used for the valuation report must not be older than 3 months** as of the relevant date; this means the valuation must be based on very recent audited numbers rather than stale data.

For compliance purposes, the practical effect is that companies planning restructurings, mergers, demergers, or other arrangements under these regulations need to coordinate **board approval, financial close, valuation, and exchange filing timelines tightly**, because delays trigger a requirement to restart the approval process with updated materials. The circular is therefore not just advisory; it imposes a **mandatory filing timeline and recency standards for financial statements and valuation inputs** that listed entities must satisfy before the exchange will process the scheme application.

rows.title: Format of Cyber Security Incidence Disclosure under Corporate Governance Report
rows.summary:
SEBI has amended the Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations, 2015 by inserting Regulation 27(2)(ba) through Notification No. SEBI/LAD-NRO/GN/2023/131 dated June 14, 2023. This new provision requires listed entities to disclose, in the Corporate Governance Report, whether they had any cyber security incidents, cyber security breaches, or loss of data/documents during the quarter, and to submit that disclosure to the stock exchanges on a quarterly basis. The requirement became effective from July 14, 2023.

To operationalize this obligation, the National Stock Exchange has added new fields to the existing Corporate Governance Report XBRL utility. The added disclosure fields require the company to state: whether there were any cyber security incidents/breaches/loss of data or documents during the quarter under Regulation 27(2)(ba) (Yes/No), the date of the event, and brief details of the event. These utility changes take effect for the quarter ended September 30, 2023 and for all subsequent quarters, so listed entities should ensure their quarterly corporate governance reporting processes capture and validate this information going forward.

rows.title: Filing of Related Party Transactions disclosure on NEAPS Portal
rows.summary:
This NSE circular, dated September 29, 2023 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2023/68), instructs all listed entities to change how they file the six-monthly Related Party Transactions (RPT) disclosure required under Regulation 23(9) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. The disclosure must still be made every six months, on the same date that the company publishes its standalone and consolidated financial results, but the Exchange now requires that the filing be submitted **only in XBRL format** through **NEAPS > Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Related Party Transactions**.

The circular explicitly states that the XBRL filing is the **only** filing method that will be treated as compliant under Regulation 23(9). Any other format, **including PDF**, will **not** be considered compliance. NSE also notes that the XBRL utility for preparing the disclosure in the prescribed format is available on the same NEAPS path, and listed entities should use that utility to complete the submission.

For compliance teams, the key operational change is that RPT disclosure filings must be routed through the NEAPS XBRL upload workflow rather than being submitted in parallel or alternative formats. If there are filing issues or questions, the Exchange directs listed entities to contact **nsexbrl@nse.co.in** or use the contact details available on the NEAPS platform.

rows.title: Extension of timelines (i) for nomination in eligible demat accounts and (ii) for submission of PAN, Nomination and KYC details by physical security holders; and voluntary nomination for trading accounts
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India circular dated September 27, 2023 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2023/67) is a transmittal notice to all listed entities, informing them of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/POD-1/P/CIR/2023/158 dated September 26, 2023. The NSE circular itself does not create new substantive requirements; it forwards the SEBI circular for information and “necessary action,” and notes that the SEBI circular is available on the NSE website.

For a compliance team, the key point is that SEBI has extended the timelines relating to two compliance matters for investors/security holders: (1) nomination in eligible demat accounts, and (2) submission of PAN, nomination, and KYC details by physical security holders. The SEBI circular also addresses voluntary nomination for trading accounts. However, the NSE notice provided here does not state the new deadline dates or the exact extended timeline; it only confirms that the timelines have been extended and directs recipients to the SEBI circular for the operative details.

Accordingly, listed entities should review the referenced SEBI circular immediately to identify the revised compliance dates and any required operational changes, especially if they maintain investor servicing, registrar/transfer agent coordination, or communications around demat, physical holding, or trading account nomination/KYC compliance. The notice was issued on September 27, 2023 and is marked as informational, but it indicates that action may be required at the entity level based on SEBI’s underlying directive.

rows.title: Redressal of investor grievances through the SEBI Complaint Redressal (SCORES) Platform and linking it to Online Dispute Resolution platform.
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is a transmission notice telling all listed entities that SEBI has issued Circular No. SEBI/HO/OIAE/IGRD/CIR/P/2023/156 dated September 20, 2023, on the redressal of investor grievances through the SEBI Complaint Redressal (SCORES) platform and its linkage to the Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) platform. The NSE circular itself does not create separate substantive obligations; it serves to notify listed entities, through their Company Secretaries, that the SEBI circular is enclosed and must be acted upon as applicable. It applies to all listed entities and concerns how investor complaints are to be handled through SCORES and connected into the ODR process.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that SEBI’s September 20, 2023 circular is the operative document that may impose new complaint-handling and escalation procedures, and listed entities should review and implement those requirements promptly. No deadlines, thresholds, or rate changes are stated in the NSE covering circular itself, and no specific procedural details are reproduced in the text provided beyond the subject matter of grievance redressal via SCORES and linkage to ODR. The NSE notes that the SEBI circular is available on its website and has been circulated “for necessary action” by the listed entity.

rows.title: Change in Mode of Payment w.r.t. SEBI Investor Protection and Education Fund Bank A/c
rows.summary:
This NSE listing circular is a forwarding notice to all listed entities informing them of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/GSD/TAD/P/CIR/2023/149 dated September 4, 2023, titled “Change in Mode of Payment w.r.t. SEBI Investor Protection and Education Fund Bank A/c.” The NSE circular itself does not set out substantive compliance instructions; instead, it advises listed companies that SEBI has issued the underlying direction and that a copy of that SEBI circular is enclosed and also available on the NSE website for review and necessary action.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the change relates to the mode of payment for transactions connected with the SEBI Investor Protection and Education Fund bank account. No specific deadline, threshold, rate, or operational procedure is stated in the NSE notice itself, and it does not identify a subset of listed entities as excluded; the communication is addressed broadly to “all listed entities.” Companies should therefore review the referenced SEBI circular directly to determine the exact payment-mode change and any required updates to their internal processes, treasury handling, or reporting obligations.

rows.title: Mandating additional disclosures by Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) that fulfil certain objective criteria
rows.summary:
This NSE listing circular, dated September 1, 2023, does not itself impose the detailed disclosure rules; rather, it forwards SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/AFD/AFD–PoD–2/CIR/P/2023/148 dated August 24, 2023 and instructs all listed entities to take note of it and act as necessary. The subject of the underlying SEBI action is “mandating additional disclosures by Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) that fulfil certain objective criteria,” so the compliance impact is on FPIs that meet those criteria and, indirectly, on listed entities that may receive or rely on such shareholding/disclosure information.

From the text provided, the circular does not spell out the objective criteria, the exact additional disclosure items, thresholds, or filing mechanics; it only signals that SEBI has issued a separate circular requiring those disclosures. No specific effective date, grace period, or deadline is stated in the NSE covering letter itself. For compliance purposes, the key action is to review the attached SEBI circular dated August 24, 2023 and determine whether any FPI investment in the company, or any FPI-related shareholder reporting, is subject to the new disclosure obligations. The NSE circular also indicates the SEBI circular is available on the NSE website for reference and necessary action by listed entities.

rows.title: Filing of Abridged Prospectus of Public Issues in XBRL format
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India has introduced a new filing requirement for public issues: the Abridged Prospectus must now be filed in XBRL format through the NSE online portal at https://neaps.nseindia.com/NEWLISTINGCORP/. This is a continuation of the earlier SEBI-driven process for issue-related disclosures, following the Exchange’s prior introduction of Issue Summary Document (ISD) filing and issue advertisement dissemination under SEBI Circular dated February 15, 2023, and the Exchange notice dated February 16, 2023.

The new obligation applies to Merchant Bankers and Issuers involved in Public Issues, specifically public issues of equity shares. They must file the Abridged Prospectus of the issue in the SEBI-prescribed format under SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/SSEP/CIR/P/2022/14 dated February 04, 2022, but now in structured XBRL form, and this filing must be completed before the issue opens. The circular states that this XBRL filing requirement applies to all such public issues opening on or after September 01, 2023.

From a compliance perspective, this means issuers and their merchant bankers need to ensure the abridged prospectus is prepared and uploaded in XBRL format as part of the pre-opening issue workflow, rather than treating it as a later-stage or optional disclosure. The stated purpose is to improve structured data availability for stakeholders such as researchers, policy makers, market analysts, and other market participants. The circular does not specify any fee, threshold, or exception; it is a blanket procedural requirement for the covered public issues. rows.summary:
This document extends SEBI’s insider-trading trading-window control framework by requiring listed companies to restrict trading by Designated Persons by freezing PAN at the security level, rather than relying only on a broader entity-level restriction. In practical terms, if a Designated Person’s PAN is frozen for a particular security, the person will be blocked from trading that security during the trading window closure period, which is meant to make insider-trading controls more effective and harder to bypass across accounts or intermediaries.

The change is being rolled out to all listed companies in a phased manner, so compliance teams should expect implementation to expand over time rather than as a single immediate switch for everyone. The document is tied to Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, meaning it sits within the existing framework governing trading-window closure and insider-trading controls for Designated Persons. The key compliance obligation is to align internal controls and broker/depository processes so that PAN-level freezes can be applied at the security level for the relevant trading-window closure periods.

A compliance officer should treat this as requiring coordination between the company, its compliance function, brokers, and depositories to ensure the freeze mechanism is operational for all affected DPs and securities. Because the measure is being introduced across listed companies in phases, firms should monitor the applicable rollout date or SEBI/market-utility implementation timetable for when the requirement becomes mandatory for their entity and ensure procedures are updated before that date.

The purpose is to improve transparency and ensure timely disclosure of material events and information, and the circular specifically directs companies to follow the revised filing approach when an event arises from a board meeting decision.

For any event that emanates from a board of directors meeting, the listed entity must first file the disclosure in PDF format under the subject line “Outcome of Board Meeting.” If the relevant event is not already available in the existing drop-down options, the filer must select “Others” in the Type field and then update the announcement text to accurately describe the event’s subject. The disclosure must also include the start and end time of the board meeting.

The circular adds a mandatory data point for all Regulation 30 PDF filings: the date and time of occurrence of the event or information must be stated in the PDF disclosure itself. In addition, if the disclosure is being submitted late, the company must explicitly mention the reason for the delay in the PDF filing. These requirements apply to all listed entities filing under Regulation 30, not just board-meeting outcomes, and are meant to standardize filings and reduce ambiguity about timing and late reporting.

rows.title: Master Circular for Listed Entities
rows.summary:
This SEBI master circular for listed entities implements amendments to the annual audit-report filing requirements for entities submitting audited financial results. It distinguishes between entities whose audit reports have **unmodified opinions** and those with **modified opinions** for the financial year ended **March 31, 2016**, and then changes the continuing filing regime for all later annual filings.

For listed entities that had **already filed Form A** for the year ended March 31, 2016 in cases of **unmodified audit opinions**, SEBI treats that filing as **sufficient compliance** with the amended requirements. Listed entities that **had not filed Form A** for that same period must submit the declaration referenced in **SEBI Circular CIR/CFD/CMD/56/2016** **within 30 days from the date of this circular**, and it must be signed by the **CEO, Managing Director, CFO, or Audit Committee Chairman**.

For listed entities with **modified audit opinions** for the year ended March 31, 2016, SEBI requires submission of a **“Statement on Impact of Audit Qualifications”** **within 60 days from the date of this circular**, in the format provided in **Annexure I**. This obligation applies **regardless of whether Form B had already been submitted**. The annexure specifies that this statement is to be filed **along with the annual audited financial results**, and it must be prepared **separately for standalone and consolidated financial statements**.

For **all subsequent annual filings of audited financial results**, SEBI says the earlier requirement to submit **Form A/Form B will be discontinued**. Going forward, all listed entities must instead submit either the **declaration for unmodified opinions** or the **Statement on Impact of Audit Qualifications for modified opinions**, in the prescribed Annexure I format, **within the same timeline applicable for filing annual audited financial results**. In other words, compliance officers should update annual reporting procedures so that the required statement or declaration is embedded in the audited-results filing process rather than treating Form A/Form B as a separate recurring submission.

rows.title: Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level
rows.summary:
This circular introduces a framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) during trading window closure periods under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. The key change is that listed entities are now required to implement a mechanism to **freeze PAN at the security level** so that when a trading window is closed for a specific security, DPs cannot trade in that security through any broker or demat account linked to their PAN.

Operationally, the framework requires the listed entity to identify its DPs, map their PAN to their demat holdings across depositories, and ensure that the PAN is “frozen” for the relevant security during the closure period. This is intended to prevent circumvention of the trading window restrictions by using multiple accounts or brokers. The restriction applies specifically to **DPs** and is tied to **individual securities** subject to the trading window closure, not a blanket restriction on all trading by the person in all securities unless the entity has independently imposed one.

Compliance officers should note that this is a systems-and-process obligation, not merely a policy statement: the entity must coordinate with market infrastructure / depository participants / brokers as needed to operationalize the freeze, monitor that the restriction is effective, and ensure that the PAN-level security freeze is lifted when the trading window reopens. The document is framed as a control to enforce existing insider trading restrictions under the PIT Regulations, so entities should align internal insider-trading policies, DP identification, and trade-pre-clearance/monitoring procedures with this freeze mechanism. The only explicit timing in the title/content is that the freeze is applicable **during the trading window closure period** under the PIT Regulations; no separate numerical threshold, rate, or monetary limit is set in the provided text.
