rows.summary:
This circular from NSE’s Listing Department, dated **June 21, 2023** and addressed to **the Company Secretary / Resolution Professional of all listed companies**, seeks comments and feedback on a proposed change to the reporting format for **announcements relating to Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP)**. The key proposal is to **migrate CIRP-related corporate announcements from PDF to XBRL (eXtensible Business Reporting Language)**, with the stated goal of standardizing securities market data and creating homogeneous compliance data structures that are easier for stock exchanges to analyze and for listed entities to comply with.

The circular explains that listed entities already have a general obligation to make disclosures to stock exchanges within prescribed timelines under the **SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (SEBI LODR)** and related provisions, circulars, and guidance notes, as amended from time to time. It notes that XBRL reporting has been mandated for financial filings since **2015** and that stock exchanges have been progressively converting other SEBI LODR and SEBI-related compliance filings from PDF to XBRL. In this case, the document says that **announcements pertaining to CIRP would be required to be filed exclusively in XBRL**, and that the relevant filing formats are provided in the **Annexure**.

From a compliance perspective, the practical implication is that **listed entities undergoing CIRP, and the relevant personnel responsible for insolvency/disclosure filings, should prepare for XBRL-only submission of CIRP announcements once the proposal is implemented**, rather than continuing to rely on PDF uploads. The document itself is a **consultation/feedback circular**, so it is not yet the final operative rule in the text provided; however, it clearly signals the direction of compliance change and the expected filing mechanism. No specific monetary thresholds, numeric filing deadlines, or transition date are set out in the excerpt provided, but the circular makes clear that the new XBRL format is intended to apply to the relevant CIRP announcement disclosures required under SEBI LODR and associated requirements.

rows.title: Circular for Seeking of comments, feedback on the XBRL for Loss of Share Certificate/Issue of Duplicate Share Certificate and Closure of Trading Window
rows.summary:
NSE is seeking comments and feedback on a proposed move from PDF to XBRL-only filing for two specific corporate announcements: **loss of share certificate / issue of duplicate share certificate** and **closure of trading window**. The proposal applies to **all listed entities** that must make disclosures under the **SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (SEBI LODR)** and/or the **SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (SEBI PIT)**, as amended from time to time, and any other applicable laws. If implemented, these announcements would no longer be submitted in PDF; they would have to be filed **exclusively in XBRL format**.

The circular explains that listed entities are already required to make disclosures to stock exchanges within the prescribed timelines under SEBI LODR and SEBI PIT, and that XBRL has been used for financial filings since 2015. NSE and the other stock exchanges have been progressively shifting disclosure filings from PDF to XBRL to standardize market data and create uniform, machine-readable compliance records. The stated operational effect is that this migration should reduce compliance burden over time while improving the ability of exchanges and regulators to analyze filed data.

For compliance teams, the key takeaway is that this is a **consultation/feedback circular**, not a final implementation notice in the text provided. The document does **not** state an effective date, deadline for comments, or a go-live date for mandatory XBRL filing in the excerpt given. However, it clearly signals that listed entities should prepare for a future requirement to submit these two categories of announcements in XBRL rather than PDF, with the same underlying SEBI filing obligations and timelines continuing to apply.

rows.title: Filing of Annual Secretarial Compliance Report (ASCR) in XBRL format on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has announced that listed entities must file the Annual Secretarial Compliance Report (ASCR) required under Regulation 24A of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 in **XBRL format** through the **NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS)**. This filing facility becomes **available effective June 15, 2023**, so entities should use the NEAPS XBRL workflow for ASCR submissions from that date onward. The circular specifically notes that this update follows earlier NSE circulars **NSE/CML/2023/21 dated March 16, 2023** and **NSE/CML/2023/30 dated April 10, 2023**.

For the **financial year ended March 31, 2023**, the **deadline to submit the Secretarial Compliance Report in XBRL format is June 30, 2023**. The submission process requires the listed entity to log in to the NEAPS portal, navigate to **COMPLIANCE > Common XBRL Upload**, choose **Secretarial Compliance Report** under the Module dropdown, download the offline Excel utility, complete it, and generate the XML file. After XML generation, the filer must enter the required details on the portal, attach the **PDF version of the SCR**, and then click **“Upload XBRL File”** to finish the filing.

This requirement applies to **all listed entities** that are subject to SEBI LODR Regulation 24A secretarial compliance reporting. The circular also provides a contact point for questions: the **Secretarial Compliance team at nsexbrl@nse.co.in**, or the contact details available in **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us**.

rows.title: Online processing of investor service requests and complaints by RTAs
rows.summary: This NSE circular is a forwarding notice to all listed companies, informing them of a new SEBI circular dated June 8, 2023 (SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/72) on “Online processing of investor service requests and complaints by RTAs.” The NSE letter itself does not set out the detailed requirements, thresholds, or timelines; it states that the SEBI circular is enclosed and should be reviewed for necessary action. In practical terms, the compliance obligation for listed companies is to take note of the SEBI requirements governing how Registrars and Transfer Agents (RTAs) must handle investor service requests and complaints online, and to implement any related coordination, oversight, or operational changes that may flow through to the issuer. No new effective date, deadline, fee, or numeric threshold is specified in the NSE communication itself; the operative details are contained in the referenced SEBI circular. The circular is addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed companies and is for information and necessary action, with the SEBI circular also made available on the NSE website.

rows.title: Model Tripartite Agreement between the Issuer Company, Existing Share Transfer Agent and New Share Transfer Agent as per Regulation 7(4) of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulation, 2015
rows.summary:
The NSE’s circular dated May 26, 2023 informs all listed companies of a SEBI circular issued on May 25, 2023 concerning a **model tripartite agreement** to be used among the **issuer company, the existing share transfer agent (STA), and the new STA** under **Regulation 7(4) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015**. The notice itself does not create new substantive requirements beyond flagging that SEBI has issued the model agreement and that listed companies should take the “necessary action” required under that SEBI circular.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that this communication applies to **listed companies**, particularly where there is a **change from one share transfer agent to another**, and it is intended to standardize the contractual transition arrangement among the issuer and both STAs. No deadlines, monetary thresholds, or procedural details are set out in the NSE covering note itself, but the circular directs recipients to the attached SEBI circular for the operative requirements and says the circular is available on the NSE website. Compliance teams should therefore review the SEBI circular and, if a transfer-agent change is contemplated or underway, ensure the tripartite agreement used matches SEBI’s prescribed model.

rows.title: Dematerialization of securities of Hold Cos and SPVs held by Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs)
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is an informational transmission of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2023/76 dated May 22, 2023, issued on May 23, 2023 under the title “Dematerialization of securities of Hold Cos and SPVs held by Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs).” The NSE addresses it to the Company Secretary of all listed InvITs and to all parties to REITs and InvITs, and says the SEBI circular is enclosed for reference and necessary action. In substance, the operative change is that securities of holding companies (Hold Cos) and special purpose vehicles (SPVs) held by InvITs are subject to dematerialization, meaning these securities must be held in demat form rather than in physical form, and compliance teams at affected InvITs/Hold Cos/SPVs should review and implement the SEBI directions accordingly.  

The NSE notice itself does not restate the detailed mechanics, timelines, thresholds, or procedural steps from SEBI’s circular; it simply directs recipients to the underlying SEBI circular for the exact requirements and notes that the circular is also available on the NSE website. No separate deadline, numerical threshold, or reporting date is specified in this NSE cover circular, so the compliance obligation comes from the SEBI circular referenced in it. A corporate compliance team should therefore treat this as a notice that a new dematerialization requirement applies to the relevant InvIT-related securities and should obtain and follow the SEBI circular’s detailed implementation instructions.

rows.title: Dematerialization of securities of Hold Cos and SPVs held by Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs)
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated May 23, 2023 transmits SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2023/75 dated May 22, 2023, titled “Dematerialization of securities of Hold Cos and SPVs held by Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs).” The exchange is notifying all listed REITs, and all parties to REITs and InvITs, that SEBI has issued instructions requiring action on this subject; however, the NSE text itself does not restate the operative requirements, thresholds, or deadlines from the SEBI circular, and instead directs recipients to refer to the enclosed SEBI circular for necessary action.

For compliance purposes, the material point is that this is a regulatory communication affecting listed REITs and their related parties, and it signals that dematerialization of securities held in Hold Cos and SPVs is now a matter requiring compliance attention. The notice also makes clear that the SEBI circular is available through the NSE website and that recipients are expected to review and implement whatever procedures the SEBI circular requires. Since the NSE letter does not include the substantive rule text, a compliance team should obtain and review the SEBI circular itself to identify the exact dematerialization obligations, implementation timeline, and any procedural steps or reporting requirements.

rows.title: FAQ’s on filing of announcements in XBRL format on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform.
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is not a new substantive regulation, but an implementation guidance document for listed companies on how to file certain corporate announcements in XBRL format through the NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS). It follows up on NSE/CML/2023/28 dated March 31, 2023 and provides FAQs to help companies comply with the new filing workflow for specified equity announcements.

The filing requirement applies to listed companies submitting disclosures under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (LODR) framework for the following subject matters: issuance or forfeiture of securities; split or consolidation of shares; buyback of securities; restrictions on transferability of securities; alteration in the terms or structure of existing securities, including forfeiture, reissue of forfeited securities, alteration of calls, and redemption of securities; certain binding agreements that are not in the ordinary course of business, including shareholder agreements, joint venture agreements, family settlement agreements to the extent they affect management and control of the listed entity, and agreements/treaties/contracts with media companies; frauds/defaults by a promoter, key managerial personnel, or the listed entity, including arrest of a promoter or KMP; one-time settlements with banks; resolution plans/restructuring relating to loans or borrowings from banks or financial institutions, including inter-creditor agreements and corporate debt restructuring; and notices of shareholders’ meetings.

The circular does not specify a new compliance deadline date or change any thresholds/rates; instead, it reinforces that these disclosures should now be filed in XBRL format on NEAPS and that the attached FAQ is intended as guidance for doing so. Compliance teams should therefore ensure that the company’s announcement process is aligned to the XBRL-enabled NEAPS submission workflow for all covered Regulation 30 items, and that the filing is made in the required format when one of these events occurs. For questions, the Exchange directs companies to contact the Announcements team at takeover@nse.co.in or use the contact details available on the NEAPS platform.

rows.title: Introduction of Issue Summary Document (ISD) – Buy-back
rows.summary:
This NSE listing circular, dated April 28, 2023 (Ref. NSE/CML/2023/33), tells all listed companies that the exchange has enabled a new filing process on the NEAPS platform for the **Issue Summary Document (ISD) for buy-backs**. It is issued in reference to SEBI Circular **SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/29 dated February 15, 2023**, which introduced the ISD and related issue advertisements.

The substantive regulatory change is that, **effective May 2, 2023**, listed entities undertaking either of the following buy-back transactions must prepare and file the ISD in **XBRL format**: **(1) buy-back of equity shares through tender offer** and **(2) buy-back of equity shares from the open market**. The circular does not change the buy-back law itself, but it creates a new electronic filing obligation and prescribes the filing format required by SEBI for these events.

For compliance, listed entities must use the **NEAPS “Common XBRL Upload”** workflow after logging into the portal. The company must select **“Issue Summary Document (ISD) for Buyback”** from the module drop-down, then choose the relevant announcement subject, download the corresponding offline Excel XBRL utility, complete it, generate the **XML file**, enter the required details on the portal, and upload the XML using **“Upload XBRL File”** to submit the ISD. In practical terms, this means compliance teams must ensure the buy-back announcement process now includes preparation of the ISD in the prescribed XBRL utility and completion of the portal upload step, rather than relying on a manual/non-XBRL submission.

If there are issues with the process, NSE directs users to contact the **Announcements team at takeover@nse.co.in** or use the contact details available on the NEAPS platform.

rows.title: FAQs on the submission of the quarterly Corporate Governance Report.
rows.summary:
The NSE issued Circular NSE/CML/2023/31 on April 10, 2023 to all listed entities regarding the submission of the quarterly Corporate Governance Report through the NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS), and attached updated FAQs for guidance. The circular does not change the underlying legal/regulatory requirements; instead, it clarifies how listed companies should complete the data-entry/XBRL filing, and explicitly states that the FAQs are guidance only and are not a substitute for any provision of law, regulation, or SEBI/Exchange circular.

For board-composition disclosures, if a director does not have or cannot use a DIN, the filer must enter only the dummy DIN “99999999” and explain the reason in the company remarks. If PAN is not available or applicable, the filer must enter only the dummy PAN “ZZZZZ9999Z” and likewise provide the reason in company remarks. The listed entity must disclose each director’s correct and complete name exactly as per PAN; where the name or PAN appears discrepant, the Exchange will treat it as a compliance issue for the filing.

rows.title: Additional affirmations by Practicing Company Secretaries (PCS) in Annual Secretarial Compliance Report (ASCR)
rows.summary:
This NSE circular revises the format of the Annual Secretarial Compliance Report (ASCR) for all listed entities by replacing the existing first affirmation required from Practicing Company Secretaries (PCS). The substituted item now requires the PCS to specifically confirm whether the listed entity’s compliances are in accordance with the applicable Secretarial Standards (SS) issued by the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI), with a corresponding compliance status of Yes/No/NA and PCS observations/remarks. The circular states that all other contents of the earlier circular, NSE/CML/2023/21 dated March 16, 2023, remain unchanged, and the revised format is provided as Annexure A.

The circular also changes the submission process temporarily: although listed entities are currently submitting ASCR in both PDF and XBRL, the XBRL submission functionality is still under development. Until that development is completed, entities must provisionally submit the ASCR in PDF format through NEAPS using the path NEAPS > Compliance > Announcements > Announcements/Corporate Actions. NSE further states that once the XBRL mode becomes available, listed entities will also be mandatorily required to file the ASCR in XBRL form in addition to the PDF submission.

The annexure indicates that the broader ASCR now includes “additional affirmations” based on discussions with SEBI, starting with the Secretarial Standards confirmation and continuing with a requirement to verify that all applicable SEBI-regulatory policies have been adopted with board approval and are updated in a timely manner. The circular is dated April 10, 2023 and applies to all listed entities on the National Stock Exchange of India.

rows.title: Comprehensive FAQs on SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015
rows.summary: This NSE circular does not introduce a new substantive rule by itself; it forwards SEBI’s “Comprehensive FAQs on SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015” issued on March 31, 2023, and points members to SEBI’s published clarification webpage and the enclosed copy for reference. The circular is dated April 5, 2023 and was issued by the National Stock Exchange of India’s Listing department under Ref. No. NSE/CML/2023/29 to “all members,” meaning it is a distribution notice for market participants rather than a standalone amendment. For compliance teams, the key action is to review the SEBI FAQs because they clarify how the SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015 should be interpreted and applied in practice; the circular itself does not specify any new deadlines, thresholds, rates, filing dates, or separate compliance mechanics. In other words, any operational impact will come from the SEBI clarifications contained in the linked FAQ document, which affected entities should consult directly to determine whether their insider trading policies, trading window controls, disclosures, or internal compliance procedures need to be updated.

rows.title: Filing of equity announcements in XBRL format on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform.
rows.summary:
NSE has expanded its XBRL filing requirement for equity-related corporate announcements submitted on the NEAPS platform. Under Circular NSE/CML/2023/28 dated March 31, 2023, and as a follow-up to the earlier January 27, 2023 circular (NSE/CML/2023/11), the following Regulation 30 disclosures under SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 will be available in XBRL format starting April 1, 2023: issuance or forfeiture of securities; split or consolidation of shares; buyback of securities; restrictions on transferability or other alterations to the terms/structure of existing securities (including forfeiture, reissue of forfeited securities, alteration of calls, and redemption of securities); certain binding agreements outside the normal course of business such as shareholder agreements, joint venture agreements, family settlement agreements that affect management/control, and agreements/treaties/contracts with media companies; fraud or defaults by a promoter, key managerial personnel, or the listed entity itself, including arrest of a promoter or KMP; one-time settlements with banks; resolution plans/restructuring of loans or borrowings from banks/financial institutions, including Inter-Creditors Agreements; corporate debt restructuring; and notices of shareholders’ meetings.

For compliance purposes, NSE states that at the initial stage a PDF filing will still be treated by the Exchange as sufficient compliance with Regulation 30, but every listed entity must also upload the same announcement in XBRL format within 24 hours after submitting the PDF filing. This creates a dual-filing obligation for the affected announcements: immediate PDF submission as the initial compliance filing, followed by a mandatory XBRL submission within the 24-hour window. The circular applies to all listed companies submitting the specified announcements on NEAPS.

rows.title: Extension of compliance period – Fund raising by large corporates through issuance of debt securities to the extent of 25% of their incremental borrowings in a financial year
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) circulated SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHSRACPOD1/P/CIR/2023/049 dated March 31, 2023, which extends the compliance period for the requirement on large corporates to fund raise through issuance of debt securities to the extent of 25% of their incremental borrowings in a financial year. In practical terms, the underlying obligation remains the same, but SEBI has granted more time for affected large corporates to comply with the debt-securities funding requirement.

The circular is addressed to all listed companies via their Company Secretaries, so compliance teams at listed entities should review whether the company falls within the “large corporate” category under the applicable SEBI framework and whether the 25% incremental borrowing-linked debt issuance requirement applies. The NSE note does not itself restate the technical qualification criteria or the revised compliance deadline; it merely forwards the SEBI circular for “necessary action” and indicates that the SEBI circular should be consulted directly for the operative details.

From a compliance perspective, the key takeaway is that any entity covered by the large-corporate framework should confirm the revised compliance period, reassess its fundraising strategy for the relevant financial year, and ensure any required debt issuance plan is tracked against the 25% threshold based on incremental borrowings. The circular is dated March 31, 2023 and was made available on the NSE website, but the NSE communication itself is informational and does not create a separate requirement beyond drawing attention to SEBI’s extension.

rows.title: Introduction of Issue Summary Document (ISD) – Further Issues
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India circular dated March 31, 2023 (Ref. NSE/CML/2023/26) implements SEBI’s February 15, 2023 circular on the **Introduction of the Issue Summary Document (ISD)** and says that, effective **April 3, 2023**, listed entities must file the ISD in **XBRL format** for specific further issues: **preferential issues, qualified institutional placements (QIP), rights issues, ADR issues, GDR issues, and FCCB issues**. NSE states that it has developed a filing utility for this purpose, and that the utility details are provided in **Annexure A**.

The filing requirement is not limited to a voluntary or later-stage submission: **submission of ISD details becomes mandatory for all applications submitted on or after April 3, 2023**. This applies to two categories of applications: **applications seeking in-principle approval under Regulation 28(1) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015**, and **applications seeking in-principle listing approval after allotment of securities**. The circular directs listed entities to submit the ISD details to **any stock exchange where the relevant securities are listed**, and if submitting to **NSE**, the filing must follow the procedure set out in **Annexure B**.

From a compliance standpoint, NSE warns that **failure to follow these directions will be treated as non-compliance**, and the **relevant application may not be approved**. The practical requirement for listed entities is therefore to ensure that any qualifying further issue application filed on or after April 3, 2023 is accompanied by the required ISD details in the prescribed electronic format and through the prescribed exchange filing process.

rows.title: Standard Operating Process under SEBI(PIT) Regulations, 2015 for ensuring compliance with Structured Digital Database (“SDD”)
rows.summary:
This NSE circular, dated March 29, 2023, continues the Exchange’s prior SDD compliance instructions issued on November 4, 2022, January 25, 2023, and March 16, 2023. It applies to **listed entities for whom Regulation 24A of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 is not applicable**; those entities must **continue** to submit the **Structured Digital Database (SDD) compliance certificate on a quarterly basis**. The submission must be made **within 21 days from the end of each quarter** and sent by email to **sdd_pit@nse.co.in**.

The circular states that the requirement is **effective immediately**, so there is no further implementation grace period. Compliance teams at affected listed entities should ensure their quarterly reporting calendar is aligned to the 21-day deadline and that the SDD compliance certificate is consistently filed to the specified NSE email address. The notice is directed to **all listed companies**, but the specific ongoing obligation described here is only for those entities **outside the scope of Regulation 24A**.

rows.title: Review of Securities available for trading under “permitted to trade” category
rows.summary:
This circular announces a review of all securities currently admitted for trading on the NSE under the “permitted to trade” category. It explains that the Exchange has historically allowed dealings in such securities under Chapter IV-2(c) of the Byelaws and Regulation 3.1.1 of Part A of the Capital Market Segment, but also notes that under Chapter IV, Section 12 of the Byelaws and Regulation 3.1.2, the Exchange has the right to prohibit dealings or suspend trading in any security at any time, on whatever conditions and timing it deems appropriate. The key compliance point is that companies in the “permitted to trade” category do not sign the Exchange’s listing agreement and therefore do not provide the full set of disclosures normally associated with listed companies.

The circular says that, in response to stakeholder feedback, NSE is reviewing the entire “permitted to trade” universe in consultation with, and on the advice of, the Exchange’s Relevant Authority. The resulting decisions will be communicated to market participants, and the Exchange states that adequate notice will be given before any scrip is withdrawn from the “permitted to trade” category. No specific withdrawal date, deadline, threshold, or numeric requirement is set out in this circular, but compliance teams should monitor for follow-up notices because the status of affected securities may change after the review. This applies to all members and all companies currently trading under the “permitted to trade” category.

rows.title: Common and simplified norms for processing investor’s service requests by RTAs and norms for furnishing PAN, KYC details and Nomination
rows.summary:
This NSE communication is an information notice to all listed companies, referencing SEBI circular no. **SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/37 dated 16 March 2023** on “Common and simplified norms for processing investor’s service requests by RTAs and norms for furnishing PAN, KYC details and Nomination.” The NSE circular itself does **not** create new requirements or deadlines; it simply forwards SEBI’s circular and states that a copy is enclosed and available on the NSE website for reference and necessary action by recipients. The addressees are **all listed companies**, which should review the underlying SEBI circular to understand any operational or compliance obligations for their registrar and transfer agents (RTAs) and investor-service processes.

From the text provided, the only explicit action point is that companies are expected to **take necessary action at their end** in light of the SEBI circular. No specific compliance procedure, form change, threshold, effective date beyond the **SEBI circular date of 16 March 2023**, or penalty framework is described in this NSE note itself. Because the letter merely conveys the existence of the SEBI requirements, a compliance team should treat this as a trigger to inspect the referenced SEBI circular for the actual substance on PAN, KYC, nomination, and service-request handling obligations.

rows.title: Path of filing of disclosures related to Corporate Action on NEAPS Portal
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has reminded all listed companies that, under Regulation 10 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, all required reports, statements, documents, filings, and other information must be submitted to the Exchange through the specified electronic platform, which for NSE is the NEAPS Portal. The circular is dated March 21, 2023 and applies to all listed entities on NSE.

The specific compliance change is procedural: disclosures relating to corporate actions, especially the fixing of a Record Date or Book Closure Date for actions such as dividend payments, annual general meetings, and similar corporate actions, must not be embedded in general announcements like “Outcome of Board Meeting” or “Outcome of Shareholder Meeting.” Instead, these items must be filed separately through the dedicated NEAPS path: **NEAPS – Compliance – Announcements - Announcements/CA - Intimation Type: Corporate Action**.

NSE states that all intimation regarding Record Date or Book Closure Date for any corporate action must be separately intimated under this Corporate Actions tab. The circular specifically warns that failure to separately intimate these dates under **Regulation 42** may result in the Exchange not taking the disclosure on record, and the listed entity will bear responsibility for any resulting consequences. NSE also reiterates that it will recognize only those disclosures filed through the correct relevant path on NEAPS, so compliance teams should ensure that any corporate action date-related announcement is routed through the separate Corporate Action filing flow rather than relying on a general meeting outcome disclosure.

rows.title: Additional affirmations by Practicing Company Secretaries (PCS) in Annual Secretarial Compliance Report (ASCR)
rows.summary:
The NSE circular dated March 16, 2023 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2023/21) requires that Practicing Company Secretaries include **additional affirmations** in the **Annual Secretarial Compliance Report (ASCR)** submitted by listed entities. This builds on SEBI’s ASCR framework first issued by circular **CIR/CFD/CMD1/27/2019 dated February 8, 2019**, which has been applicable to listed entities and their material subsidiaries on an **annual basis since March 31, 2019**; the PCS is still required to confirm compliance with SEBI regulations, circulars, and guidelines, but now must also expressly report on the added items below.

The new affirmations require the PCS to state the compliance status (**Yes / No / NA**) and give observations/remarks for whether the listed entity’s secretarial compliances are in accordance with the **ICSI Auditing Standards CSAS-1 to CSAS-3**. The PCS must also verify that **all applicable policies under SEBI regulations have been adopted with board approval**, that those policies are **consistent with SEBI regulations**, and that they have been **reviewed and updated in a timely manner** in line with SEBI regulations, circulars, and guidelines. In addition, the PCS must confirm the entity maintains a **functional website**, disseminates required documents and information **on time** under a separate website section, and ensures the **web-links disclosed in the annual corporate governance report under Regulation 27(2)** are **accurate and specific** and correctly redirect to the relevant document or website section.

The ASCR must also cover director eligibility by confirming that **none of the company’s directors are disqualified under Section 164 of the Companies Act, 2013**. Finally, the PCS must examine subsidiary-related matters for listed entities, specifically the **identification of material subsidiaries** and the **requirements relating to subsidiaries** (the circular text provided ends mid-point on this item, but it clearly imposes a review obligation over subsidiary compliance within the ASCR). For compliance teams, the practical effect is that the annual PCS certification now needs to address these additional affirmative checks explicitly, so listed entities should ensure supporting evidence exists for policy approvals and updates, website accuracy and timeliness, director eligibility, and subsidiary classification/compliance before the ASCR is finalized.

rows.title: Manner of filing financial results as required under regulation 33 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India issued a circular dated 15 March 2023 to all listed companies clarifying the proper filing format for financial results under Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. NSE said it had observed that some companies were uploading board meeting outcome PDFs that began with unrelated material such as shareholders’ letters or investor presentations, with the actual financial results, auditor’s report, and other required statements appearing later in the same filing.  

The exchange directed listed entities that the PDF filed as the “outcome of board meeting held to consider and approve financial results” must contain only the financial results, the auditor’s report, and the other statements specifically prescribed under Regulation 33, Part A of Schedule IV, and the related circulars. Any additional content, such as a shareholders’ letter or investor presentation, must not be bundled into that same financial-results filing and instead must be submitted as a separate announcement.  

There was no new numerical threshold, rate, or deadline introduced in this circular, but the advisory is immediate for all listed companies filing financial results under Regulation 33. Compliance teams should treat this as an operational filing requirement and ensure strict separation between the statutory financial-results submission and any optional investor-relations materials to avoid non-compliant filings.

rows.title: Operational Guidance - Amendment to Securities and Exchange Board of India (Buy-back of Securities) Regulations, 2018 (“Buy-back Regulations”)
rows.summary:
This circular from the National Stock Exchange of India is primarily a forwarding notice to all listed companies, advising them of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-2/P/CIR/2023/35 dated 8 March 2023, titled “Operational Guidance - Amendment to Securities and Exchange Board of India (Buy-back of Securities) Regulations, 2018.” The NSE letter itself does not set out the substantive amendment details; it states that a copy of the SEBI circular is enclosed and that listed companies should take “necessary action” as applicable. It was issued on 9 March 2023 by NSE Listing Circular Ref. No. NSE/CML/2023/19 and is addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed companies.

From a compliance perspective, the key action item in this document is to review the underlying SEBI circular and assess whether any company plans or ongoing activities involving share buy-backs are affected by the amended Buy-back Regulations. The notice does not specify the amended requirements, thresholds, rates, or deadlines itself, so no operational change can be confirmed from this text alone; the only explicit directive is to treat the enclosed SEBI guidance as applicable and take necessary action if the company is undertaking or considering a buy-back. The NSE also notes that the circular is available on its website for reference.

rows.title: Filing of Related Party Transactions (RPT) and Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) to be made available on the NEAPS (NSE Electronic Application Processing System) platform
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE) has expanded the NEAPS (NSE Electronic Application Processing System) platform so that, in addition to equity announcements and financial results, listed companies must also use NEAPS for filing Related Party Transactions (RPT) and the Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report (BRSR). This change is intended to consolidate these filings onto a single portal, and it becomes effective from February 25, 2023.  

For RPT filings, the required method is XBRL submission through the NEAPS navigation path **NEAPS > Common XBRL Upload > Related Party Transactions**. For BRSR filings, the required method is XBRL submission through **NEAPS > Common XBRL Upload > Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report**.  

The circular applies to **all listed companies** and does not change the underlying substantive reporting obligation for RPT or BRSR; it changes the **filing mechanism/portal** used to submit those documents. Companies needing help with submission issues or filing questions are directed to the contact details of the relevant Exchange officers available on the NEAPS portal.

rows.title: Resolution of Company complaints through NEAPS
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE), through Circular Ref. No. NSE/CML/2023/17 dated February 17, 2023, has introduced a new NEAPS functionality for **all listed companies** to view and respond to investor complaints registered against them, specifically complaints relating to **LODR (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements)**. This is not a new complaint mechanism itself, but an enhancement to the existing process that makes complaints visible in each listed company’s own NEAPS login, thereby giving companies centralized access to complaints filed against them on the common platform.

Under the new feature, listed companies can now see complaint records in NEAPS with details such as the **complaint number, symbol, company name, complainant name, complaint date, pending days, and complaint status**. Companies are also able to **submit responses online through the portal**, and any response may include **PDF attachments, including annexures**. NEAPS also now offers the ability to **download and export complaint reports**, which should help compliance teams track open items and maintain records.

The user manual attached to the circular indicates the path to the module is **Compliance → Disclosures → Investor Complaint Desk** after logging into NEAPS with the required credentials. From the complaint list, users can click the **Complaint No.** to open the **Complaint Details** tab, where the complaint information and supporting details are available. The document indicates that the communications sent in relation to the complaint are accessible from within the complaint record, but the provided text cuts off before completing that sentence, so the full extent of the communication history features is not fully visible in the excerpt.

For compliance purposes, the practical obligation is that listed companies should now **monitor complaints directly in NEAPS and use the portal to respond promptly**, rather than relying only on separate correspondence channels. No specific response deadline, fee, threshold, or penalty is stated in this circular; the change is primarily procedural and operational, aimed at improving access, tracking, and electronic response handling for complaints against listed entities.

rows.title: Introduction of Issue Summary Document (ISD) and dissemination of issue advertisements.
rows.summary:
SEBI has introduced a new requirement for listed entities and issuers proposing to list specified securities to file an Issue Summary Document (ISD) in XBRL format. The circular also requires dissemination of issue advertisements on the Exchange’s website, which means the relevant issue-related public advertisements will now be published through the Exchange platform rather than handled only through issuer-side channels. This is a regulatory change communicated by NSE on February 16, 2023, referencing SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/29 dated February 15, 2023.

For compliance purposes, the impacted parties are all listed entities and any issuers planning to list specified securities. The document does not provide procedural details, thresholds, or filing deadlines itself; it directs recipients to the SEBI circular for the operative requirements and instructs them to take note and ensure compliance. No numerical thresholds, filing windows, or transition dates are stated in this NSE notice beyond the February 15, 2023 SEBI circular date and the February 16, 2023 dissemination date.

rows.title: FAQ’s on filing of announcements in XBRL format on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform
rows.summary:
National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE) issued a February 7, 2023 listing circular addressed to all listed companies providing FAQs on the new requirement to file announcements in XBRL format through the NEAPS platform, following its earlier January 27, 2023 circular and demo sessions. The circular confirms that, for the initial period, listed companies must submit both the PDF version and the XBRL version of the disclosure; NSE says it will issue a separate circular announcing the date from which XBRL-only filing will be sufficient and PDF will no longer be required. For compliance timing, the XBRL filing must be made within 24 hours of submitting the PDF disclosure.

The FAQs also clarify that, during the transition period, the PDF filing will be treated as the compliance filing until it is accepted, but after the transition only the XBRL submission will count for compliance purposes. If a company had already filed a prior intimation of a Board meeting on or before January 28, 2023 and later, after January 28, 2023, wants to add new agenda items, it must file the additional agenda item(s) in both PDF and XBRL format. The FAQ set is guidance only and directs listed companies with questions to the NSE Announcements team at takeover@nse.co.in or the contact details available on the NEAPS platform. The document begins an additional FAQ about Board Meeting outcomes, but the provided text cuts off before that answer is completed, so no further requirement can be confirmed from the excerpt.

rows.title: Manner of achieving minimum public shareholding
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is a forwarding notice to all listed companies informing them of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD2/P/CIR/2023/18 dated 3 February 2023, titled “Manner of achieving minimum public shareholding.” The NSE notice itself does not set out the substantive rules; it states that the SEBI circular is enclosed and that listed companies should take “necessary action” in line with it.

From the compliance perspective, the document matters because it signals that SEBI has issued updated guidance on how listed entities are to achieve minimum public shareholding, which is a continuing listing requirement. The notice does not specify the exact procedural changes, timelines, thresholds, or implementation mechanics in the body of the letter, so those details would need to be taken from the enclosed SEBI circular. The NSE also notes that the circular is available on its website for reference. No separate effective date beyond the SEBI circular date of 3 February 2023 is stated in this NSE communication.

rows.title: Generating Awareness on Availability of Dispute Resolution Mechanism at Stock Exchanges against Listed Companies/Registrar to an Issue and Share Transfer Agents (RTAs)
rows.summary:
This notice is an onward communication from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited to all listed companies, pointing them to SEBI Letter No. SEBI/HO/OIAE/2023/03391 dated January 27, 2023. The subject of the SEBI letter is the “Generating Awareness on Availability of Dispute Resolution Mechanism at Stock Exchanges against Listed Companies/Registrar to an Issue and Share Transfer Agents (RTAs).” The exchange is not itself setting out detailed new operational requirements in this text; rather, it is formally alerting listed companies that SEBI has issued guidance on the availability of a stock-exchange dispute resolution mechanism for complaints or disputes involving listed companies and RTAs, and it requests “necessary action at your end.”

From a compliance perspective, the key point is that the communication is directed to all listed companies and concerns their awareness and handling of the stock-exchange dispute resolution route that may be used against them or their RTAs. The notice states that a copy of SEBI’s January 27, 2023 letter is enclosed and also available on the NSE website (www.nseindia.com), indicating that firms should review the underlying SEBI letter for the substantive process expectations and any specific obligations. No implementation deadline, fee, threshold, or quantitative requirement is stated in this covering communication itself. The practical obligation created by this letter is therefore to review the referenced SEBI communication promptly and take whatever internal compliance, investor grievance, or registrar/transfer-agent coordination steps are required under that underlying directive.
