From a compliance standpoint, entities affected are all listed companies that enter CIRP and the IRP/RP handling the process, and they must ensure that every key CIRP event is intimated in the prescribed digital format and through the correct subject classification.

rows.title: Extension of facility for conducting annual meeting and other meetings of unitholders of REITs and InvITs through Video Conferencing (VC) or through Other Audio-Visual means (OAVM)
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India is informing listed Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs), listed Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs), and their parties that SEBI has extended the permission to conduct annual meetings and other meetings of unitholders through Video Conferencing (VC) or other Audio-Visual means (OAVM). The NSE circular itself does not set out new operational rules; it points recipients to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div2/P/CIR/2022/079 dated June 03, 2022, which is the controlling document for the extension and any related compliance steps. The NSE issued this as Listing Circular Ref. No. NSE/CML/2022/26 on June 07, 2022, and explicitly states that the SEBI circular is enclosed and should be acted on as necessary.  

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the electronic-meeting facility for InvIT and REIT unitholder meetings remains available beyond prior deadlines, so entities covered by the SEBI circular should continue using VC/OAVM for annual and other unitholder meetings in accordance with SEBI’s directions and any procedural requirements in that circular. No thresholds, voting percentages, or dates for specific meeting notices are stated in the NSE text itself, and no additional obligations are introduced in the NSE communication beyond awareness and implementation of the enclosed SEBI circular.

rows.title: Circular on Development of Passive Funds
rows.summary: The document is an informational forwarding circular addressed to **all Asset Management Companies (AMCs)**, referring them to **SEBI Notification No. SEBI/HO/IMD/DOF2/P/CIR/2022/69 dated May 23, 2022**, titled **“Circular on Development of Passive Funds.”** It does **not itself impose new obligations, deadlines, thresholds, or procedures**; rather, it states that the SEBI circular is available on the **NSE website** for reference. The only practical compliance implication from this notice is that AMCs should review the underlying **SEBI circular** to determine any requirements related to the development of passive funds, but this NSE communication alone is merely informational and does not add substantive compliance requirements.

rows.title: Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for dispute resolution under the Stock Exchange arbitration mechanism for disputes between a Listed Company and/or Registrars to an Issue and Share Transfer Agents (RTAs) and its Shareholder(s)/Investor(s)
rows.summary: This NSE listing circular dated May 31, 2022 simply forwards and calls attention to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD_RTAMB/P/CIR/2022/76 dated May 30, 2022, which establishes Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for dispute resolution through the stock exchange arbitration mechanism in disputes involving a listed company and/or its Registrar and Share Transfer Agent (RTA) and the company’s shareholder(s)/investor(s). The circular is addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed companies and instructs recipients to refer to the enclosed SEBI circular and take “necessary action” as applicable; it also notes that the SEBI circular is available on the NSE website. No specific operational steps, deadlines, monetary thresholds, or reporting dates are set out in the NSE covering letter itself, beyond the issuance date of May 31, 2022 and the reference to the underlying SEBI circular dated May 30, 2022. For compliance purposes, the material action point is that listed companies should review the SEBI SOP on arbitration/dispute resolution and align their internal dispute-handling processes with the exchange arbitration framework for shareholder/investor complaints against the company and/or its RTAs.

rows.title: Simplification of procedure and standardization of formats of documents for issuance of duplicate securities certificates
rows.summary:
This NSE circular informs all listed companies that SEBI has issued Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD_RTAMB/P/CIR/2022/70 on May 25, 2022, titled “Simplification of procedure and standardization of formats of documents for issuance of duplicate securities certificates.” The NSE notice itself does not restate the full operational rules; it serves as an intimation and forwards the SEBI circular for “necessary action,” meaning the actual compliance requirements are contained in the SEBI circular referenced by this notice.

The document is addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed companies, so the affected entities are all companies listed on the NSE (and, by implication, any issuer subject to SEBI’s duplicate certificate procedures). It indicates that companies should review and implement the simplified procedure and standardized document formats for issuing duplicate securities certificates as prescribed by SEBI. No separate deadline, transition date, threshold, or numerical requirement is stated in this NSE communication beyond the circular date of May 25, 2022.

For compliance purposes, the key takeaway is that listed companies and their registrars/transfer agents should align internal processes, documentation, and investor service workflows with the SEBI-issued duplicate certificate framework and standardized forms referenced in the attached circular. The notice also confirms that the SEBI circular is available on the NSE website for reference.

rows.title: Streamlining the Process of Rights Issue
rows.summary:
This circular from the National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. is addressed to all listed companies and serves to notify them of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/SSEP/CIR/P/2022/66 dated May 19, 2022, titled “Streamlining the Process of Rights Issue.” The NSE communication itself does not set out the detailed procedural changes; instead, it forwards SEBI’s circular for reference and “necessary action,” meaning the operative requirements are those contained in the SEBI circular and apply to listed companies that undertake rights issues.  

For compliance purposes, the key point is that companies planning a rights issue must align their process with SEBI’s revised streamlined framework effective from May 19, 2022, rather than relying on prior rights issue procedures. The notice does not specify any monetary thresholds, ratios, or filing deadlines in the text provided, but it does indicate that immediate review and implementation of the SEBI circular’s requirements is expected where a rights issue is being undertaken.  

Because the circular is directed to “all listed companies,” compliance teams at listed issuers should treat this as a market-wide procedural update affecting capital-raising via rights issue and should ensure the company secretary and issue-management teams review the enclosed SEBI circular in full for the exact operational steps, approvals, disclosures, and timelines now required.

rows.title: Simplification of procedure and standardization of formats of documents for transmission of securities
rows.summary: This NSE circular does not itself create new substantive requirements; it forwards and calls attention to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD_RTAMB/P/CIR/2022/65 dated May 18, 2022, titled “Simplification of procedure and standardization of formats of documents for transmission of securities pursuant to amendments to the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.” It is addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed companies and states that the SEBI circular is enclosed for reference and necessary action, so the compliance obligation is to review and implement the SEBI-prescribed transmission procedure and standardized document formats at the issuer level. The NSE notice itself is dated May 19, 2022 and is informational in nature, with the only explicit operational instruction being that listed companies should take necessary action in line with the enclosed SEBI circular. No separate thresholds, rates, deadlines, or entity-specific exceptions are provided in the NSE text beyond its application to all listed companies.

rows.title: Relaxation from compliance with certain provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is an informational transmission to all listed companies, forwarding SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CMD2/CIR/P/2022/62 dated May 13, 2022, titled “Relaxation from compliance with certain provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.” The NSE notice itself does not set out the substantive relaxation details; it states that the SEBI circular is enclosed and should be referred to for “necessary action,” meaning the operative compliance relief or exemption is contained in the SEBI circular rather than in the NSE cover note.

For compliance purposes, the key facts in this document are the issuance date of the NSE communication, May 16, 2022, and its applicability to all listed companies through their Company Secretaries. No new thresholds, reporting formats, deadlines, or numerical requirements are introduced in the NSE letter itself, and it does not amend any obligations independently. The document’s practical effect is to notify listed entities that SEBI has issued temporary or otherwise specific relaxations from certain LODR provisions, and that entities should review the SEBI circular directly to determine which obligations are modified, the duration of the relaxation, and any conditional compliance steps.

rows.title: Reduction of timelines for listing of units of Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT)
rows.summary: This communication informs **all listed companies** that the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)** has issued Circular No. **SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div3/P/CIR/2022/55 dated April 28, 2022**, titled **“Reduction of timelines for listing of units of Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT)”**. The notice itself does not set out the new timelines or operational details, but it directs recipients to the attached SEBI circular for the specific changes and for any required action. In compliance terms, the relevant impact is on entities involved in the issuance/listing process for **InvIT units**—particularly listed companies and any other market participants responsible for completing listing formalities—because SEBI has reduced the time allowed for listing those units. The communication is informational and does not specify a separate implementation date beyond the referenced **April 28, 2022** SEBI circular, so compliance teams should review that circular immediately to confirm the revised listing deadline and update internal issuance/listing procedures accordingly.

rows.title: Reduction of timelines for listing of units of Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT)
rows.summary:
This notice is a transmission by the National Stock Exchange of India Limited to all listed companies, pointing them to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div3/P/CIR/2022/54 dated April 28, 2022, which is titled “Reduction of timelines for listing of units of Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT).” The document itself does not set out the underlying rule changes or the revised timelines; it simply states that SEBI has issued a circular reducing the time period for listing REIT units and that a copy of that circular is enclosed for reference and “necessary action.”

For compliance purposes, the only explicit action required by this notice is to review the referenced SEBI circular and take any needed internal action if your company is involved in REIT-related issuance or listing activities. The notice is addressed broadly to “all listed companies,” so the immediate operational effect is informational rather than a direct company-specific directive in this text. The effective date of the referenced SEBI change is April 28, 2022, but no specific deadline, numeric timeline, threshold, or procedural detail is provided in the body of this letter itself.

rows.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) – Disclosure of Related Party Transactions under regulation 23 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015
rows.summary:
The NSE issued this circular on April 25, 2022 to all listed companies, pointing them to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CMD1/CIR/P/2021/662 dated November 22, 2021, which introduced revised disclosure obligations for related party transactions (RPTs) under Regulation 23 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. The NSE’s communication does not itself create new substantive rules; it circulates SEBI’s FAQs and instructs listed entities to comply with the listing regulations and any other applicable regulations as amended from time to time. It also states explicitly that the FAQs are only for guidance, so the binding obligation remains the underlying SEBI circular and the applicable regulations.

The FAQ material provided in the document clarifies how to apply the new SEBI disclosure format for transactions undertaken within a consolidated group. Specifically, when a transaction occurs between members of the consolidated entity—meaning between the listed entity and its subsidiary, or between subsidiaries—the transaction should be disclosed only once and should not be duplicated in the RPT reporting from each entity’s perspective. The example given is a listed holding company, X Ltd., selling goods worth Rs. 10 crores to its subsidiary Y Ltd.; that transaction must be reported once only, either as a sale by X Ltd. or as a purchase by Y Ltd., but not both.

The document fragment ends before the answer to Q2, so no effective date, transition period, threshold, or additional procedural requirement is visible in the provided text beyond the general instruction to follow the new SEBI RPT disclosure format and avoid double-counting intra-group transactions in consolidated disclosures.

rows.title: XBRL based filing of Investor Grievance for Listed Companies at NSE
rows.summary:
NSE has issued a circular dated April 11, 2022 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2022/17) requiring all listed companies to file the quarterly Investor Grievance report under Regulation 13(3) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 using an XBRL-based process instead of the prior standard filing approach. The underlying regulatory obligation remains the same: listed entities must, within 21 days from the end of each quarter, report the number of investor complaints pending at the beginning of the quarter, received during the quarter, disposed of during the quarter, and remaining unresolved at quarter-end.

The change introduced by this circular is procedural and technology-based. NSE is providing an offline Excel utility (attached as Annexure 1) that must be used to generate the XBRL/XML file in the prescribed format. Companies must then upload the generated XML file through the NEAPS portal by navigating to Compliance > Common XBRL upload, selecting “Investor Grievance” from the Modules dropdown, choosing the relevant quarter, and uploading the XML file via the upload tab. After successful submission, the portal will display a “File Uploaded successfully” message and an acknowledgement email will be sent to the registered email address.

This requirement applies to all listed companies filing the Regulation 13(3) investor grievance statement with NSE. The circular does not change the substantive complaint data that must be disclosed, but it does change the filing format and submission process to XBRL through NEAPS. For issues or clarification, NSE instructs filers to contact nsexbrl@nse.co.in.

rows.title: FAQ’s - LODR amendments dated August 03, 2021
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India issued this April 8, 2022 circular to all listed companies, updating its FAQs on the LODR amendments dated August 3, 2021. The circular does not itself create new obligations beyond the LODR amendment; instead, it directs listed entities to comply with the Listing Regulations and any other applicable regulations as amended from time to time, and states that the FAQs are for guidance only.

The substantive clarification concerns newly inserted Regulation 17(1C), which requires a listed entity to obtain shareholder approval for the appointment of a person to its Board of Directors at the next general meeting or within three months from the date of appointment, whichever is earlier. The FAQ clarifies that this amended requirement applies only to director appointments made on or after January 1, 2022; directors appointed on or before December 31, 2021 remain governed by the pre-amendment provisions. It also clarifies that the type of shareholder resolution required for the approval—ordinary or special—must be determined based on the provisions then currently in force under the LODR.

In a second clarification, NSE states that Regulation 17(1C) applies not only to initial appointments but also to re-appointments of directors. For compliance teams, this means any board appointment or re-appointment made from January 1, 2022 onward should be tracked to ensure shareholder approval is secured no later than the earlier of the next general meeting or three months from the appointment date.

rows.title: Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for dispute resolution available under the stock exchange arbitration mechanism for disputes between a listed company and its shareholder(s)/investor(s)
rows.summary: This NSE circular dated April 8, 2022 is a forwarding/implementation notice to the Company Secretary of all listed companies, sent through recognized stock exchanges, and it directs companies to note and act on the underlying SEBI circular dated the same day: SEBI/HO/CFD/SSEP/CIR/P/2022/48, titled “Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for dispute resolution available under the stock exchange arbitration mechanism for disputes between a listed company and its shareholder(s)/investor(s).” The text provided does not itself set out the SOP details, but it makes clear that SEBI has issued a formal procedure for resolving disputes between listed companies and their shareholders/investors through the stock exchange arbitration framework, and that the SEBI circular is attached/enclosed for necessary action. The compliance implication is that listed companies should review the SEBI circular immediately and prepare to follow the arbitration/dispute-resolution process it prescribes for investor-shareholder disputes, as this is an exchange-circulated regulatory requirement rather than a voluntary guidance note. No separate effective date, transition period, filing deadline, numeric threshold, or penalty is stated in this NSE covering letter beyond the circular date itself (April 8, 2022); the operative requirements would be contained in the SEBI circular referenced and enclosed.

rows.title: Clarification on applicability of Regulation 23(4) read with Regulation 23(3)(e) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 in relation to Related Party Transactions
rows.summary:
This circular from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited is primarily a forwarding notice to all listed companies, stating that SEBI issued Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CMD1/CIR/P/2022/47 on April 08, 2022, titled “Clarification on applicability of Regulation 23(4) read with Regulation 23(3)(e) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 in relation to Related Party Transactions.” The NSE informs companies that a copy of the SEBI circular is enclosed and available on the NSE website, and requests “necessary action” at the recipient’s end, but this NSE letter itself does not set out the substantive rule change or separate compliance deadline beyond the April 08, 2022 circular date.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the operative guidance is in the referenced SEBI circular, which clarifies how Regulation 23(4) should be read together with Regulation 23(3)(e) for related party transactions under the LODR Regulations, 2015. The document applies to all listed companies through recognized stock exchanges, and the subject matter is related party transaction approval and disclosure treatment. Because the text provided here is only the NSE forwarding communication, a compliance officer would need to review the enclosed SEBI circular directly to identify the precise approval thresholds, exemptions, procedural requirements, and any implementation or effective date details that may apply to the company.

rows.title: Processing of waiver applications by the Exchanges in case of commonly listed entities
rows.summary:
This NSE circular, issued on March 31, 2022 and effective for waiver applications submitted on or after April 1, 2022, changes how waiver requests for SOP fines are handled when the same listed company is listed on more than one exchange. It is issued in the context of SEBI’s SOP framework, under which exchanges monitor listed-entity filings and may impose penalties, shift securities to the “Z” category, freeze promoter holdings, or suspend trading for non-compliance; SEBI also permits exchanges to deviate from prescribed SOP actions only if they record reasons in writing. Under the new procedure, waiver applications from “commonly listed entities” are to be segregated so that only one exchange will process the application, and the decision taken by that processing exchange will be binding on all other exchanges that have levied penalties for the same non-compliance.

The circular also states that the exchange handling the waiver request will charge a nominal processing fee. The detailed procedural mechanics and the applicable fee schedule are not in the main circular text provided here; they are set out in Annexure I, which governs the process for waiver applications of SOP fines from the effective date onward. For compliance purposes, the key operational change is that dual or multiple exchange waiver filings for the same default are no longer to be handled independently by each exchange; instead, the company should expect a single exchange-led review whose outcome applies across all relevant exchanges.

rows.title: Clarification on applicability of Regulation 23 of  SEBI  (Listing  Obligations  and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 in relation to Related Party Transactions
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated **March 31, 2022** does not itself introduce new substantive requirements; it **notifies all listed companies**, through recognized stock exchanges, of a corresponding **SEBI circular dated March 30, 2022** that clarifies how **Regulation 23 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015** applies to **related party transactions**. The NSE states that the SEBI circular is enclosed and is also available on the NSE website, and instructs recipients to take **“necessary action”** based on that SEBI clarification.

For compliance purposes, the important point is that this communication is directed to **all listed companies** and concerns their obligations under **LODR Regulation 23** in connection with **related party transactions**. However, the text provided here does **not** spell out the actual clarification, thresholds, approvals, exemptions, reporting requirements, or any effective date beyond the circular date itself; those details would be contained in the referenced SEBI circular, not in this NSE covering notice. In practice, a compliance team should treat this as a formal alert that the SEBI clarification may affect how the company identifies, reviews, approves, and discloses related party transactions under Regulation 23, and should review the enclosed SEBI circular immediately for the exact operational requirements.

rows.title: Automation of disclosure requirements under SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 - System Driven Disclosures - Ease of doing business
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is a forwarding notice to all listed companies, informing them that SEBI issued Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/DCR-3/P/CIR/2022/27 on March 7, 2022, titled **“Automation of disclosure requirements under SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 - System Driven Disclosures - Ease of doing business.”** The NSE letter itself does **not** set out the underlying disclosure mechanics or thresholds; it simply encloses the SEBI circular and directs recipients to review it and take any necessary action.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the subject matter concerns **automated, system-driven disclosures** under the **SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 (SAST Regulations)**, which indicates that disclosure obligations around share acquisitions/takeovers are being moved toward an exchange/system-generated framework rather than solely manual reporting. The notice is addressed to the **Company Secretary of all listed companies through recognized stock exchanges**, so the affected population is broad and includes every listed company subject to NSE/stock exchange disclosure workflows. The circular is dated **March 7, 2022**, and the NSE states the SEBI circular is available on its website and is enclosed for reference.

Because the text provided is only the forwarding cover note and not the SEBI circular itself, it does **not** specify the exact disclosure triggers, numerical thresholds, filing timelines, or procedural steps being automated. A compliance officer should therefore treat this as an alert that the company should review the enclosed SEBI circular immediately to determine whether any internal shareholding monitoring, disclosure controls, or exchange reporting processes need to be updated to align with the system-driven disclosure regime.

rows.title: Extension to SEBI Circular on “Relaxation in adherence to prescribed timelines issued by SEBI due to Covid 19” dated April 13, 2020
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India is notifying all listed companies, through recognized stock exchanges, of a SEBI circular dated **February 25, 2022** that **extends the relief granted under SEBI’s April 13, 2020 Covid-19 timeline-relaxation circular**. The NSE communication itself does not create new substantive obligations or change any filing requirement; instead, it directs companies to refer to SEBI Circular No. **SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD_RTAMB/P/CIR/2022/26** for the applicable extended timelines and to take “necessary action” based on that SEBI extension.  

For compliance purposes, the key point is that any listed company or other entity covered by the original SEBI Covid-era timeline relaxations should check whether the relief period has been prolonged by the **February 25, 2022** SEBI extension and ensure its internal deadlines and implementation schedules are aligned accordingly. The NSE states that a copy of the SEBI circular is enclosed and also available on the NSE website, but the NSE notice itself provides **no specific dates, thresholds, or procedural changes** beyond confirming the extension and instructing recipients to act as required under the SEBI circular.

rows.title: Approach to securities market data access and terms of usage of data provided by data sources in Indian securities market
rows.summary: This NSE circular, dated February 25, 2022, is a forwarding notice to the Company Secretaries of all REITs and all InvITs, informing them of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DEPA-III/DEPA-III_SSU/P/CIR/2022/25 issued the same day, titled “Approach to securities market data access and terms of usage of data provided by data sources in Indian securities market.” The NSE does not itself set out new substantive obligations in this note; instead, it states that the SEBI circular is enclosed for reference and “necessary action” and is also available on the NSE website. From a compliance perspective, the affected entities are REITs and InvITs, and the operational requirement is to review the underlying SEBI circular and implement any data-access or data-usage obligations that SEBI imposes on market data sources or users. No specific deadlines, thresholds, fees, or procedural details are provided in this NSE cover circular itself beyond the date of issue and the instruction to take necessary action based on the enclosed SEBI guidance.

rows.title: Release of New Digital Portal for filing of Information with the Exchange – for Equity Announcements and Disclosures under SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India’s Listing Compliance circular dated February 17, 2022 announces the launch of a new Digital Portal for filings with the Exchange and states that it will go live on February 19, 2022. In Phase 1, the portal is mandatory only for two filing types: equity announcements and disclosures under the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 (SAST). All other filings will continue to be submitted through the existing NEAPS portal for now, so this is a partial migration rather than a full replacement.

The Exchange instructs all listed entities to log in to the new portal by February 18, 2022 to avoid filing delays once the portal becomes active on February 19, 2022. Access details are provided: the portal link is https://digitalexchange.nseindia.com, the username is the existing NEAPS login, and the default password is “Welcome@12345” (the circular also references “Continuation Sheet” in the login instructions). A demo session is scheduled for Friday, February 18, 2022 at 11:00 a.m. to show users how to access the portal, and the link for that demo was reportedly emailed to all listed entities.

For support, the NSE has set up a dedicated help desk for questions or issues relating to the new portal. The help desk can be reached at toll-free number 1800 266 0050 (IVR option 4) or by email at compliancecustomersupport@nse.co.in. The circular is issued on behalf of the National Stock Exchange of India Limited by Avishkar Naik, Head – Listing.

rows.title: Conversion of Private Unlisted InvIT into Private Listed InvIT
rows.summary:
This communication from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited is a forwarding notice to all Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) about SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div3/P/CIR/2022/16 dated February 9, 2022, titled “Conversion of Private Unlisted InvIT into Private Listed InvIT.” The document itself does not set out the conversion requirements, procedural steps, thresholds, or timelines; it simply alerts InvITs that SEBI has issued a circular on this subject and encloses that circular for reference and necessary action.  

For compliance purposes, the only actionable point in this notice is that private unlisted InvITs should review the referenced SEBI circular to determine whether and how they may convert into private listed InvITs and what filings, approvals, disclosures, or other compliance steps may be required. No effective date beyond the date of the referenced SEBI circular is stated here, and no substantive changes or obligations are described in this notice itself.

rows.title: Disclosures in the abridged prospectus and front cover page of the offer document
rows.summary:
The notice is addressed to all issuers proposing to list their specified securities and is a forwarding communication from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited enclosing SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/SSEP/CIR/P/2022/14 dated February 4, 2022, titled “Disclosures in the abridged prospectus and front cover page of the offer document.” The exchange is informing issuers that SEBI has issued this circular and that the enclosed circular should be referred to for implementation and necessary action. The document itself does not reproduce the detailed disclosure requirements, any thresholds, or the full procedural changes; it only alerts issuers that their abridged prospectus and offer document front cover page disclosures are subject to the SEBI circular.

For compliance purposes, the affected entities are issuers planning to list specified securities in India, and the practical obligation is to review and comply with the SEBI circular’s updated disclosure expectations in the abridged prospectus and on the front cover page of the offer document when preparing a public issue or similar listing document package. No separate effective date, transition period, penalty, or numeric threshold is stated in this cover communication beyond the referenced SEBI circular date of February 4, 2022.

rows.title: Framework for conversion of Private Listed InvIT into Public InvIT
rows.summary:
This communication from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited is a forwarding notice to all Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) regarding SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div3/P/CIR/2022/15 dated February 09, 2022, titled “Framework for conversion of Private Listed InvIT into Public InvIT.” The document itself does not restate the substantive conversion rules; it advises recipients that SEBI has issued a framework governing how a privately listed InvIT may convert into a public InvIT, and that the SEBI circular is enclosed for reference and necessary action.

For compliance purposes, the affected entities are all InvITs, specifically private listed InvITs that may seek conversion into public InvIT status. No implementation deadline, transitional timeline, thresholds, fees, or procedural steps are provided in this covering notice; those details would be contained in the referenced SEBI circular rather than in this communication. The practical obligation conveyed here is to review the enclosed SEBI framework and take any required action under that circular if the InvIT is considering or is subject to such a conversion.

rows.title: Schemes of Arrangement by Listed Entities
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is a forwarding notice to **all listed companies** advising them of a **same-day SEBI circular dated February 1, 2022** titled **“Schemes of Arrangement by Listed Entities.”** The NSE letter itself does **not set out the substantive requirements**, change any rules directly, or create an independent compliance deadline; it simply states that the SEBI circular is enclosed and should be acted upon as necessary. From a compliance standpoint, the key point is that **listed entities contemplating or implementing a scheme of arrangement** must review and follow the **SEBI circular issued on February 1, 2022**, because the NSE is expressly directing listed companies to take “necessary action” in light of that SEBI guidance.

The document is addressed to the **Company Secretary of all listed companies**, so the affected population is broad: any NSE-listed entity that may engage in a merger, demerger, compromise, reconstruction, or other scheme of arrangement. No monetary thresholds, rates, filing dates, or procedural steps are stated in this NSE cover note, and no new compliance timetable appears here beyond the **February 1, 2022** date of the referenced SEBI circular. In practice, a compliance team should treat this as a prompt to obtain and implement the enclosed SEBI circular’s requirements for schemes of arrangement, since the NSE notice confirms that the SEBI framework is the operative document.

rows.title: Issuance of Securities in dematerialized form in case of Investor Service Requests
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated January 27, 2022 is an information/intimation notice to the Company Secretary of all listed companies, sent through recognized stock exchanges, referencing SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD_RTAMB/P/CIR/2022/8 dated January 25, 2022. The NSE circular itself does not set out the substantive compliance requirements; it states that SEBI has issued a circular titled **“Issuance of Securities in dematerialized form in case of Investor Service Requests”** and that a copy is enclosed for reference and necessary action.  

For compliance purposes, the key point is that this notice applies to **all listed companies** and relates to **how securities must be issued in dematerialized form when responding to investor service requests**. The exchange is directing listed entities to review and act on the underlying SEBI circular, which is the operative document imposing any new procedural or reporting obligations.  

The NSE notice provides no separate deadlines, thresholds, rates, or transition dates beyond its own issuance date of **January 27, 2022** and the referenced SEBI circular date of **January 25, 2022**. A compliance team should therefore treat the SEBI circular as the controlling text and confirm whether internal procedures for handling investor service requests now require issuance only in demat form, and whether any registrar/share transfer agent or secretarial workflows need to be updated accordingly.

rows.title: Launch of Digital Portal for filings done with the Exchange
rows.summary:
NSE announced the launch of a new Digital Portal for exchange filings, replacing the current NEAPS system for listed entities in a phased migration. Until the transition is complete, listed companies will continue to be moved onto the Digital Portal gradually, but NSE stated that all filings will ultimately be made through the new portal rather than NEAPS. In the initial phase, the portal will cover two filing types: exchange announcements and disclosures made under the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011.

The circular says all listed entities will receive an email from the Digital Portal address, noreply@digitalexchange.nse.co.in, on or before January 08, 2021, instructing them to migrate to the new NSE Digital Portal. The migration steps for Company Super Users and Sub Users are provided in Annexure 1, and the activation link is sent to the email address registered on the NEAPS portal. Users are instructed to click the “here” button in the email to access the activation flow and complete migration of the company’s user credentials.

NSE also said it will conduct webinars to explain how the Digital Portal should be accessed and used. The document does not specify a separate hard deadline for full migration, filing cutovers, or penalties, but it does make clear that the portal is intended to become the new filing channel for all listed entities and that detailed circulars on the submission process will be issued later.

rows.title: Extension of facility for conducting annual meeting and other meetings of unitholders of REITs and InvITs through Video Conferencing (VC) or through Other Audio-Visual means (OAVM)
rows.summary:
This NSE circular does not itself create new substantive requirements; it informs all listed InvITs, all listed REITs, and all parties involved with REITs and InvITs that SEBI has extended the permission to hold annual meetings and other unitholder meetings through video conferencing (VC) or other audio-visual means (OAVM). The exchange is forwarding SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div2/P/CIR/2021/697 dated December 22, 2021, and states that the SEBI circular is enclosed for reference and for any necessary action by recipients. The document does not set out separate NSE deadlines, thresholds, voting rules, or procedural details; those operative requirements would be in the referenced SEBI circular, not in this NSE notice.

From a compliance perspective, the key point is that REITs and InvITs can continue using VC/OAVM for annual meetings and other unitholder meetings under the extended SEBI framework, and entities should review the underlying SEBI circular to confirm the exact conditions and any compliance steps required for conducting such meetings virtually. The circular is dated January 5, 2022 and is issued by the National Stock Exchange of India Limited as a market notice for information and onward action.

rows.title: Schemes of Arrangement by Listed Entities - Clarification w.r.t. timing of submission of NOC from the lending scheduled commercial banks/ financial institutions/ debenture trustee
rows.summary:
This NSE circular informs all listed companies of a clarification issued by SEBI on January 3, 2022 regarding the timing for submitting the no-objection certificate (NOC) from lending scheduled commercial banks, financial institutions, or the debenture trustee in connection with schemes of arrangement under Regulation 37(1) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. The key change/clarification is that, where an NOC is required under SEBI’s earlier circulars dated November 16, 2021 and November 18, 2021, the NOC must be submitted to the stock exchange before the exchange issues its no-objection letter under Regulation 37(1). In other words, the exchange will not issue its no-objection letter until it has received the relevant lender/debenture trustee NOC.

The circular applies to listed entities proposing schemes of arrangement that fall under Regulation 37 and that involve outstanding borrowings or debentures requiring consent/objection clearance from scheduled commercial banks, financial institutions, or a debenture trustee. No numerical thresholds or monetary limits are introduced in this circular, and no new filing form is prescribed; the operative compliance obligation is purely timing-based. NSE also reminds companies that they must continue to comply with its earlier Circular ref. no. NSE/CML/2021/43 dated November 02, 2021, which sets out the Standard Operating Procedure for applications filed under Regulation 37 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. The circular is effective from January 3, 2022, the date of SEBI’s clarification and NSE’s communication.

rows.title: FAQ’s - LODR amendments dated August 03, 2021
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated December 22, 2021 issued FAQs on the SEBI LODR amendments notified on August 3, 2021, and it is addressed to all listed companies. The circular does not itself create a new substantive rule beyond pointing companies to the amended LODR requirements and noting that the FAQs are only for assistance; companies remain responsible for complying with the listing regulations and any other applicable regulations as amended from time to time.

The FAQ clarifies the application of newly inserted Regulation 17(1C), which requires a listed entity to obtain shareholder approval for the appointment of a person to the Board of Directors at the next general meeting or within three months from the date of appointment, whichever is earlier. This provision applies only to appointments made on or after January 1, 2022; directors appointed on or before December 31, 2021 remain governed by the pre-amendment rules.

The FAQ also specifies that the form of shareholder resolution required for such approval—ordinary or special—must be determined according to the provisions then currently prevailing under LODR. For compliance purposes, listed entities should therefore distinguish between board appointments made before and after January 1, 2022, track the shareholder-approval deadline of the earlier of the next general meeting or three months from appointment for post-January 1, 2022 appointments, and ensure the correct resolution type is used under the applicable LODR framework.

rows.title: Clarification with respect to Circular dated November 03, 2021, on Common and simplified norms for processing investor’s service request by RTAs and norms for furnishing PAN, KYC details and Nomination
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated December 15, 2021 does not itself impose a new operational rule; it transmits and points listed companies to SEBI Notification No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD_RTAMB/P/CIR/2021/687 dated December 14, 2021, titled “Clarification with respect to Circular dated November 03, 2021, on Common and simplified norms for processing investor’s service request by RTAs and norms for furnishing PAN, KYC details and Nomination.” The stated audience is the Company Secretary of all listed companies, routed through recognized stock exchanges, and the exchange is asking recipients to note the SEBI clarification and take any necessary action at their end. The circular indicates that the SEBI clarification is attached/enclosed for reference and is also available on the NSE website.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that this NSE communication is an informational forwarding notice, not a substantive implementation deadline notice in its own text. No specific deadlines, thresholds, forms, or procedural changes are set out in this NSE note itself; any actual compliance obligations would be contained in the referenced SEBI clarification and the earlier November 3, 2021 circular it amends/clarifies. Accordingly, listed companies should review the attached SEBI circular to determine whether investor-service request processing by RTAs, PAN/KYC furnishing, or nomination-related requirements have been clarified or changed, and then ensure internal and registrar-facing processes are aligned.

rows.title: Master Circular for Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs)
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India is forwarding SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div3/P/CIR/2021/674 dated November 29, 2021, titled “Master Circular for Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs),” to **all listed REITs** for information and necessary action. The NSE document itself does **not** set out the substantive requirements of the master circular; it is a transmittal notice confirming that the SEBI circular is enclosed and should be reviewed and implemented as applicable.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the affected entities are **listed REITs**, and the operative regulatory text is in the **SEBI circular dated November 29, 2021**, not in the NSE covering letter. The NSE circular is dated **December 1, 2021** and advises recipients to take any necessary action based on the attached SEBI master circular. Since the substance is not reproduced in the NSE notice, a compliance officer would need to review the enclosed SEBI circular directly to identify specific obligations, deadlines, thresholds, or procedural changes.

rows.title: Master Circular for Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs)
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India issued this notice on December 1, 2021 to all listed Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs), stating that SEBI had released a “Master Circular for Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs)” on November 29, 2021. The NSE circular itself does not set out new substantive compliance requirements, thresholds, deadlines, or procedural changes; it is an informational forwarding circular that encloses the SEBI master circular and instructs recipients to take the enclosed SEBI communication into account and comply as necessary. 

For compliance purposes, the key point is that all listed InvITs are the intended audience, and the operative regulatory content is contained in SEBI’s November 29, 2021 master circular rather than in the NSE notice. Accordingly, a compliance team should treat this NSE communication as a prompt to review the enclosed SEBI circular in full for any binding obligations applicable to listed InvITs, but no additional rule change is specified in the text provided here.

rows.title: Non-compliance with certain provisions of SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018.
rows.summary:
This communication is a forwarding notice from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited to the Company Secretary of all listed companies, pointing to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/DIL1/P/CIR/2021/0660 dated November 23, 2021, titled “Non-compliance with certain provisions of SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018.” The letter itself does not set out new substantive rules, penalties, or deadlines; instead, it informs listed companies that SEBI has issued the referenced circular and encloses it for their reference and “necessary action,” indicating that companies should review the SEBI circular and determine whether their disclosures, issue procedures, or other actions under the ICDR Regulations need to be brought into compliance.

From the content provided, the affected entities are all listed companies, and the relevant subject matter is compliance with specific provisions of the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018. Because the document is only an enclosing/intimation letter and does not reproduce the SEBI circular’s operative requirements, no specific threshold, penalty amount, timeline, or procedural change is stated here beyond the date of the underlying SEBI circular: November 23, 2021. A compliance team should therefore treat this as a notice to obtain and analyze the enclosed SEBI circular and assess whether any obligations under the ICDR Regulations, particularly relating to non-compliance handling, apply to the company.

rows.title: Payment of fees in connection with filings made with SEBI
rows.summary:
This NSE circular advises all listed companies that SEBI’s fee-payment process for certain filings has changed, and companies should ensure payments are made only through the specified SEBI-approved mechanisms. For filings under the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, and the SEBI (Buyback of Securities) Regulations, 2018, fees are currently paid through the Payment Gateway available on the SEBI Intermediary Portal. If a particular application is not supported on that portal, listed companies must follow the payment method set out in SEBI’s attached communication rather than using any alternate method.

The key compliance point is that, effective from October 13, 2021, filings where fees have been paid using modes other than the specified ones may be delayed in processing. The circular does not introduce a new fee amount or rate, but it does create an operational requirement for listed companies to review their filing/payment process and ensure that any SEBI-related filing is accompanied by payment through the correct channel. Compliance teams should verify internal procedures for SEBI filings, confirm which applications are portal-supported, and avoid non-prescribed payment modes so that regulatory filings are not held up.

rows.title: Master Circular on Scheme of Arrangement
rows.summary:
This NSE circular does not itself create new substantive requirements; it is a forwarding notice from the National Stock Exchange of India to all listed companies alerting them to SEBI’s circular no. SEBI/HO/CFD/DIL2/CIR/P/2021/0000000665 dated November 23, 2021, titled “Master Circular on Scheme of Arrangement.” The NSE states that a copy of the SEBI circular is enclosed “for your reference and for necessary action at your end,” which means listed issuers should review the SEBI master circular and apply any scheme-of-arrangement requirements to any current or future merger, demerger, restructuring, or similar arrangement they are proposing or processing through the listed-entity approval and disclosure framework. The circular is addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed companies and was issued by NSE on November 24, 2021 under download ref. no. NSE/CML/2021/48.

Because the text provided is only the NSE covering communication, it does not specify the operative procedural changes, thresholds, timelines, filing requirements, or conditions contained in the underlying SEBI master circular itself. From a compliance perspective, the key action item in this document is to obtain and review the enclosed SEBI circular immediately and ensure that any scheme of arrangement being contemplated or already underway is checked against the updated SEBI framework, with necessary action taken at the company level to comply with whatever requirements the SEBI circular prescribes.

rows.title: Disclosure obligations of listed entities in relation to Related Party Transaction
rows.summary:
This NSE circular (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2021/47, dated November 23, 2021) is a forwarding notice to the Company Secretary of **all entities that have listed their specified securities**. It informs them that SEBI has issued a new notification/circular titled **“Disclosure obligations of listed entities in relation to Related Party Transactions”** under SEBI Notification No. **SEBI/HO/CFD/CMD1/CIR/P/2021/662 dated November 22, 2021**.

The document itself does **not** set out the substantive disclosure requirements; instead, it directs listed entities to the enclosed SEBI circular for the actual obligations and states that the SEBI circular is available for reference and necessary action. From a compliance perspective, the immediate requirement is to **review the SEBI notification/circular and implement whatever related-party-transaction disclosure changes it contains** for listed entities with specified securities. No explicit effective date, deadline, threshold, or procedural detail is stated in the NSE covering circular itself beyond the issuance date and reference to the underlying SEBI action.

rows.title: Addendum to SEBI Circular dated November 16, 2021 relating to Schemes of Arrangement by Listed Entities
rows.summary: This communication is an addendum/covering notice from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited to the Company Secretary of all listed companies, drawing attention to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/DIL2/CIR/P/2021/0000000659 dated November 18, 2021, titled “Schemes of Arrangement by Listed Entities.” The notice itself does not introduce new substantive requirements, thresholds, timelines, or procedures; instead, it serves to forward the SEBI circular and state that it is enclosed “for your reference and for necessary action” by recipients. The affected parties are all listed companies, particularly their company secretarial/compliance functions, to the extent they are considering or implementing schemes of arrangement. Because the actual compliance obligations are contained in the referenced SEBI circular and not in this addendum, a compliance officer should treat this document as a notification requiring review of the enclosed SEBI circular and any related action needed for ongoing or proposed scheme-of-arrangement filings.

rows.title: Schemes of Arrangement by Listed Entities
rows.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India issued this circular on November 17, 2021 to all listed companies, forwarding SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/DIL2/CIR/P/2021/0000000657 dated November 16, 2021, titled “Schemes of Arrangement by Listed Entities.” The NSE notice itself does not set out the detailed substantive requirements; it serves as a communication that SEBI’s circular on schemes of arrangement for listed entities is enclosed and should be reviewed for necessary action. For compliance purposes, the affected entities are all listed companies, and the subject matter is any scheme of arrangement involving a listed entity. No separate effective date, deadline, threshold, or procedural requirement is stated in the NSE cover circular beyond the instruction that the SEBI circular is for the recipient’s information and necessary action.

rows.title: Common and Simplified Norms for processing investor’s service request by RTAs and norms for furnishing PAN, KYC details and Nomination
rows.summary:
This NSE communication is a forwarding circular, not a standalone substantive rule, but it matters because it notifies all listed companies that SEBI has issued new requirements on **common and simplified norms for processing investor service requests by RTAs** and on **furnishing PAN, KYC details, and nomination**. The NSE circular is **Ref. No. NSE/CML/2021/44 dated November 03, 2021**, and it is addressed to the **Company Secretary of all listed companies through recognized stock exchanges**. NSE states that it is enclosing **SEBI Notification No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD_RTAMB/P/CIR/2021/655 dated November 03, 2021** for reference and “necessary action,” meaning listed issuers should review and implement the SEBI circular’s requirements as applicable to their investor servicing and registrar/transfer agent processes.

The document itself does **not restate the operative SEBI requirements, thresholds, procedures, or deadlines**; it only points recipients to the SEBI notification for the actual compliance obligations. From a compliance standpoint, the key action item is to **obtain and operationalize the underlying SEBI circular** because this NSE letter signals that the new framework affects the handling of investor requests by RTAs and likely touches issuer-side processes around **PAN/KYC/Nomination collection and validation**. No specific effective date other than the **November 03, 2021** issuance date is provided in this NSE letter, and no numerical thresholds, forms, or timelines are set out here.

rows.title: Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)on application filed under Regulation 37 of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 w.r.t. Scheme of Arrangements
rows.summary:
This SOP applies to all listed companies/listed entities that file a draft Scheme of Arrangement with the stock exchange(s) seeking the exchange’s no-objection/observation under Regulation 37 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, read with the SEBI circulars dated March 10, 2017 and subsequent amendments. The key filing deadline is that the scheme application, together with all documents required by the exchange checklist, must be submitted within 15 working days of the board meeting that approves the draft scheme; if the company misses that 15-working-day window, it must obtain fresh board approval based on fresh financial statements, a fresh valuation report, and similar updated materials before reapplying.

For schemes involving unlisted company(ies), the listed entity must submit audited financial statements for the last 3 years, and those financials must not be older than 6 months at the time of submission. The circular states that these audited financials are to be used by the valuer for the valuation report under the Income Approach. In addition, when the stock exchange issues its observation letter, it will require an undertaking from the listed entity confirming that the unlisted company’s financials will still be no more than 6 months old at the time the scheme is submitted to the National Company Law Tribunal (the text cuts off after “submi…”, but the obligation clearly described is the freshness requirement for NCLT submission).

For compliance purposes, the operational change is that companies must tightly coordinate board approval, financial reporting cut-off dates, valuation work, and exchange filing timing so the application is not delayed beyond 15 working days and the unlisted-company financials remain within the 6-month age limit. Missing these timing conditions triggers a re-approval and re-documentation process rather than simply curing the filing, so companies should treat the dates of the board meeting, financial statements, valuation report, and intended filing/submission as a single controlled compliance timeline.

rows.title: Transmission of Securities to joint Holder(s)
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated **October 19, 2021** is a forwarding notice to **all listed companies** (through the stock exchanges) regarding a new **SEBI notification dated October 18, 2021** titled **“Transmission of Securities to joint Holder(s).”** The circular itself does **not restate the full operative requirements** of the SEBI notification; it advises listed companies that the SEBI circular is enclosed, available on the NSE website, and should be reviewed for **necessary action**.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that this communication is a **directive to take note of and implement the SEBI transmission framework for securities held in joint names**, if applicable to the company’s registrars, transfer agents, and investor servicing processes. The document does **not provide any specific effective date, deadlines, thresholds, or procedural details** beyond the fact that the SEBI notification was issued on **October 18, 2021** and the NSE circular followed on **October 19, 2021**. Because the actual rules are contained in the referenced SEBI notification rather than reproduced here, a compliance team would need to review that underlying circular to determine the precise obligations, impacted transactions, and any changes to transmission processing for joint holders.

rows.title: XBRL based filing of Related Party Transactions for Listed Companies at NSE
rows.summary:
NSE Circular NSE/CML/2021/42 dated October 19, 2021 clarifies the earlier requirement under Circular NSE/CML/2021/34 dated September 6, 2021 that all listed companies file Related Party Transactions disclosures under Regulation 23(9) in XBRL format only. The new circular creates an exception for **listed banking companies**: the XBRL submission requirement **does not apply for the half year ended September 30, 2021** for these entities.

For that reporting period, listed banking companies must **continue filing Related Party Transactions in PDF format** instead of XBRL. The circular does not change the underlying obligation to file Related Party Transactions; it only postpones the XBRL-only filing requirement for banking companies for the September 30, 2021 half-year filing cycle. All other listed companies remain subject to the original XBRL-based filing requirement under Regulation 23(9) as stated in the September 6, 2021 circular.

rows.title: Contact details of NSE’s Listing department officials
rows.summary: NSE has informed all listed companies that the contact details of its Listing department officials, together with the profiles/domains they handle, are now available on the NEAPS portal under **Help > Contact Us**. rows.title: Amendments to manner and mechanism of providing exit option to dissenting unit holders pursuant to Regulation 22(6A) and Regulation 22(8) of SEBI (Real Estate Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014 (“SEBI (REIT) Regulations”)
rows.summary:

rows.title: Guidance note on Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulation 23(9) regarding disclosure of related party transactions
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India issued this guidance note on September 29, 2021, to clarify how listed entities must make the related party transactions disclosure required under Regulation 23(9) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. It references an earlier NSE guidance circular dated April 1, 2021, and a subsequent circular dated September 6, 2021 on XBRL-based filing of related party transactions for listed companies at NSE, and specifically clarifies the answer to question 3 of the prior guidance note.

The substantive requirement clarified is the basis on which related party transactions must be filed. If a listed entity submits only standalone financial results under Regulation 33 of the SEBI LODR Regulations, it must submit its related party transactions disclosure on a standalone basis under Regulation 23(9). If, however, a listed entity submits both standalone and consolidated financial results under Regulation 33, then it must submit related party transactions disclosure only on a consolidated basis under Regulation 23(9). In other words, the filing format follows the scope of the financial results being submitted: standalone-only filers disclose standalone related party transactions, while filers of both standalone and consolidated results disclose only consolidated related party transactions.

This clarification applies to all listed entities covered by Regulation 33 and Regulation 23(9), and it affects the compliance process for periodic disclosure of related party transactions to the exchange, including the XBRL-based filing process referenced in the earlier circulars. The circular does not introduce a new deadline, rate, threshold, or numerical requirement; it is a procedural clarification on the required reporting basis for the disclosure.

rows.title: Bank accounts for payment of fees to SEBI under the SEBI (Infrastructure Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014, SEBI (Real Estate Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014, SEBI (Informal Guidance) Scheme, 2003, SEBI (Issue and Listing of Non-convertible Securities) Regulations, 2021 and SEBI (Issue and Listing of Securitized Debt Instruments and Security Receipts) Regulations, 2008
rows.summary:
This NSE circular (dated **September 28, 2021**) communicates SEBI’s updated procedure for paying various fees under the **SEBI (Infrastructure Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014**, **SEBI (Real Estate Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014**, **SEBI (Informal Guidance) Scheme, 2003**, **SEBI (Issue and Listing of Non-convertible Securities) Regulations, 2021**, and **SEBI (Issue and Listing of Securitized Debt Instruments and Security Receipts) Regulations, 2008**. It applies to **all InvITs, all REITs, and all issuers making public issues of non-convertible securities, securitised debt instruments, and security receipts**.

The key change is that **fees must be remitted only to the specified ICICI Bank virtual accounts**; SEBI has designated **ICICI Bank Ltd.** as the bank, with **IFSC code ICIC0000106** and beneficiary name **Securities and Exchange Board of India**. The circular lists the required **virtual account codes** for each fee type: **Filing Fee – InvITs (SEBIRCINVITFILFEE)**, **Filing Fee – REITs (SEBIRCREITFILFEE)**, **Regulatory Fee – Public Issue of Debt Securities (SEBIRCDEBTPUBLICPLC)**, **Regulatory Fee – Public Issue of Non-convertible Redeemable Preference Shares (SEBIRCNCRPSPUBLICPLC)**, **Filing Fee – Public Issue of Securitised Debt Instruments (SEBIRCSDIPUBLICPLC)**, **Registration Fees – Trustee/Special Purpose Distinct Entity, including application/registration/annual fees (SEBIRCSPDE)**, **Exemption Fees under LODR/NCS (SEBIRCEXEMPTFEE)**, and **Informal Guidance (SEBIRCIG)**. This means the payment method is now tightly controlled and fee payments must map to the correct virtual account depending on the transaction or regulatory filing.

For **REIT and InvIT registration matters**, SEBI requires that the **application fee and registration fee be paid only through the SEBI Intermediary Portal**; they are not to be paid through the general virtual account mechanism described for other fees. The circular explicitly warns filers **not to transfer or pay fees by any other means or mode**, because doing so will create reconciliation problems and **delay processing**. As an additional compliance step, remitters must send the **particulars of remittance by email to od-ddhs@sebi**. There are no other effective dates, thresholds, or fee amounts specified in the circular—its operative requirement is the exclusive use of the designated payment channels and the email notification of payment details.

rows.title: XBRL based filing of Related Party Transactions for Listed Companies at NSE
rows.summary:
NSE has introduced **mandatory XBRL-only filing** for **Related Party Transactions disclosures under Regulation 23(9) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015** for **all listed companies**. This replaces prior filing methods for this disclosure on the NSE platform: companies must now submit the related party transactions report **only in XBRL mode** through NSE’s NEAPS system.

The filing requirement remains tied to **Regulation 23(9)**, which requires listed entities to submit **within 30 days from the date of publication of their standalone and consolidated financial results for the half year** the disclosures of related party transactions on a consolidated basis. NSE states that the XBRL filing facility is being introduced **with immediate effect** to improve accuracy and efficiency, so compliance teams should treat XBRL submission as already operative from **September 6, 2021** (the circular date).

For submission, companies must use the **Excel utility attached as Annexure 1** to generate the XBRL/XML file, or use the utility provided by another stock exchange to generate the XML file, and then upload it on the **NEAPS portal** via **Compliance > Common XBRL upload > Related Party Transactions** by selecting the relevant **financial year** and **period type**. After a successful upload, the system displays **“File Uploaded successfully”** and an **acknowledgement email** is sent to the registered email address.

The circular does not change the underlying disclosure content required by Regulation 23(9), but it does impose a **new procedural/compliance obligation**: listed companies must ensure their related party transactions disclosure is prepared in the prescribed XBRL format and filed electronically through the NSE’s XBRL workflow, rather than in a non-XBRL format. For any issues or clarifications, NSE directs filers to contact **nsexbrl@nse**.

rows.title: Automation of Continual Disclosures under Regulation 7(2) of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 - System driven disclosures - Ease of doing business

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the disclosure process under **Regulation 7(2)** is being moved toward an **automated, system-generated regime**, so listed entities should expect that continual disclosure reporting connected with insider trading obligations will be driven by system data rather than solely manual filing. The circular does not specify a separate deadline, threshold, or numerical trigger in the NSE note itself, but the operative date referenced for the SEBI action is **August 13, 2021**, with the NSE circular issued on **August 16, 2021**. Companies should review the enclosed SEBI circular immediately to understand any implementation steps, internal process changes, or reporting adjustments required for their compliance and disclosures under the insider trading framework.

rows.title: Continuous disclosures in compliances by InvITs -Amendments

rows.title: Continuous disclosures in compliances by REITs - Amendments

rows.title: Guidance note for companies undergoing Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process
rows.summary:
This NSE guidance note, issued on 9 July 2021 and addressed to all listed companies, does not create a new standalone rule; it points companies to a January 3, 2018 circular of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) and reminds them that companies undergoing a Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) must continue to comply with listing regulations and all other applicable laws as amended from time to time. The note is explicitly described as guidance for assistance only, so the underlying obligations remain those in the applicable regulations and the IBBI circular.

The cited IBBI circular places responsibility on the Interim Resolution Professional, Resolution Professional, or Liquidator (as applicable) to exercise reasonable care and diligence and take all necessary steps to ensure that the corporate debtor complies with applicable laws during CIRP or liquidation. It also clarifies that if the company incurs any loss, including any penalty, because of non-compliance with applicable laws during the process, that loss is not to be treated as insolvency resolution process cost or liquidation process cost under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code. However, if non-compliance occurs because of the insolvency professional’s conduct, the insolvency professional can be held responsible for that non-compliance.

For listed entities, the practical compliance message is that CIRP does not suspend legal and disclosure obligations under SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) and related regulations; the company and the appointed insolvency professional must still ensure timely compliance with all applicable filing, disclosure, and governance requirements throughout the process. No new thresholds, monetary limits, or specific deadlines are introduced in this note beyond the issuance date, but companies are instructed to review and comply with the current version of all applicable listing and regulatory requirements during CIRP.

rows.title: Standard Operating Procedure for listed subsidiary company desirous of getting delisted through a Scheme of Arrangement wherein the listed parent holding company and the listed subsidiary are in the same line of business

rows.title: Guidance Note on Analyst/Institutional Investors meet
rows.summary:
This guidance note, issued by NSE on June 29, 2021, explains the effect of SEBI’s May 5, 2021 amendments to the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, specifically the enhanced disclosure requirement under point 15 of para A of Part A of Schedule III. For listed companies, disclosure of **group meetings** with analysts/institutional investors is now **mandatory**, including both the **schedule** of such meetings and the **post-meeting disclosures**; however, disclosure of **one-on-one meetings** is **not mandatory** under this clarification. The note also requires that **all audio/video recordings and transcripts of post-earnings or quarterly investor calls**, whether held physically or digitally and whether organized by the listed entity or any other entity, must be **disclosed to the recognized stock exchange**.

In addition, the Exchange says it has been advised to issue further guidance under the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 to strengthen disclosures where **Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (UPSI)** is shared during analyst/research/investor meetings. This second requirement is explicitly limited to situations where UPSI is in fact shared during the meet, and it applies even if the meeting was **not organized by the listed company**, because the possibility of sharing price-sensitive information in such meetings cannot be ruled out. The practical compliance implication is that listed entities must treat analyst/institutional investor interactions as potentially disclosure-relevant when UPSI may be discussed, and ensure the required disclosures and filings are made in line with these clarified expectations.

rows.title: FAQ’s - LODR amendments dated May 05, 2021
rows.summary:
SEBI’s May 5, 2021 amendments to the LODR Regulations, 2015, as explained in this NSE FAQ circular dated June 28, 2021, clarify how listed entities should determine applicability and the compliance timeline for certain risk-management-related changes. For Regulation 3(2), the market-capitalization cutoff date to determine whether a listed entity is subject to the relevant provisions is **March 31, 2021**. Listed companies are also reminded that they must comply with the amended LODR requirements and any other applicable regulations as updated from time to time; the FAQ is only interpretive assistance and does not replace the regulations.

The substantive amendment addressed in the FAQ is to **Regulation 21(2)**, which now requires the **Risk Management Committee (RMC)** to have **at least three members**, with a **majority from the board of directors**, including **at least one independent director**; and for entities with **outstanding SR equity shares**, **at least two-thirds of the RMC must be independent directors**. Regulation **21(3A)** changes the frequency requirement from **“once” to “twice”**, and Regulation **21(5)** changes the threshold from **500 to 1000** (as amended in the regulation text). The amendment to **Schedule III, Part D** requires formulation of a **detailed risk management policy**.

On timing, the FAQ says compliance periods are available for the amended provisions, but the visible text in the provided document cuts off before the full timing table is shown. It does clearly indicate that the time available differs by provision, and specifically references **Regulation 21(2), 21(5), and Schedule III, Part D** as items for which a compliance period is being provided. The circular is addressed to **all listed companies** and issued by the **National Stock Exchange of India Limited** as a response to common implementation questions about the SEBI amendment.

rows.title: Action(s) to be initiated against listed companies for non-payment of outstanding Annual Listing Fees (“ALF”)
rows.summary:
This circular informs all listed entities that have not paid their outstanding Annual Listing Fees (ALF) that the NSE will initiate enforcement action in line with SEBI’s SOP on non-payment of ALF. The process is staged: first, the Exchange will issue reminder letters during the six-month period after the ALF invoice is issued; second, once those six months expire, the Exchange will send a formal notice requiring payment within 15 days, and if the entity still does not pay within that 15-day period, the Exchange will withhold approval for any further listing of securities by that defaulting listed entity.

If the listed entity still fails to clear the ALF after that notice period, the Exchange will escalate the matter to the promoter(s) of the defaulting entity. A notice will be sent to the promoter(s) using the information available with the Exchange, requiring them to ensure compliance and arrange payment of the outstanding ALF within 30 days from the date of that promoter notice. The circular also states that the concerned promoter(s) may submit a representation to the Exchange by email at listingsop@nse.in (the text provided cuts off immediately after this, so any additional filing details or subsequent steps are not visible in the excerpt).

For compliance purposes, the key obligation is to ensure ALF is paid promptly after invoice issuance, because the enforcement timeline begins with the invoice date and quickly escalates from reminders to formal notice, then to restriction on further listing approvals, and finally to promoter-level action. The document applies specifically to listed entities with unpaid ALF and, at the final stage, to their promoter(s); no other fee amounts or numeric thresholds are specified beyond the six-month reminder window, the 15-day cure period, and the 30-day promoter payment period.
